column2: Zhōngguó gǔdài yǒu yí wèi zhéxuéjiā, zài tā de shū zhōng jiǎng le zhèyàng yí ge yùyán gùshi:
column3: An ancient Chinese philosopher told this fable in his book:

column1: 从前有位老人，喂养了一群猴子当宠物。相处久了，彼此居然可以从表情、声音和行为举止中了解对方的意思。
column2: Cóngqián yǒu wèi lǎorén, wèiyǎng le yì qún hóuzi dàng chǒngwù. Xiāngchǔ jiǔ le, bǐcǐ jūrán kěyǐ cóng biǎoqíng, shēngyīn hé xíngwéi jǔzhǐ zhōng liǎojiě duìfāng de yìsi.
column3: Once upon a time there was an old man who kept a troop of monkeys as pets. After living together for a long time, they could actually understand each other from facial expressions, sounds and behavior.

column1: 猴子太多，每天要吃大量的瓜果、蔬菜和粮食。然而，一个普通的家庭，财产不多，哪有那么大的财力满足一群猴子对食物的长期需要呢？老人甚至必须减少家人的消费，好节省些食物拿去喂养猴子。他注意到该限制猴子的食量了。
column2: Hóuzi tài duō, měi tiān yào chī dàliàng de guāguǒ, shūcài hé liángshi. Rán'ér, yí ge pǔtōng de jiātíng, cáichǎn bù duō, nǎ yǒu nàme dà de cáilì mǎnzú yì qún hóuzi duì shíwù de chángqī xūyào ne? Lǎorén shènzhì bìxū jiǎnshǎo jiārén de xiāofèi, hǎo jiéshěng xiē shíwù ná qu wèiyǎng hóuzi. Tā zhùyì dào gāi xiànzhì hóuzi de shíliàng le.
column3: There were so many monkeys that they ate huge amounts of fruit, vegetables and grain every day. But an ordinary family without much property—how could it afford to meet a troop of monkeys' long-term need for food? The old man even had to cut back on his family's spending to save some food to feed the monkeys. He realized it was time to limit how much the monkeys ate.

column1: 问题是，猴子不像猫、狗，吃不饱时仅仅只是叫叫，它们如果得不到好的待遇，就会像一群调皮的孩子，经常跟人淘气。
column2: Wèntí shì, hóuzi bú xiàng māo, gǒu, chī bu bǎo shí jǐnjǐn zhǐshì jiàojiao, tāmen rúguǒ dé bu dào hǎo de dàiyù, jiù huì xiàng yì qún tiáopí de háizi, jīngcháng gēn rén táoqì.
column3: The problem was that monkeys aren't like cats and dogs, which merely cry a bit when they're not full. If monkeys don't get good treatment, they act like a bunch of naughty children and keep making mischief.

column1: 老人的朋友送给他很多橡子，这是一种猴子爱吃的果实。在其他粮食不足的情况下，用橡子喂猴子倒是个办法。于是老人对猴子们说：“今后你们除了吃馒头，还可以再吃一些橡子。我早上给你们三颗，晚上给四颗。”
column2: Lǎorén de péngyou sònggěi tā hěn duō xiàngzǐ, zhè shì yì zhǒng hóuzi ài chī de guǒshí. Zài qítā liángshi bùzú de qíngkuàng xià, yòng xiàngzǐ wèi hóuzi dàoshì ge bànfǎ. Yúshì lǎorén duì hóuzimen shuō: "Jīnhòu nǐmen chúle chī mántou, hái kěyǐ zài chī yìxiē xiàngzǐ. Wǒ zǎoshang gěi nǐmen sān kē, wǎnshang gěi sì kē."
column3: A friend of the old man gave him lots of acorns, a fruit that monkeys love. With other food running short, feeding the monkeys acorns was actually a good idea. So the old man said to the monkeys, "From now on, besides steamed buns, you can also have some acorns. I'll give you three in the morning and four in the evening."

column1: 猴子们似乎只弄懂了主人前面说的一个“三”，觉得自己吃了亏，一个个立起身子跳来跳去，对着老人大喊大叫地发脾气。
column2: Hóuzimen sìhū zhǐ nòngdǒng le zhǔrén qiánmiàn shuō de yí ge "sān", juéde zìjǐ chī le kuī, yí gègè lìqǐ shēnzi tiào lái tiào qù, duìzhe lǎorén dà hǎn dà jiào de fā píqi.
column3: The monkeys seemed to understand only the "three" their master had said first, and felt cheated. One after another they stood up, jumped about, and threw a tantrum, shrieking and yelling at the old man.

column1: 老人见猴子们不接受，就换了一种方式，安慰它们说道：“要不这样吧，既然你们觉得少，那就改成每天早上四颗，晚上三颗，这样总够了吧？”
column2: Lǎorén jiàn hóuzimen bù jiēshòu, jiù huàn le yì zhǒng fāngshì, ānwèi tāmen shuōdào: "Yàobù zhèyàng ba, jìrán nǐmen juéde shǎo, nà jiù gǎichéng měi tiān zǎoshang sì kē, wǎnshang sān kē, zhèyàng zǒng gòu le ba?"
column3: Seeing that the monkeys wouldn't accept it, the old man tried another approach and soothed them: "How about this: since you think it's too few, I'll change it to four every morning and three every evening. Surely that's enough?"

column1: 猴子把主人前面说的一个“四”当成全天多得了的橡子，所以马上安静下来，显得格外开心。老人看着这情景，哈哈地笑了。
column2: Hóuzi bǎ zhǔrén qiánmiàn shuō de yí ge "sì" dàngchéng quán tiān duō dé le de xiàngzǐ, suǒyǐ mǎshàng ānjìng xialai, xiǎnde géwài kāixīn. Lǎorén kànzhe zhè qíngjǐng, hāhā de xiào le.
column3: The monkeys took the "four" their master said first to mean they were getting more acorns for the day, so they quieted down at once and looked especially happy. Watching this scene, the old man laughed heartily.

column1: 哲学家用这个故事告诉人们，不要太关心生死、得失，因为到最后我们会发现没有失去什么，也没有得到什么。不过，发展到今天，“朝三暮四”这个成语的意义已经完全改变了。你知道它现在是什么意思吗？
column2: Zhéxuéjiā yòng zhège gùshi gàosu rénmen, bú yào tài guānxīn shēngsǐ, déshī, yīnwèi dào zuìhòu wǒmen huì fāxiàn méiyǒu shīqù shénme, yě méiyǒu dédào shénme. Búguò, fāzhǎn dào jīntiān, "zhāo sān mù sì" zhège chéngyǔ de yìyì yǐjīng wánquán gǎibiàn le. Nǐ zhīdào tā xiànzài shì shénme yìsi ma?
column3: With this story the philosopher tells people not to care too much about life and death, gain and loss, because in the end we will find we haven't lost anything, nor gained anything. However, by today the meaning of the idiom "three in the morning, four in the evening" has changed completely. Do you know what it means now?

column1: 美食很大一部分是靠名人推动的，这一点在民国时期表现得尤其突出。例如著名的文学家鲁迅，在吃喝这件事上，就算是个地道的行家，不但会吃，还会亲自动手做，对许多美食都有独特的见解。这是近代新时尚。
column2: Měishí hěn dà yí bùfen shì kào míngrén tuīdòng de, zhè yì diǎn zài Mínguó shíqī biǎoxiàn de yóuqí tūchū. Lìrú zhùmíng de wénxuéjiā Lǔ Xùn, zài chīhē zhè jiàn shì shang, jiù suànshì ge dìdao de hángjia, búdàn huì chī, hái huì qīnzì dòngshǒu zuò, duì xǔduō měishí dōu yǒu dútè de jiànjiě. Zhè shì jìndài xīn shíshàng.
column3: Fine food owes a great deal to the promotion of famous people, and this was especially striking in the Republican era. The famous writer Lu Xun, for example, was a true connoisseur when it came to eating and drinking: he not only knew how to eat well but also cooked himself, and had his own views on many dishes. This was a new fashion of modern times.

column1: 北京是鲁迅长期生活过的城市，仅从这一时期鲁迅写作的日记中，我们发现他去过的知名餐馆就有65家，另外，他还很爱吃稻香村的点心。作为大作家、大学问家，鲁迅对吃很讲究，吃的内容在他的日记里占了很大一部分。在众多餐馆里，鲁迅去得最多、最喜欢的是广和居，平均每周都要去一次。
column2: Běijīng shì Lǔ Xùn chángqī shēnghuó guo de chéngshì, jǐn cóng zhè yì shíqī Lǔ Xùn xiězuò de rìjì zhōng, wǒmen fāxiàn tā qù guo de zhīmíng cānguǎn jiù yǒu liùshíwǔ jiā, lìngwài, tā hái hěn ài chī Dàoxiāngcūn de diǎnxin. Zuòwéi dà zuòjiā, dà xuéwènjiā, Lǔ Xùn duì chī hěn jiǎngjiu, chī de nèiróng zài tā de rìjì li zhàn le hěn dà yí bùfen. Zài zhòngduō cānguǎn li, Lǔ Xùn qù de zuì duō, zuì xǐhuan de shì Guǎnghéjū, píngjūn měi zhōu dōu yào qù yí cì.
column3: Beijing was a city where Lu Xun lived for a long time. From the diaries he wrote in this period alone, we find he visited 65 well-known restaurants; he was also very fond of the pastries from Daoxiangcun. As a great writer and scholar, Lu Xun was very particular about food, and eating takes up a large part of his diaries. Among the many restaurants, the one he went to most and liked best was Guangheju, which he visited on average once a week.

column1: 鲁迅经常到这家店的一个重要原因是距离近，广和居的大门就在他当时住的胡同的斜对面。位于菜市口附近的广和居是北京“八大居”之首，在民国时期非常出名。广和居算不上豪华，但却很适合朋友在这里聚会、热闹。这里特别欢迎文人的光临，为他们的聚会创造了很好的条件。广和居院里分成大小不同的各种房间，有一个人的，有三五人小聚的，也有十多个人大聚会的。这大大满足了鲁迅爱和朋友吃饭的要求。他爱好交际，大方好客，常呼朋唤友，多数是三五个人一起吃，有时甚至会直接让广和居送外卖到家里，在家招待朋友。
column2: Lǔ Xùn jīngcháng dào zhè jiā diàn de yí ge zhòngyào yuányīn shì jùlí jìn, Guǎnghéjū de dàmén jiù zài tā dāngshí zhù de hútòng de xié duìmiàn. Wèiyú Càishìkǒu fùjìn de Guǎnghéjū shì Běijīng "bā dà jū" zhī shǒu, zài Mínguó shíqī fēicháng chūmíng. Guǎnghéjū suàn bu shàng háohuá, dàn què hěn shìhé péngyou zài zhèlǐ jùhuì, rènao. Zhèlǐ tèbié huānyíng wénrén de guānglín, wèi tāmen de jùhuì chuàngzào le hěn hǎo de tiáojiàn. Guǎnghéjū yuàn li fēnchéng dàxiǎo bùtóng de gè zhǒng fángjiān, yǒu yí ge rén de, yǒu sān wǔ rén xiǎo jù de, yě yǒu shí duō ge rén dà jùhuì de. Zhè dàdà mǎnzú le Lǔ Xùn ài hé péngyou chīfàn de yāoqiú. Tā àihào jiāojì, dàfang hàokè, cháng hū péng huàn yǒu, duōshù shì sān wǔ ge rén yìqǐ chī, yǒushí shènzhì huì zhíjiē ràng Guǎnghéjū sòng wàimài dào jiāli, zài jiā zhāodài péngyou.
column3: An important reason Lu Xun often went there was that it was close: Guangheju's front gate was diagonally across from the hutong he lived in at the time. Located near Caishikou, Guangheju was the foremost of Beijing's "Eight Great Ju" restaurants and very famous in the Republican era. It wasn't luxurious, but it was perfect for friends to gather and have a lively time. It especially welcomed men of letters and made their gatherings very easy. Its courtyard was divided into rooms of different sizes: some for one person, some for small get-togethers of three to five, and some for big parties of more than ten. This suited Lu Xun's love of eating with friends perfectly. He enjoyed socializing, was generous and hospitable, and often called his friends together, usually eating in groups of three to five; sometimes he even had Guangheju deliver food straight to his home to entertain friends there.

column1: 当然最重要的还是因为广和居有鲁迅喜欢的菜。那里的菜既有高档的，也有适合普通百姓的，样样都让人有胃口。
column2: Dāngrán zuì zhòngyào de háishi yīnwèi Guǎnghéjū yǒu Lǔ Xùn xǐhuan de cài. Nàli de cài jì yǒu gāodàng de, yě yǒu shìhé pǔtōng bǎixìng de, yàngyàng dōu ràng rén yǒu wèikǒu.
column3: Of course, the most important reason was that Guangheju had dishes Lu Xun liked. Its food included both high-end dishes and ones suited to ordinary people, and every one of them whetted the appetite.

column1: 鲁迅也爱喝酒，虽然明明知道自己有胃病，不应该喝酒，但却很难戒掉。他是每顿饭必喝酒的人。现在保存的历史资料记载，他和郁达夫一起喝酒的次数最多。鲁迅酒量不大，经常喝醉，而且在喝酒的过程中烟不离手。郁达夫在1933年曾经作诗形容他：“醉眼蒙胧上酒楼，彷徨呐喊两悠悠”，描写得十分形象。
column2: Lǔ Xùn yě ài hē jiǔ, suīrán míngmíng zhīdào zìjǐ yǒu wèibìng, bù yīnggāi hē jiǔ, dàn què hěn nán jièdiào. Tā shì měi dùn fàn bì hē jiǔ de rén. Xiànzài bǎocún de lìshǐ zīliào jìzǎi, tā hé Yù Dáfū yìqǐ hē jiǔ de cìshù zuì duō. Lǔ Xùn jiǔliàng bú dà, jīngcháng hēzuì, érqiě zài hē jiǔ de guòchéng zhōng yān bù lí shǒu. Yù Dáfū zài yī jiǔ sān sān nián céngjīng zuò shī xíngróng tā: "Zuìyǎn ménglóng shàng jiǔlóu, Pánghuáng Nàhǎn liǎng yōuyōu", miáoxiě de shífēn xíngxiàng.
column3: Lu Xun also loved to drink. Although he knew perfectly well that he had a stomach problem and shouldn't drink, he found it hard to quit. He drank at every meal. According to surviving historical records, the person he drank with most often was Yu Dafu. Lu Xun couldn't hold much liquor and often got drunk, and he never had a cigarette out of his hand while drinking. In 1933 Yu Dafu wrote a poem describing him: "Bleary-eyed with drink he climbs the tavern stairs; Wandering and Call to Arms, both of lasting reach"—a very vivid portrait.

column1: 1872年的一天，在美国加利福尼亚州的一个酒店里，斯坦福与科恩围绕“马奔跑时蹄子是否着地”进行了辩论。斯坦福认为，马奔跑得那么快，在跳起时四蹄应该都是不落地的；而科恩认为，马要是四蹄都不着地，那不是成了青蛙啦？应该是始终有一蹄着地。两人各执一词，争论得脸红脖子粗，谁也说服不了谁。于是他们就请英国摄影师麦布里奇来判断，可麦布里奇也弄不清楚。不过摄影师毕竟是摄影师，主意还是有的。他们一起来到一个操场，在一条跑道的一边等距离放上24个照相机，照相机对准跑道；在跑道另一边打24个洞，分别插进24根木棍，木棍上系着细线，细线穿过跑道，接上相机快门。
column2: Yī bā qī èr nián de yì tiān, zài Měiguó Jiālìfúníyà Zhōu de yí ge jiǔdiàn li, Sītǎnfú yǔ Kē'ēn wéirào "mǎ bēnpǎo shí tízi shìfǒu zháo dì" jìnxíng le biànlùn. Sītǎnfú rènwéi, mǎ bēnpǎo de nàme kuài, zài tiàoqǐ shí sì tí yīnggāi dōu shì bú luò dì de; ér Kē'ēn rènwéi, mǎ yàoshi sì tí dōu bù zháo dì, nà bú shì chéng le qīngwā la? Yīnggāi shì shǐzhōng yǒu yì tí zháo dì. Liǎng rén gè zhí yì cí, zhēnglùn de liǎn hóng bózi cū, shéi yě shuōfú bu liǎo shéi. Yúshì tāmen jiù qǐng Yīngguó shèyǐngshī Màibùlǐqí lái pànduàn, kě Màibùlǐqí yě nòng bu qīngchu. Búguò shèyǐngshī bìjìng shì shèyǐngshī, zhǔyi háishi yǒu de. Tāmen yìqǐ láidào yí ge cāochǎng, zài yì tiáo pǎodào de yìbiān děng jùlí fàngshang èrshísì ge zhàoxiàngjī, zhàoxiàngjī duìzhǔn pǎodào; zài pǎodào lìng yìbiān dǎ èrshísì ge dòng, fēnbié chājìn èrshísì gēn mùgùn, mùgùn shang jìzhe xì xiàn, xì xiàn chuānguò pǎodào, jiēshang xiàngjī kuàimén.
column3: One day in 1872, in a hotel in California, USA, Stanford and Cohen got into a debate over "whether a horse's hooves touch the ground when it runs". Stanford argued that a horse runs so fast that when it leaps, none of its four hooves should be on the ground; Cohen argued that if a horse had all four hooves off the ground, wouldn't it be a frog? There must always be one hoof on the ground. Each stuck to his own view, and they argued until they were red in the face, neither able to convince the other. So they asked the English photographer Muybridge to settle it, but Muybridge couldn't figure it out either. Still, a photographer is a photographer, and he did have an idea. They went to a sports field and set up 24 cameras at equal intervals along one side of a track, all aimed at the track; on the other side of the track they dug 24 holes and stuck a wooden stick into each, with a thin thread tied to each stick, running across the track and connected to a camera shutter.

column1: 一切都准备好了，麦布里奇让一匹马从跑道的一头飞奔到另一头，马一边跑，一边按顺序撞断拦路的24根细线，相机连续拍下了24张相片，相邻两张相片的差距都很小。相片显示：马奔跑时始终有一蹄着地，科恩赢了。
column2: Yíqiè dōu zhǔnbèi hǎo le, Màibùlǐqí ràng yì pǐ mǎ cóng pǎodào de yì tóu fēibēn dào lìng yì tóu, mǎ yìbiān pǎo, yìbiān àn shùnxù zhuàngduàn lánlù de èrshísì gēn xì xiàn, xiàngjī liánxù pāixià le èrshísì zhāng xiàngpiàn, xiānglín liǎng zhāng xiàngpiàn de chājù dōu hěn xiǎo. Xiàngpiàn xiǎnshì: mǎ bēnpǎo shí shǐzhōng yǒu yì tí zháo dì, Kē'ēn yíng le.
column3: With everything ready, Muybridge had a horse gallop from one end of the track to the other. As it ran, the horse broke the 24 threads across its path in order, and the cameras took 24 photos in a row, with very little difference between each pair of neighboring photos. The photos showed that a running horse always has one hoof on the ground. Cohen had won.

column1: 事后，有人无意识地快速拉动那一长串相片，“奇迹”出现了：各张相片中静止的马连成了一匹运动的马，相片“活”了。这就是电影最早的样子。
column2: Shìhòu, yǒu rén wú yìshí de kuàisù lādòng nà yì cháng chuàn xiàngpiàn, "qíjì" chūxiàn le: gè zhāng xiàngpiàn zhōng jìngzhǐ de mǎ liánchéng le yì pǐ yùndòng de mǎ, xiàngpiàn "huó" le. Zhè jiù shì diànyǐng zuì zǎo de yàngzi.
column3: Afterwards, someone happened to flip quickly through that long string of photos, and a "miracle" happened: the still horses in the photos joined into one moving horse—the photos had "come alive". This was the earliest form of film.

column1: 经过艰苦的试验，电影拍摄技术逐渐改进、成熟。1895年12月28日，法国人卢米埃尔兄弟在巴黎第一次向公众播放了短片《火车到站》，这一天后来成为电影产生的纪念日，兄弟俩也成为历史上最早的电影导演。
column2: Jīngguò jiānkǔ de shìyàn, diànyǐng pāishè jìshù zhújiàn gǎijìn, chéngshú. Yī bā jiǔ wǔ nián shí'èr yuè èrshíbā rì, Fǎguó rén Lúmǐ'āi'ěr xiōngdì zài Bālí dì-yī cì xiàng gōngzhòng bōfàng le duǎnpiàn "Huǒchē Dào Zhàn", zhè yì tiān hòulái chéngwéi diànyǐng chǎnshēng de jìniànrì, xiōngdì liǎ yě chéngwéi lìshǐ shang zuì zǎo de diànyǐng dǎoyǎn.
column3: After hard experimentation, filmmaking technology gradually improved and matured. On December 28, 1895, the French Lumière brothers showed the short film "The Arrival of a Train" to the public for the first time in Paris. That day later became the anniversary of the birth of cinema, and the two brothers became the earliest film directors in history.

column1: 留心生活的每一瞬间，并为之争论，适时请求帮助、认真研究，或许重大发现就在你的眼前。
column2: Liúxīn shēnghuó de měi yí shùnjiān, bìng wèi zhī zhēnglùn, shìshí qǐngqiú bāngzhù, rènzhēn yánjiū, huòxǔ zhòngdà fāxiàn jiù zài nǐ de yǎnqián.
column3: Pay attention to every moment of life, argue over it, ask for help at the right time and study it carefully—perhaps a major discovery is right before your eyes.

column1: 医学研究证明，人类睡眠有其特定的机制，自然醒是最符合人体生物钟规律的。光线是自然醒的必要条件，是人体内的生物闹钟。
column2: Yīxué yánjiū zhèngmíng, rénlèi shuìmián yǒu qí tèdìng de jīzhì, zìrán xǐng shì zuì fúhé réntǐ shēngwùzhōng guīlǜ de. Guāngxiàn shì zìrán xǐng de bìyào tiáojiàn, shì réntǐ nèi de shēngwù nàozhōng.
column3: Medical research has shown that human sleep has its own specific mechanism, and waking up naturally fits the body's biological clock best. Light is a necessary condition for waking naturally; it is the body's built-in biological alarm clock.

column1: 早晨，人体感受到逐渐变强的太阳光线，新陈代谢随之加快，人逐渐从熟睡过渡到浅睡，直到醒来。这就是阴雨天人们往往喜欢睡懒觉的原因。
column2: Zǎochen, réntǐ gǎnshòu dào zhújiàn biàn qiáng de tàiyáng guāngxiàn, xīnchén dàixiè suí zhī jiākuài, rén zhújiàn cóng shúshuì guòdù dào qiǎn shuì, zhídào xǐnglai. Zhè jiù shì yīnyǔtiān rénmen wǎngwǎng xǐhuan shuì lǎnjiào de yuányīn.
column3: In the morning, the body senses the gradually strengthening sunlight, and the metabolism speeds up accordingly; a person gradually passes from deep sleep into light sleep until waking up. This is why people often like to sleep in on dark, rainy days.

column1: 紧张的现代生活，使很多上班的人无法享受轻松舒适的睡眠、自然地醒来，闹钟的用途就显得格外重要了。但实验研究证明，人们对自然醒与被闹钟铃声叫醒这两种方式所产生的反应是很不相同的。从睡眠状态过渡到清醒状态时，人的呼吸会从16次/分钟提高到24次/分钟，心跳每分钟加快10次。如果突然被闹钟叫醒，将在心理上使人产生心慌、情绪低落、感觉没睡醒等不适。如果是从深度睡眠中被突然叫醒，那么，人的短期记忆能力、计算技能都会受到影响，这些能力最多为正常状态的65%，与醉酒者相当。
column2: Jǐnzhāng de xiàndài shēnghuó, shǐ hěn duō shàngbān de rén wúfǎ xiǎngshòu qīngsōng shūshì de shuìmián, zìrán de xǐnglai, nàozhōng de yòngtú jiù xiǎnde géwài zhòngyào le. Dàn shíyàn yánjiū zhèngmíng, rénmen duì zìrán xǐng yǔ bèi nàozhōng língshēng jiàoxǐng zhè liǎng zhǒng fāngshì suǒ chǎnshēng de fǎnyìng shì hěn bù xiāngtóng de. Cóng shuìmián zhuàngtài guòdù dào qīngxǐng zhuàngtài shí, rén de hūxī huì cóng shíliù cì/fēnzhōng tígāo dào èrshísì cì/fēnzhōng, xīntiào měi fēnzhōng jiākuài shí cì. Rúguǒ tūrán bèi nàozhōng jiàoxǐng, jiāng zài xīnlǐ shang shǐ rén chǎnshēng xīnhuāng, qíngxù dīluò, gǎnjué méi shuìxǐng děng búshì. Rúguǒ shì cóng shēndù shuìmián zhōng bèi tūrán jiàoxǐng, nàme, rén de duǎnqī jìyì nénglì, jìsuàn jìnéng dōu huì shòudào yǐngxiǎng, zhèxiē nénglì zuì duō wéi zhèngcháng zhuàngtài de bǎi fēn zhī liùshíwǔ, yǔ zuìjiǔzhě xiāngdāng.
column3: Hectic modern life means many working people can't enjoy relaxed, comfortable sleep and wake up naturally, so alarm clocks become especially important. But experimental research shows that people react very differently to waking naturally and being woken by an alarm. When passing from sleep to wakefulness, a person's breathing rises from 16 to 24 breaths per minute, and the heart speeds up by 10 beats a minute. Being woken suddenly by an alarm can cause psychological discomfort such as palpitations, low mood and feeling as if you haven't slept enough. If you are suddenly woken from deep sleep, your short-term memory and calculation skills are affected, reaching at most 65% of their normal level—about the same as someone who is drunk.

column1: 出于自我保护，被闹钟叫醒时我们的身体会提高体内的肾上腺素水平。这种状态如果持续数天、数周、数月，将导致高血压、失眠和一些精神问题等。研究发现，突然被闹铃惊醒的人比自然醒的人血压更高、心跳更快。对此，专家解释说，人在睡眠时，身体会发生一些变化，因此人们在早上醒来时更容易发病，而闹铃则会使发病的可能性变得更大。如果你必须定个闹钟，应采用有柔和的声音或音乐。
column2: Chūyú zìwǒ bǎohù, bèi nàozhōng jiàoxǐng shí wǒmen de shēntǐ huì tígāo tǐnèi de shènshàngxiànsù shuǐpíng. Zhè zhǒng zhuàngtài rúguǒ chíxù shù tiān, shù zhōu, shù yuè, jiāng dǎozhì gāoxuèyā, shīmián hé yìxiē jīngshén wèntí děng. Yánjiū fāxiàn, tūrán bèi nàolíng jīngxǐng de rén bǐ zìrán xǐng de rén xuèyā gèng gāo, xīntiào gèng kuài. Duì cǐ, zhuānjiā jiěshì shuō, rén zài shuìmián shí, shēntǐ huì fāshēng yìxiē biànhuà, yīncǐ rénmen zài zǎoshang xǐnglai shí gèng róngyì fābìng, ér nàolíng zé huì shǐ fābìng de kěnéngxìng biàn de gèng dà. Rúguǒ nǐ bìxū dìng ge nàozhōng, yīng cǎiyòng yǒu róuhé de shēngyīn huò yīnyuè.
column3: Out of self-protection, when we're woken by an alarm our body raises its adrenaline level. If this state lasts for days, weeks or months, it can lead to high blood pressure, insomnia and some mental problems. Research has found that people startled awake by an alarm have higher blood pressure and faster heartbeats than those who wake naturally. Experts explain that the body undergoes certain changes during sleep, so people are more likely to fall ill when they wake in the morning, and an alarm makes this even more likely. If you must set an alarm, choose one with a gentle sound or music.

column1: 各种醒来方式中，当然是自然醒最符合我们的愿望。可谁能替你拉开窗帘让阳光照进来呢？近年来，市场上出现了一种新的电子产品，名为“光闹钟”。它能在室内模仿早晨自然光线的变化，通过光线的作用使人在设定的时间里自然地醒来，可避免传统闹钟突然惊醒对人体健康的伤害。希望这样能向真正的“自然醒”走近一点，再走近一点。
column2: Gè zhǒng xǐnglai fāngshì zhōng, dāngrán shì zìrán xǐng zuì fúhé wǒmen de yuànwàng. Kě shéi néng tì nǐ lākāi chuānglián ràng yángguāng zhào jinlai ne? Jìnnián lái, shìchǎng shang chūxiàn le yì zhǒng xīn de diànzǐ chǎnpǐn, míng wéi "guāng nàozhōng". Tā néng zài shìnèi mófǎng zǎochen zìrán guāngxiàn de biànhuà, tōngguò guāngxiàn de zuòyòng shǐ rén zài shèdìng de shíjiān li zìrán de xǐnglai, kě bìmiǎn chuántǒng nàozhōng tūrán jīngxǐng duì réntǐ jiànkāng de shānghài. Xīwàng zhèyàng néng xiàng zhēnzhèng de "zìrán xǐng" zǒujìn yìdiǎn, zài zǒujìn yìdiǎn.
column3: Of all the ways to wake up, waking naturally is of course what we'd most like. But who can open the curtains for you and let the sunshine in? In recent years a new electronic product has appeared on the market called the "light alarm clock". It can imitate the changes in natural morning light indoors and, through the effect of light, let you wake naturally at a set time, avoiding the harm to your health of being startled awake by a traditional alarm. Hopefully this will bring us a little closer, and then a little closer still, to truly "waking up naturally".

column1: 国际足球明星梅西用微信直播自己的颠球技术，把手机另一头一个正在哭的小宝贝逗笑。这条30秒的全新广告宣传片在全球15个国家和地区同步上线。
column2: Guójì zúqiú míngxīng Méixī yòng Wēixìn zhíbō zìjǐ de diānqiú jìshù, bǎ shǒujī lìng yì tóu yí ge zhèngzài kū de xiǎo bǎobèi dòuxiào. Zhè tiáo sānshí miǎo de quánxīn guǎnggào xuānchuánpiàn zài quánqiú shíwǔ ge guójiā hé dìqū tóngbù shàngxiàn.
column3: International football star Messi live-streams his ball-juggling skills on WeChat, making a crying baby on the other end of the phone laugh. This brand-new 30-second promotional ad was launched simultaneously in 15 countries and regions around the world.

column1: 如此大手笔的推广，腾讯自有其底气所在。微信“在海外注册用户已经超过7000万，且在快速增长当中”。7月3日，在北京召开的2013腾讯合作伙伴大会上，腾讯总裁刘炽平言语间充满了骄傲。
column2: Rúcǐ dà shǒubǐ de tuīguǎng, Téngxùn zì yǒu qí dǐqì suǒzài. Wēixìn "zài hǎiwài zhùcè yònghù yǐjīng chāoguò qīqiān wàn, qiě zài kuàisù zēngzhǎng dāngzhōng". Qī yuè sān rì, zài Běijīng zhàokāi de èr líng yī sān Téngxùn hézuò huǒbàn dàhuì shang, Téngxùn zǒngcái Liú Chìpíng yányǔ jiān chōngmǎn le jiāo'ào.
column3: Tencent naturally has its reasons for the confidence behind such a lavish promotion. WeChat's "registered users overseas already exceed 70 million and are growing fast". On July 3, at the 2013 Tencent Partners Conference in Beijing, Tencent President Liu Chiping spoke with obvious pride.

column1: 2011年1月，微信上线；同年4月，以英文名WeChat正式进入国际市场；2011年12月，实现支持全球100个国家的短信注册；2012年底，覆盖国家和地区超过100个。如今，微信已经覆盖了200多个国家和地区、支持16种外语，是全球使用人数最多的移动通信应用。
column2: Èr líng yī yī nián yī yuè, Wēixìn shàngxiàn; tóngnián sì yuè, yǐ Yīngwén míng WeChat zhèngshì jìnrù guójì shìchǎng; èr líng yī yī nián shí'èr yuè, shíxiàn zhīchí quánqiú yìbǎi ge guójiā de duǎnxìn zhùcè; èr líng yī èr nián dǐ, fùgài guójiā hé dìqū chāoguò yìbǎi ge. Rújīn, Wēixìn yǐjīng fùgài le èrbǎi duō ge guójiā hé dìqū, zhīchí shíliù zhǒng wàiyǔ, shì quánqiú shǐyòng rénshù zuì duō de yídòng tōngxìn yìngyòng.
column3: WeChat launched in January 2011; in April of the same year it officially entered the international market under the English name WeChat; in December 2011 it began supporting SMS registration in 100 countries worldwide; and by the end of 2012 it covered more than 100 countries and regions. Today WeChat covers over 200 countries and regions, supports 16 foreign languages, and is the mobile messaging app with the most users in the world.

column1: 在美国互联网企业“称霸”全球的背景下，作为中国自己的移动互联网产品，微信的出现，自然吸引了更多的关注。
column2: Zài Měiguó hùliánwǎng qǐyè "chēngbà" quánqiú de bèijǐng xià, zuòwéi Zhōngguó zìjǐ de yídòng hùliánwǎng chǎnpǐn, Wēixìn de chūxiàn, zìrán xīyǐn le gèng duō de guānzhù.
column3: Against the backdrop of American internet companies "dominating" the globe, the emergence of WeChat, as China's own mobile internet product, naturally attracted even more attention.

column1: 被称为“微信之父”的腾讯公司高级副总裁张小龙介绍了微信的发展过程：微信的研究开发工作开展得很早，2010年底，移动互联网刚起步，腾讯广州产品研发中心就开始考虑相关业务。他们清楚地认识到了这样的现实——在个人计算机时代，由于中国互联网的用户数量以及市场成熟程度等都低于发达国家，在产品创新上难有领导地位，而移动互联网是一个重新开始的机会。
column2: Bèi chēngwéi "Wēixìn zhī fù" de Téngxùn gōngsī gāojí fùzǒngcái Zhāng Xiǎolóng jièshào le Wēixìn de fāzhǎn guòchéng: Wēixìn de yánjiū kāifā gōngzuò kāizhǎn de hěn zǎo, èr líng yī líng nián dǐ, yídòng hùliánwǎng gāng qǐbù, Téngxùn Guǎngzhōu chǎnpǐn yánfā zhōngxīn jiù kāishǐ kǎolǜ xiāngguān yèwù. Tāmen qīngchu de rènshi dào le zhèyàng de xiànshí—zài gèrén jìsuànjī shídài, yóuyú Zhōngguó hùliánwǎng de yònghù shùliàng yǐjí shìchǎng chéngshú chéngdù děng dōu dī yú fādá guójiā, zài chǎnpǐn chuàngxīn shang nán yǒu lǐngdǎo dìwèi, ér yídòng hùliánwǎng shì yí ge chóngxīn kāishǐ de jīhuì.
column3: Zhang Xiaolong, Tencent's senior vice president, known as "the father of WeChat", described how WeChat developed: research and development on WeChat began very early. At the end of 2010, when the mobile internet was just taking off, Tencent's Guangzhou product R&D center began considering related business. They clearly recognized this reality: in the PC era, because China's number of internet users and the maturity of its market were lower than those of developed countries, it was hard to take a leading position in product innovation, whereas the mobile internet was a chance to start afresh.

column1: 在经营销售上，微信针对不同的国家和地区，推出了不同的广告片，邀请当地明星和名人代言，收效相当不错。海外用户群中不仅有华裔和新移民，还出现了更多的外国人。
column2: Zài jīngyíng xiāoshòu shang, Wēixìn zhēnduì bùtóng de guójiā hé dìqū, tuīchū le bùtóng de guǎnggàopiàn, yāoqǐng dāngdì míngxīng hé míngrén dàiyán, shōuxiào xiāngdāng búcuò. Hǎiwài yònghù qún zhōng bùjǐn yǒu huáyì hé xīn yímín, hái chūxiàn le gèng duō de wàiguó rén.
column3: In marketing and sales, WeChat launched different ads for different countries and regions and invited local stars and celebrities to endorse it, with quite good results. Its overseas user base includes not only people of Chinese descent and new immigrants but also more and more foreigners.

column1: 篮球运动是1891年由美国马萨诸塞州的体育教师詹姆士·奈史密斯博士发明的。那年的冬天特别冷，奈史密斯所在的训练学校缺乏在室内进行的球类比赛项目，他从当地人把球扔进桃子篮（当地产桃子，各家各户都备有装桃子的专用篮子）的游戏中得到启发，将两只篮筐分别安装在体育馆两边看台的栏杆上，学生分为甲乙两队，以足球为比赛工具向篮内投，按得分多少决定输赢。
column2: Lánqiú yùndòng shì yī bā jiǔ yī nián yóu Měiguó Mǎsàzhūsāi Zhōu de tǐyù jiàoshī Zhānmǔshì Nàishǐmìsī bóshì fāmíng de. Nà nián de dōngtiān tèbié lěng, Nàishǐmìsī suǒzài de xùnliàn xuéxiào quēfá zài shìnèi jìnxíng de qiúlèi bǐsài xiàngmù, tā cóng dāngdìrén bǎ qiú rēngjìn táozi lán (dāngdì chǎn táozi, gèjiā gèhù dōu bèiyǒu zhuāng táozi de zhuānyòng lánzi) de yóuxì zhōng dédào qǐfā, jiāng liǎng zhī lánkuāng fēnbié ānzhuāng zài tǐyùguǎn liǎngbiān kàntái de lángān shang, xuésheng fēnwéi jiǎ yǐ liǎng duì, yǐ zúqiú wéi bǐsài gōngjù xiàng lán nèi tóu, àn défēn duōshǎo juédìng shūyíng.
column3: Basketball was invented in 1891 by Dr. James Naismith, a physical education teacher in Massachusetts, USA. That winter was especially cold, and the training school where Naismith worked lacked ball games that could be played indoors. He took inspiration from a game in which local people threw balls into peach baskets (the area grew peaches, and every household kept special baskets for holding them). He fixed two baskets to the railings of the stands on either side of the gym, split the students into Team A and Team B, and had them throw a soccer ball into the baskets, with the winner decided by the score.

column1: 这项运动很快流行起来。不过，由于栏杆上固定的是真正的篮筐，每当球投进时，就得有一个人踩着梯子上去把球取出来。这样的行为必须一再地重复，为此，比赛不得不断断续续地进行，缺少了激烈紧张的气氛，连运动员都不满意，更何况看比赛的球迷呢？为了解决这个问题，大家纷纷出主意，想出了很多取球的办法。有一位工程师甚至专门制造出一种机器，在下面一拉篮筐就能把球弹出来。可是，这些办法都没能让比赛顺畅起来。
column2: Zhè xiàng yùndòng hěn kuài liúxíng qilai. Búguò, yóuyú lángān shang gùdìng de shì zhēnzhèng de lánkuāng, měi dāng qiú tóujìn shí, jiù děi yǒu yí ge rén cǎizhe tīzi shàngqu bǎ qiú qǔ chulai. Zhèyàng de xíngwéi bìxū yízài de chóngfù, wèicǐ, bǐsài bùdébù duànduàn xùxù de jìnxíng, quēshǎo le jīliè jǐnzhāng de qìfēn, lián yùndòngyuán dōu bù mǎnyì, gèng hékuàng kàn bǐsài de qiúmí ne? Wèile jiějué zhège wèntí, dàjiā fēnfēn chū zhǔyi, xiǎng chu le hěn duō qǔ qiú de bànfǎ. Yǒu yí wèi gōngchéngshī shènzhì zhuānmén zhìzào chu yì zhǒng jīqì, zài xiàmiàn yì lā lánkuāng jiù néng bǎ qiú tán chulai. Kěshì, zhèxiē bànfǎ dōu méi néng ràng bǐsài shùnchàng qilai.
column3: The sport quickly caught on. However, because real baskets were fixed to the railings, every time the ball went in, someone had to climb up a ladder to take it out. This had to be repeated again and again, so the game could only go on in fits and starts and lacked an intense, exciting atmosphere. Even the players weren't satisfied, let alone the fans watching. To solve this problem, people offered one idea after another and came up with many ways to retrieve the ball. One engineer even built a special machine that could pop the ball out of the basket with a pull from below. But none of these methods made the game flow smoothly.

column1: 几年后的一天，一个上幼儿园的小男孩跟着父亲从一群正在进行篮球比赛的人旁边经过。看到大人们一次次辛苦地取球，小男孩好奇地问父亲：“何必这么麻烦呢？把篮筐的底去掉不就行了吗？”多亏了他这句话，人们如梦初醒，一位球员连忙找来一把锯子把篮筐的底锯掉。你瞧，困扰人们很长时间的取球问题就这样被一个小孩子解决了。
column2: Jǐ nián hòu de yì tiān, yí ge shàng yòu'éryuán de xiǎo nánhái gēnzhe fùqīn cóng yì qún zhèngzài jìnxíng lánqiú bǐsài de rén pángbiān jīngguò. Kàndào dàrenmen yícìcì xīnkǔ de qǔ qiú, xiǎo nánhái hàoqí de wèn fùqīn: "Hébì zhème máfan ne? Bǎ lánkuāng de dǐ qùdiào bú jiù xíng le ma?" Duōkuī le tā zhè jù huà, rénmen rúmèng chūxǐng, yí wèi qiúyuán liánmáng zhǎolái yì bǎ jùzi bǎ lánkuāng de dǐ jùdiào. Nǐ qiáo, kùnrǎo rénmen hěn cháng shíjiān de qǔ qiú wèntí jiù zhèyàng bèi yí ge xiǎo háizi jiějué le.
column3: One day a few years later, a little boy in kindergarten was walking with his father past a group of people playing basketball. Seeing the adults struggle to retrieve the ball time after time, the boy asked his father curiously, "Why go to all that trouble? Wouldn't it work if you just took out the bottom of the basket?" Thanks to what he said, people suddenly saw the light, and one player hurried to fetch a saw and sawed off the bottom of the basket. See—the ball-retrieving problem that had bothered people for so long was solved just like that by a small child.

column1: 去掉篮筐的底，本是一件简单的事，可为什么那么多人都没有想到呢？说白了，因为我们的思维像篮球一样被篮筐的底挡在了半空中。于是，我们呆呆地去搬梯子、造机器……其实，世界上本来就没有太复杂的事，复杂都是我们自己造成的。
column2: Qùdiào lánkuāng de dǐ, běn shì yí jiàn jiǎndān de shì, kě wèishénme nàme duō rén dōu méiyǒu xiǎngdào ne? Shuōbái le, yīnwèi wǒmen de sīwéi xiàng lánqiú yíyàng bèi lánkuāng de dǐ dǎng zài le bànkōng zhōng. Yúshì, wǒmen dāidāi de qù bān tīzi, zào jīqì…… Qíshí, shìjiè shang běnlái jiù méiyǒu tài fùzá de shì, fùzá dōu shì wǒmen zìjǐ zàochéng de.
column3: Removing the bottom of the basket was a simple thing, so why did so many people fail to think of it? To put it plainly, it's because our thinking, like the basketball, was blocked in midair by the bottom of the basket. So we blindly went off to carry ladders and build machines... In fact, there's nothing in the world that's really that complicated—the complexity is all of our own making.

column1: 生活仿佛篮筐，许多时候，我们需要的只不过是一把锯子，来锯掉那些阻碍我们的“筐底”。
column2: Shēnghuó fǎngfú lánkuāng, xǔduō shíhou, wǒmen xūyào de zhǐ búguò shì yì bǎ jùzi, lái jùdiào nàxiē zǔ'ài wǒmen de "kuāng dǐ".
column3: Life is like a basket: much of the time, all we need is a saw to cut away the "basket bottoms" that hold us back.

column1: “四”指东、西、南、北四面，“合”就是四面房屋围在一起，中间形成一个方形的院子。四合院在中国汉族民居中历史最悠久，分布最广泛。不过，只要人们一提到四合院，便自然会想到北京四合院，这是因为传统的北京四合院都有一套固定的样式，十分具有代表性，在各种各样的四合院中，北京四合院可以代表其主要特点。
column2: Sì zhǐ dōng, xī, nán, běi sì miàn, "hé" jiù shì sì miàn fángwū wéi zài yìqǐ, zhōngjiān xíngchéng yí ge fāngxíng de yuànzi. Sìhéyuàn zài Zhōngguó Hànzú mínjū zhōng lìshǐ zuì yōujiǔ, fēnbù zuì guǎngfàn. Búguò, zhǐyào rénmen yì tídào sìhéyuàn, biàn zìrán huì xiǎngdào Běijīng sìhéyuàn, zhè shì yīnwèi chuántǒng de Běijīng sìhéyuàn dōu yǒu yí tào gùdìng de yàngshì, shífēn jùyǒu dàibiǎoxìng, zài gèzhǒng gèyàng de sìhéyuàn zhōng, Běijīng sìhéyuàn kěyǐ dàibiǎo qí zhǔyào tèdiǎn.
column3: Si (four) refers to the four sides—east, west, south and north—and "he" (enclose) means the houses on the four sides enclose a square courtyard in the middle. Among the folk dwellings of China's Han people, the siheyuan has the longest history and is the most widely distributed. However, whenever people mention siheyuan, they naturally think of Beijing's, because traditional Beijing siheyuan all follow a fixed style and are highly representative; of all the many kinds of siheyuan, the Beijing siheyuan can represent their main features.

column1: 北京有各种规模的四合院。最简单的四合院只有一个院子，比较复杂的有两三个，而有钱人家的，通常是由好几座四合院并列组成的。大门一般开在东南角或西北角，院中的北房是正房，比其他房屋的规模大，一般包括长辈的卧室和具备日常起居、接待客人等功能的客厅。院子的两边是东西厢房，是晚辈们生活的地方。在正房和厢房之间建有走廊，可以供人行走和休息。院子是十分理想的室外生活空间。有的人家喜欢种草、养花、种竹子，有的人家则喜欢用大缸养金鱼。院子不仅拉近了人与自然的关系，也让家里人在此得到了感情的交流，对创造生活情趣起了很大作用，因而最为人们所喜爱。
column2: Běijīng yǒu gè zhǒng guīmó de sìhéyuàn. Zuì jiǎndān de sìhéyuàn zhǐ yǒu yí ge yuànzi, bǐjiào fùzá de yǒu liǎng sān ge, ér yǒuqián rénjiā de, tōngcháng shì yóu hǎo jǐ zuò sìhéyuàn bìngliè zǔchéng de. Dàmén yìbān kāi zài dōngnán jiǎo huò xīběi jiǎo, yuàn zhōng de běifáng shì zhèngfáng, bǐ qítā fángwū de guīmó dà, yìbān bāokuò zhǎngbèi de wòshì hé jùbèi rìcháng qǐjū, jiēdài kèrén děng gōngnéng de kètīng. Yuànzi de liǎngbiān shì dōng xī xiāngfáng, shì wǎnbèimen shēnghuó de dìfang. Zài zhèngfáng hé xiāngfáng zhījiān jiàn yǒu zǒuláng, kěyǐ gōng rén xíngzǒu hé xiūxi. Yuànzi shì shífēn lǐxiǎng de shìwài shēnghuó kōngjiān. Yǒu de rénjiā xǐhuan zhòng cǎo, yǎng huā, zhòng zhúzi, yǒu de rénjiā zé xǐhuan yòng dà gāng yǎng jīnyú. Yuànzi bùjǐn lājìn le rén yǔ zìrán de guānxi, yě ràng jiālirén zài cǐ dédào le gǎnqíng de jiāoliú, duì chuàngzào shēnghuó qíngqù qǐ le hěn dà zuòyòng, yīn'ér zuì wéi rénmen suǒ xǐ'ài.
column3: Beijing has siheyuan of all sizes. The simplest have only one courtyard, more complex ones have two or three, and those of wealthy families usually consist of several siheyuan side by side. The main gate is generally in the southeast or northwest corner. The north building in the courtyard is the main house; it is larger than the other buildings and usually contains the elders' bedrooms and a living room used for daily life and receiving guests. On the two sides of the courtyard are the east and west wing rooms, where the younger generation lives. Between the main house and the wing rooms are corridors where people can walk and rest. The courtyard is an ideal outdoor living space. Some families like to grow grass, flowers and bamboo, while others like to keep goldfish in big vats. The courtyard not only brings people closer to nature, but also lets family members share their feelings there; it does much to add charm to daily life, which is why people love it most.

column1: 只要关闭起大门，四合院内便形成一个封闭式的小环境。住在四合院里的人不常与周围的邻居打交道。在小院里，一家人过着与世无争的日子，充分享受家庭的乐趣，自然有一种令人感到自在亲切的气氛。但也有多户合住一座四合院的情况，被称为“大杂院”，住户多为普通劳动人民。邻里之间有时虽然也有矛盾，但更多时候是互帮互助，不是亲人胜过亲人，这种浓浓的情感是许多老北京人无法忘记的。
column2: Zhǐyào guānbì qi dàmén, sìhéyuàn nèi biàn xíngchéng yí ge fēngbìshì de xiǎo huánjìng. Zhù zài sìhéyuàn li de rén bù cháng yǔ zhōuwéi de línjū dǎ jiāodao. Zài xiǎoyuàn li, yìjiārén guòzhe yǔshì wúzhēng de rìzi, chōngfèn xiǎngshòu jiātíng de lèqù, zìrán yǒu yì zhǒng lìng rén gǎndào zìzai qīnqiè de qìfēn. Dàn yě yǒu duō hù hézhù yí zuò sìhéyuàn de qíngkuàng, bèi chēngwéi "dàzáyuàn", zhùhù duō wéi pǔtōng láodòng rénmín. Línlǐ zhījiān yǒushí suīrán yě yǒu máodùn, dàn gèng duō shíhou shì hùbāng hùzhù, bú shì qīnrén shèngguò qīnrén, zhè zhǒng nóngnóng de qínggǎn shì xǔduō lǎo Běijīngrén wúfǎ wàngjì de.
column3: Once the main gate is closed, the inside of a siheyuan becomes a small, enclosed world. People living in siheyuan don't often deal with the neighbors around them. In their little courtyard, the family lives a life aloof from worldly strife and fully enjoys the pleasures of home, so naturally there is a relaxed, warm atmosphere. But sometimes several households share one siheyuan; this is called a "dazayuan" (compound courtyard), and the residents are mostly ordinary working people. Although neighbors sometimes have conflicts, more often they help each other out and are closer than family even though they aren't related. This deep affection is something many old Beijingers can never forget.

column1: 两千二百多年前的战国末期，赵国名将赵奢有个儿子叫赵括，他从小就熟读兵书，跟别人谈论起军事来，没有人说得过他，就是父亲赵奢也难不住他。赵括因此很骄傲，自以为天下无敌，连父亲也不放在眼里。
column2: Liǎngqiān èrbǎi duō nián qián de Zhànguó mòqī, Zhào guó míngjiàng Zhào Shē yǒu ge érzi jiào Zhào Kuò, tā cóngxiǎo jiù shúdú bīngshū, gēn biéren tánlùn qi jūnshì lai, méiyǒu rén shuō de guò tā, jiùshì fùqīn Zhào Shē yě nán bu zhù tā. Zhào Kuò yīncǐ hěn jiāo'ào, zì yǐwéi tiānxià wúdí, lián fùqīn yě bú fàng zài yǎn li.
column3: More than 2,200 years ago, at the end of the Warring States period, Zhao She, a famous general of the State of Zhao, had a son named Zhao Kuo. Since childhood he had studied military books thoroughly, and when he discussed military affairs with others, no one could out-argue him—not even his father Zhao She could stump him. Because of this Zhao Kuo became very arrogant, thinking himself invincible, and didn't even take his father seriously.

column1: 但是赵奢心里明白，自己的儿子虽然对军事理论都很了解，但是没有实战经验，想法很不符合实际。他曾经偷偷对妻子说：“儿子的本事是会讲大道理，缺乏实际锻炼，不能当大将。如果让他当了大将，迟早会害了赵国。”
column2: Dànshì Zhào Shē xīnli míngbai, zìjǐ de érzi suīrán duì jūnshì lǐlùn dōu hěn liǎojiě, dànshì méiyǒu shízhàn jīngyàn, xiǎngfǎ hěn bù fúhé shíjì. Tā céngjīng tōutōu duì qīzi shuō: "Érzi de běnshi shì huì jiǎng dà dàoli, quēfá shíjì duànliàn, bù néng dāng dàjiàng. Rúguǒ ràng tā dāng le dàjiàng, chízǎo huì hài le Zhào guó."
column3: But Zhao She knew in his heart that although his son understood military theory well, he had no real combat experience and his ideas were far from reality. He once told his wife privately, "Our son's skill is talking about grand principles; he lacks practical training and can't be a general. If he's made a general, sooner or later he'll bring ruin to Zhao."

column1: 几年后，赵奢去世了。这一年正好秦国军队来打赵国，赵国派老将廉颇带20万大军迎战。廉颇根据敌强我弱的形势，命令士兵们坚守阵地，绝对不可主动出战。秦军多次挑战，骂他是胆小鬼，他还是不出兵。这个办法果然非常有效，成功地把秦军拦在了国门之外。渐渐地，秦军无法快速取得胜利，粮食也快没了，产生了撤军的念头。
column2: Jǐ nián hòu, Zhào Shē qùshì le. Zhè yì nián zhènghǎo Qín guó jūnduì lái dǎ Zhào guó, Zhào guó pài lǎojiàng Lián Pō dài èrshí wàn dàjūn yíngzhàn. Lián Pō gēnjù dí qiáng wǒ ruò de xíngshì, mìnglìng shìbīngmen jiānshǒu zhèndì, juéduì bù kě zhǔdòng chūzhàn. Qín jūn duō cì tiǎozhàn, mà tā shì dǎnxiǎoguǐ, tā háishi bù chūbīng. Zhège bànfǎ guǒrán fēicháng yǒuxiào, chénggōng de bǎ Qín jūn lán zài le guómén zhī wài. Jiànjiàn de, Qín jūn wúfǎ kuàisù qǔdé shènglì, liángshi yě kuài méi le, chǎnshēng le chèjūn de niàntou.
column3: A few years later, Zhao She died. That very year the army of Qin came to attack Zhao, and Zhao sent the veteran general Lian Po with an army of 200,000 to meet them. Seeing that the enemy was strong and they were weak, Lian Po ordered his soldiers to hold their positions and absolutely not to take the offensive. The Qin army challenged them many times and called him a coward, but he still didn't send out his troops. This approach proved very effective and kept the Qin army outside the borders. Gradually, unable to win quickly and running out of food, the Qin army began to think about withdrawing.

column1: 秦人深知廉颇善于用兵，如果想在短期内打败赵国，必须想办法叫赵国把廉颇调回去。于是，他们在赵国四处散布谣言，说秦军最怕赵括，别的人都不放在眼里。
column2: Qín rén shēn zhī Lián Pō shànyú yòngbīng, rúguǒ xiǎng zài duǎnqī nèi dǎbài Zhào guó, bìxū xiǎng bànfǎ jiào Zhào guó bǎ Lián Pō diào huiqu. Yúshì, tāmen zài Zhào guó sìchù sànbù yáoyán, shuō Qín jūn zuì pà Zhào Kuò, bié de rén dōu bú fàng zài yǎn li.
column3: The Qin knew well that Lian Po was skilled at commanding troops; if they wanted to defeat Zhao in a short time, they had to find a way to get Zhao to recall him. So they spread rumors all over Zhao, saying that the Qin army feared Zhao Kuo most and didn't take anyone else seriously.

column1: 这时，赵王正因廉颇闭门不战而生气呢，听到外面的那些谣言，果然上当了，他派赵括去换回廉颇。赵括的母亲再三阻止赵王任命儿子为大将，说他还没有独立带兵作战的资格。可是，糊涂的赵王哪里听得进去！
column2: Zhè shí, Zhào wáng zhèng yīn Lián Pō bìmén bú zhàn ér shēngqì ne, tīngdào wàimiàn de nàxiē yáoyán, guǒrán shàngdàng le, tā pài Zhào Kuò qù huàn huí Lián Pō. Zhào Kuò de mǔqīn zàisān zǔzhǐ Zhào wáng rènmìng érzi wéi dàjiàng, shuō tā hái méiyǒu dúlì dài bīng zuòzhàn de zīgé. Kěshì, hútu de Zhào wáng nǎli tīng de jìnqu!
column3: At this time the King of Zhao was angry that Lian Po was staying behind closed gates and refusing to fight. When he heard those rumors, he fell for them, just as Qin had hoped, and sent Zhao Kuo to replace Lian Po. Zhao Kuo's mother repeatedly tried to stop the king from appointing her son as general, saying he was not yet qualified to lead troops into battle on his own. But how could the muddle-headed king listen?

column1: 公元前260年，赵括带兵出战。一直盲目自信、轻视秦军的他完全改变了廉颇的作战方案，死搬兵书上的理论，主动进攻秦军，结果数十万赵军全部被杀，丢掉了宝贵的生命。
column2: Gōngyuán qián èr liù líng nián, Zhào Kuò dài bīng chūzhàn. Yìzhí mángmù zìxìn, qīngshì Qín jūn de tā wánquán gǎibiàn le Lián Pō de zuòzhàn fāng'àn, sǐ bān bīngshū shang de lǐlùn, zhǔdòng jìngōng Qín jūn, jiéguǒ shù shí wàn Zhào jūn quánbù bèi shā, diūdiào le bǎoguì de shēngmìng.
column3: In 260 BC, Zhao Kuo led his troops into battle. Blindly self-confident all along and contemptuous of the Qin army, he completely changed Lian Po's battle plan, rigidly applied the theories from his military books, and took the offensive against Qin. As a result, several hundred thousand Zhao soldiers were all killed, losing their precious lives.

column1: 这就是成语“纸上谈兵”的故事。现在常用这个成语讽刺那些只会空谈理论的人，提醒大家做事一定要灵活，要注意理论联系实际。
column2: Zhè jiù shì chéngyǔ "zhǐshàng tánbīng" de gùshi. Xiànzài cháng yòng zhège chéngyǔ fěngcì nàxiē zhǐ huì kōngtán lǐlùn de rén, tíxǐng dàjiā zuòshì yídìng yào línghuó, yào zhùyì lǐlùn liánxì shíjì.
column3: This is the story behind the idiom "zhi shang tan bing" (discussing warfare on paper). Today the idiom is often used to mock people who can only talk theory, reminding everyone to be flexible in what they do and to make sure theory is linked to practice.

column1: 一项最新的研究发现：由于人们在一周内的营养摄入和饮食模式会影响到他们的体重变化，因此节食者的体重会在一周内上下波动。
column2: Yí xiàng zuìxīn de yánjiū fāxiàn: yóuyú rénmen zài yì zhōu nèi de yíngyǎng shèrù hé yǐnshí móshì huì yǐngxiǎng dào tāmen de tǐzhòng biànhuà, yīncǐ jiéshízhě de tǐzhòng huì zài yì zhōu nèi shàngxià bōdòng.
column3: A new study has found that because people's nutrient intake and eating patterns over a week affect changes in their weight, dieters' weight fluctuates up and down within a week.

column1: 总共有80名年龄在25～62岁之间的成年人参与了这项研究。研究人员根据他们的相对体重变化将其分为三种类型：体重减轻者、体重增加者和体重保持者。这些成年人在每天起床之后、早餐之前称一下自己的体重，为了保证可靠性，只有那些至少连续7天以上称过体重的人才会被纳入分析。对这些志愿者的跟踪调查时间最短为15天，最长为330天。
column2: Zǒnggòng yǒu bāshí míng niánlíng zài èrshíwǔ dào liùshí'èr suì zhījiān de chéngniánrén cānyù le zhè xiàng yánjiū. Yánjiū rényuán gēnjù tāmen de xiāngduì tǐzhòng biànhuà jiāng qí fēnwéi sān zhǒng lèixíng: tǐzhòng jiǎnqīngzhě, tǐzhòng zēngjiāzhě hé tǐzhòng bǎochízhě. Zhèxiē chéngniánrén zài měitiān qǐchuáng zhīhòu, zǎocān zhīqián chēng yíxià zìjǐ de tǐzhòng, wèile bǎozhèng kěkàoxìng, zhǐyǒu nàxiē zhìshǎo liánxù qī tiān yǐshàng chēngguo tǐzhòng de rén cái huì bèi nàrù fēnxī. Duì zhèxiē zhìyuànzhě de gēnzōng diàochá shíjiān zuì duǎn wéi shíwǔ tiān, zuì cháng wéi sānbǎi sānshí tiān.
column3: A total of 80 adults aged between 25 and 62 took part in the study. Based on their relative weight change, the researchers divided them into three types: weight losers, weight gainers and weight maintainers. Every day these adults weighed themselves after getting up and before breakfast. To ensure reliability, only those who had weighed themselves for at least seven consecutive days were included in the analysis. The volunteers were followed for as little as 15 days and as long as 330 days.

column1: 研究成果显示：这些人的体重变化表现出清晰的模式，即周末之后体重升高，在工作日体重减轻（周五达到最低点）。研究人员还意外地发现，体重减轻者和体重增加者在体重波动模式上存在着明显不同。体重减轻者会表现出较强的补偿模式，即在周末之后体重立即下降，这一下降趋势直至周五结束；而体重增加者每天的体重都会存在差异，他们在工作日的体重并无明显减轻。
column2: Yánjiū chéngguǒ xiǎnshì: zhèxiē rén de tǐzhòng biànhuà biǎoxiàn chū qīngxī de móshì, jí zhōumò zhīhòu tǐzhòng shēnggāo, zài gōngzuòrì tǐzhòng jiǎnqīng (zhōuwǔ dádào zuì dī diǎn). Yánjiū rényuán hái yìwài de fāxiàn, tǐzhòng jiǎnqīngzhě hé tǐzhòng zēngjiāzhě zài tǐzhòng bōdòng móshì shang cúnzàizhe míngxiǎn bùtóng. Tǐzhòng jiǎnqīngzhě huì biǎoxiàn chū jiào qiáng de bǔcháng móshì, jí zài zhōumò zhīhòu tǐzhòng lìjí xiàjiàng, zhè yí xiàjiàng qūshì zhízhì zhōuwǔ jiéshù; ér tǐzhòng zēngjiāzhě měitiān de tǐzhòng dōu huì cúnzài chāyì, tāmen zài gōngzuòrì de tǐzhòng bìng wú míngxiǎn jiǎnqīng.
column3: The results showed a clear pattern in these people's weight changes: weight rose after the weekend and fell on workdays (reaching its lowest point on Friday). The researchers also unexpectedly found that weight losers and weight gainers differed clearly in their patterns of fluctuation. Weight losers showed a stronger compensation pattern: their weight dropped right after the weekend, and this downward trend continued until Friday. Weight gainers, on the other hand, had weight that varied from day to day, with no obvious drop on workdays.

column1: 这项联合多所医学院校所做的研究发现，除了个别人以外，多数人体重的增加会从周六开始，而体重减轻则会从周二开始，特别是对于那些体重减轻者和体重保持者来说更是如此。它表明人们的体重变化在一周内会显示出一种明显的规律，工作日和周末体重的临时变化应该被视为正常现象，而非真正的体重增加，这是由于人们在周末会有更多的时间外出就餐。周末对饮食稍微有些放纵影响不大，但为了能成功减轻体重，想要变苗条的节食者应注意到这种变化规律，周末之后不要再找任何吃美食的借口，应及时采取措施阻止这一上升趋势。
column2: Zhè xiàng liánhé duō suǒ yīxué yuànxiào suǒ zuò de yánjiū fāxiàn, chúle gèbié rén yǐwài, duōshù rén tǐzhòng de zēngjiā huì cóng zhōuliù kāishǐ, ér tǐzhòng jiǎnqīng zé huì cóng zhōu'èr kāishǐ, tèbié shì duìyú nàxiē tǐzhòng jiǎnqīngzhě hé tǐzhòng bǎochízhě lái shuō gèng shì rúcǐ. Tā biǎomíng rénmen de tǐzhòng biànhuà zài yì zhōu nèi huì xiǎnshì chū yì zhǒng míngxiǎn de guīlǜ, gōngzuòrì hé zhōumò tǐzhòng de línshí biànhuà yīnggāi bèi shìwéi zhèngcháng xiànxiàng, ér fēi zhēnzhèng de tǐzhòng zēngjiā, zhè shì yóuyú rénmen zài zhōumò huì yǒu gèng duō de shíjiān wàichū jiùcān. Zhōumò duì yǐnshí shāowēi yǒuxiē fàngzòng yǐngxiǎng bú dà, dàn wèile néng chénggōng jiǎnqīng tǐzhòng, xiǎng yào biàn miáotiao de jiéshízhě yīng zhùyì dào zhè zhǒng biànhuà guīlǜ, zhōumò zhīhòu búyào zài zhǎo rènhé chī měishí de jièkǒu, yīng jíshí cǎiqǔ cuòshī zǔzhǐ zhè yí shàngshēng qūshì.
column3: This study, carried out jointly by several medical schools, found that with few exceptions, most people's weight starts to rise on Saturday and starts to fall on Tuesday—especially for weight losers and weight maintainers. It shows that people's weight changes follow a clear pattern over the week; the temporary changes between workdays and weekends should be seen as normal rather than as real weight gain, and they happen because people have more time to eat out on weekends. Indulging a little on weekends doesn't matter much, but to lose weight successfully, dieters who want to slim down should be aware of this pattern, stop making excuses to eat good food after the weekend, and take timely steps to stop the upward trend.

column1: 我奶奶说过：“人们应该在最美好的时候离开。”因为这个认知而获得诺贝尔奖的，不是我奶奶，而是心理学家丹尼尔·卡内曼。他将这一现象命名为“峰终定律”：我们对事物的记忆仅在高峰和结尾，而事情的经过对记忆几乎没有影响。高峰之后，终点出现得越迅速，这件事留给我们的印象就越深刻。
column2: Wǒ nǎinai shuōguo: "Rénmen yīnggāi zài zuì měihǎo de shíhou líkāi." Yīnwèi zhège rènzhī ér huòdé Nuòbèi'ěr jiǎng de, bú shì wǒ nǎinai, ér shì xīnlǐxuéjiā Dānní'ěr Kǎnèimàn. Tā jiāng zhè yí xiànxiàng mìngmíng wéi "fēng zhōng dìnglǜ": wǒmen duì shìwù de jìyì jǐn zài gāofēng hé jiéwěi, ér shìqing de jīngguò duì jìyì jīhū méiyǒu yǐngxiǎng. Gāofēng zhīhòu, zhōngdiǎn chūxiàn de yuè xùnsù, zhè jiàn shì liú gěi wǒmen de yìnxiàng jiù yuè shēnkè.
column3: My grandmother once said, "People should leave at the best moment." The person who won a Nobel Prize for this insight was not my grandmother but the psychologist Daniel Kahneman. He named the phenomenon the "peak-end rule": our memory of something rests only on its peak and its end, while the course of events has almost no effect on memory. The sooner the end comes after the peak, the deeper the impression the experience leaves on us.

column1: 大部分人不理解这一定律。比如说为了一场戏剧演出，我们会投入很多时间，准备服装、化妆、道具、舞台美术，以创造良好的效果，争取给观众留下一个好的印象，却常常忽视结束退场时的准备。演出开始时人们认为很有魅力，但是糟糕的结局会给人留下难以忘记的坏印象。
column2: Dà bùfen rén bù lǐjiě zhè yí dìnglǜ. Bǐrú shuō wèile yì chǎng xìjù yǎnchū, wǒmen huì tóurù hěn duō shíjiān, zhǔnbèi fúzhuāng, huàzhuāng, dàojù, wǔtái měishù, yǐ chuàngzào liánghǎo de xiàoguǒ, zhēngqǔ gěi guānzhòng liúxià yí ge hǎo de yìnxiàng, què chángcháng hūshì jiéshù tuìchǎng shí de zhǔnbèi. Yǎnchū kāishǐ shí rénmen rènwéi hěn yǒu mèilì, dànshì zāogāo de jiéjú huì gěi rén liúxià nányǐ wàngjì de huài yìnxiàng.
column3: Most people don't understand this rule. For example, for a stage performance we put in a lot of time preparing costumes, makeup, props and stage design to create a good effect and leave the audience with a good impression, yet we often neglect preparing for the ending and the exit. People may find the start of the show very appealing, but a poor ending leaves a bad impression that's hard to forget.

column1: 有一次，我去参加一个婚礼，前三个小时感觉都很好，只在最后一个小时感到无聊。三个小时快乐减一个小时无聊等于两个小时快乐，也就是说，我愉快地度过了两个小时。但是，我的记忆并不是这样计算的。如果我参加另外一次活动，只在那里待一个小时，早早地告别，我却享受了满满60分钟的快乐。与第一次相比，第二次的聚会留给我的印象更为美好。
column2: Yǒu yí cì, wǒ qù cānjiā yí ge hūnlǐ, qián sān ge xiǎoshí gǎnjué dōu hěn hǎo, zhǐ zài zuìhòu yí ge xiǎoshí gǎndào wúliáo. Sān ge xiǎoshí kuàilè jiǎn yí ge xiǎoshí wúliáo děngyú liǎng ge xiǎoshí kuàilè, yě jiùshì shuō, wǒ yúkuài de dùguò le liǎng ge xiǎoshí. Dànshì, wǒ de jìyì bìng bú shì zhèyàng jìsuàn de. Rúguǒ wǒ cānjiā lìngwài yí cì huódòng, zhǐ zài nàli dāi yí ge xiǎoshí, zǎozǎo de gàobié, wǒ què xiǎngshòu le mǎnmǎn liùshí fēnzhōng de kuàilè. Yǔ dì-yī cì xiāngbǐ, dì-èr cì de jùhuì liú gěi wǒ de yìnxiàng gèng wéi měihǎo.
column3: Once I went to a wedding. The first three hours felt great; only the last hour was boring. Three hours of fun minus one hour of boredom equals two hours of fun—in other words, I spent two pleasant hours. But my memory doesn't calculate it that way. If I go to another event, stay only an hour and leave early, I've enjoyed a full 60 minutes of fun. Compared with the first, the second gathering leaves me with a better impression.

column1: 看电影也是如此。一部电影，开始虽然剧情平平常常，如果最后半个小时能使我们感动，我们依然会向别人推荐它。相反，如果在前半个小时就把剧情的创造力表现得淋漓尽致，结尾却非常普通，那么，观众对这部电影的评价就肯定不好，甚至会说这是一部“烂片”。
column2: Kàn diànyǐng yě shì rúcǐ. Yí bù diànyǐng, kāishǐ suīrán jùqíng píngpíng chángcháng, rúguǒ zuìhòu bàn ge xiǎoshí néng shǐ wǒmen gǎndòng, wǒmen yīrán huì xiàng biéren tuījiàn tā. Xiāngfǎn, rúguǒ zài qián bàn ge xiǎoshí jiù bǎ jùqíng de chuàngzàolì biǎoxiàn de línlí jìnzhì, jiéwěi què fēicháng pǔtōng, nàme, guānzhòng duì zhè bù diànyǐng de píngjià jiù kěndìng bù hǎo, shènzhì huì shuō zhè shì yí bù "lànpiàn".
column3: The same goes for watching movies. Even if a film's plot is ordinary at first, if the last half hour moves us, we'll still recommend it to others. On the other hand, if the plot's creativity is fully displayed in the first half hour but the ending is very ordinary, the audience will certainly rate the film poorly and may even call it a "bad movie."

column1: 作为电视节目主持人，我在工作中常常会运用“峰终定律”。例如，做节目时，与开幕式相比，我们宁可把更多的精力集中在闭幕式上，这样可以加强观众对节目的印象。虽然很多人并不了解“峰终定律”，但是，他们能从经验中体会这种做法的重要性。
column2: Zuòwéi diànshì jiémù zhǔchírén, wǒ zài gōngzuò zhōng chángcháng huì yùnyòng "fēng zhōng dìnglǜ". Lìrú, zuò jiémù shí, yǔ kāimùshì xiāngbǐ, wǒmen nìngkě bǎ gèng duō de jīnglì jízhōng zài bìmùshì shang, zhèyàng kěyǐ jiāqiáng guānzhòng duì jiémù de yìnxiàng. Suīrán hěn duō rén bìng bù liǎojiě "fēng zhōng dìnglǜ", dànshì, tāmen néng cóng jīngyàn zhōng tǐhuì zhè zhǒng zuòfǎ de zhòngyàoxìng.
column3: As a TV host, I often use the "peak-end rule" in my work. For example, when making a show, we would rather focus more energy on the closing ceremony than on the opening, because this strengthens the audience's impression of the show. Although many people don't know about the "peak-end rule," they can sense the importance of this approach from experience.

column1: 对有些人来说，抽象艺术没有古典艺术那么容易欣赏，画布上那些不规则的色块、线条，实在看不出有什么意义。抽象派画家的作品中经常见到好像随便洒上颜料而形成的画作，在有人看来极其神秘甚至丑陋，有人却从中感受到对自由、对生命的赞美。
column2: Duì yǒuxiē rén lái shuō, chōuxiàng yìshù méiyǒu gǔdiǎn yìshù nàme róngyì xīnshǎng, huàbù shang nàxiē bù guīzé de sèkuài, xiàntiáo, shízài kàn bu chū yǒu shénme yìyì. Chōuxiàngpài huàjiā de zuòpǐn zhōng jīngcháng jiàndào hǎoxiàng suíbiàn sǎ shang yánliào ér xíngchéng de huàzuò, zài yǒu rén kànlái jíqí shénmì shènzhì chǒulòu, yǒu rén què cóng zhōng gǎnshòu dào duì zìyóu, duì shēngmìng de zànměi.
column3: For some people, abstract art is not as easy to appreciate as classical art; they really can't see any meaning in the irregular patches of color and lines on the canvas. Among the works of abstract painters one often sees paintings that look as if paint had been splashed on at random. To some people they seem extremely mysterious or even ugly, while others feel in them a celebration of freedom and of life.

column1: 研究者设计了一个有趣的实验。志愿者的任务很简单，每个人会看到两两一组出现的一些图画，每组中一幅出自著名抽象艺术家之手，另一幅是业余爱好者、婴儿、黑猩猩或者大象的涂鸦。志愿者必须判断每一组画作中自己更喜欢哪一幅。
column2: Yánjiūzhě shèjì le yí ge yǒuqù de shíyàn. Zhìyuànzhě de rènwu hěn jiǎndān, měi ge rén huì kàndào liǎngliǎng yì zǔ chūxiàn de yìxiē túhuà, měi zǔ zhōng yì fú chūzì zhùmíng chōuxiàng yìshùjiā zhī shǒu, lìng yì fú shì yèyú àihàozhě, yīng'ér, hēixīngxing huòzhě dàxiàng de túyā. Zhìyuànzhě bìxū pànduàn měi yì zǔ huàzuò zhōng zìjǐ gèng xǐhuan nǎ yì fú.
column3: Researchers designed an interesting experiment. The volunteers' task was simple: each person would see pictures shown in pairs. In each pair, one was by a famous abstract artist, and the other was a scribble by an amateur, a baby, a chimpanzee or an elephant. The volunteers had to decide which painting in each pair they liked better.

column1: 其中三分之一的画作作者没有签名，而其余的则标明了身份。令人头疼的是，一些签名被故意弄错了，志愿者无法确认作者到底是谁，所以有可能志愿者认为自己看到的是黑猩猩的随手涂鸦，实际则是著名抽象艺术家的大作。
column2: Qízhōng sān fēn zhī yī de huàzuò zuòzhě méiyǒu qiānmíng, ér qíyú de zé biāomíng le shēnfèn. Lìng rén tóuténg de shì, yìxiē qiānmíng bèi gùyì nòngcuò le, zhìyuànzhě wúfǎ quèrèn zuòzhě dàodǐ shì shéi, suǒyǐ yǒu kěnéng zhìyuànzhě rènwéi zìjǐ kàndào de shì hēixīngxing de suíshǒu túyā, shíjì zé shì zhùmíng chōuxiàng yìshùjiā de dàzuò.
column3: One third of the paintings had no artist's signature, while the rest had the artist's identity marked. The tricky part was that some signatures were deliberately mislabeled, so the volunteers couldn't be sure who the artist really was. A volunteer might therefore think they were looking at a chimpanzee's random scribble when it was actually a masterpiece by a famous abstract artist.

column1: 也许有人认为，在这种情况下根本不可能分辨出来。然而在每一次测试中，志愿者普遍更喜欢的作品都是由人类艺术家挥笔完成的。由此可见，志愿者能够从画作中感知艺术家的用心，哪怕他们不能够解释原因。
column2: Yěxǔ yǒu rén rènwéi, zài zhè zhǒng qíngkuàng xià gēnběn bù kěnéng fēnbiàn chulai. Rán'ér zài měi yí cì cèshì zhōng, zhìyuànzhě pǔbiàn gèng xǐhuan de zuòpǐn dōu shì yóu rénlèi yìshùjiā huībǐ wánchéng de. Yóucǐ kějiàn, zhìyuànzhě nénggòu cóng huàzuò zhōng gǎnzhī yìshùjiā de yòngxīn, nǎpà tāmen bù nénggòu jiěshì yuányīn.
column3: Some might think it would be impossible to tell them apart under these conditions. Yet in every test, the works the volunteers generally preferred were those painted by human artists. This shows that volunteers can sense the artist's intention in a painting, even if they can't explain why.

column1: 另一个实验是这样，志愿者同时欣赏原作和画面元素被调整后的画作，包括静物画和抽象画。结果，几乎每个人都更喜欢原作。研究者发现，当看到画上物体位置变化后，大脑中有关含意和解释的区域活跃性下降了。这表明，我们的大脑注意到了原作的布局，并且可以感知其背后的用意，即使我们还没有清楚地感受到这个事实。至少目前可以这么说，没有证据表明黑猩猩或儿童可以这样做。
column2: Lìng yí ge shíyàn shì zhèyàng, zhìyuànzhě tóngshí xīnshǎng yuánzuò hé huàmiàn yuánsù bèi tiáozhěng hòu de huàzuò, bāokuò jìngwùhuà hé chōuxiànghuà. Jiéguǒ, jīhū měi ge rén dōu gèng xǐhuan yuánzuò. Yánjiūzhě fāxiàn, dāng kàndào huà shang wùtǐ wèizhi biànhuà hòu, dànǎo zhōng yǒuguān hányì hé jiěshì de qūyù huóyuèxìng xiàjiàng le. Zhè biǎomíng, wǒmen de dànǎo zhùyì dào le yuánzuò de bùjú, bìngqiě kěyǐ gǎnzhī qí bèihòu de yòngyì, jíshǐ wǒmen hái méiyǒu qīngchu de gǎnshòu dào zhège shìshí. Zhìshǎo mùqián kěyǐ zhème shuō, méiyǒu zhèngjù biǎomíng hēixīngxing huò értóng kěyǐ zhèyàng zuò.
column3: Another experiment went like this: volunteers viewed original paintings alongside versions whose elements had been rearranged, including still lifes and abstract paintings. Almost everyone preferred the originals. The researchers found that when people saw that the positions of objects in a painting had changed, activity dropped in the brain regions related to meaning and interpretation. This shows that our brains notice the composition of the original and can sense the intention behind it, even if we aren't yet clearly aware of this. At least for now, it can be said that there is no evidence that chimpanzees or children can do this.

column1: 我们的大脑究竟如何感知抽象艺术，是一个有趣的话题。每个人对抽象艺术可以有不同的解读，这既是挑战，也是自由。
column2: Wǒmen de dànǎo jiūjìng rúhé gǎnzhī chōuxiàng yìshù, shì yí ge yǒuqù de huàtí. Měi ge rén duì chōuxiàng yìshù kěyǐ yǒu bùtóng de jiědú, zhè jì shì tiǎozhàn, yě shì zìyóu.
column3: How exactly our brains perceive abstract art is an interesting topic. Everyone can interpret abstract art differently; this is both a challenge and a freedom.

column1: 家乡的众多美食中，萝卜饼是最让我怀念的。它那丰富的色彩、微甜的口感，至今仍让我十分想念。
column2: Jiāxiāng de zhòngduō měishí zhōng, luóbobǐng shì zuì ràng wǒ huáiniàn de. Tā nà fēngfù de sècǎi, wēi tián de kǒugǎn, zhìjīn réng ràng wǒ shífēn xiǎngniàn.
column3: Of all the many delicacies of my hometown, radish pancakes are what I miss most. Their rich colors and slightly sweet taste still make me long for them to this day.

column1: 家乡的萝卜有青、红、紫三种。三种萝卜看起来赏心悦目，吃起来，青的苦中带点儿甜，红的辣中带着甜，紫的像山泉般清淡可口。父老乡亲们夸它说：“橘子、葡萄、梨，比不上咱的萝卜皮。”而萝卜饼就是用这三种颜色的萝卜做成的。
column2: Jiāxiāng de luóbo yǒu qīng, hóng, zǐ sān zhǒng. Sān zhǒng luóbo kàn qilai shǎngxīn yuèmù, chī qilai, qīng de kǔ zhōng dài diǎnr tián, hóng de là zhōng dàizhe tián, zǐ de xiàng shānquán bān qīngdàn kěkǒu. Fùlǎo xiāngqīnmen kuā tā shuō: "Júzi, pútao, lí, bǐ bu shàng zán de luóbo pí." Ér luóbobǐng jiù shì yòng zhè sān zhǒng yánsè de luóbo zuòchéng de.
column3: My hometown's radishes come in three kinds: green, red and purple. All three are a pleasure to look at. As for the taste, the green ones are bitter with a hint of sweetness, the red ones are spicy with sweetness, and the purple ones are light and tasty like mountain spring water. The local folks praise them, saying: "Oranges, grapes and pears can't compare with the skin of our radishes." And radish pancakes are made with these three colors of radish.

column1: 萝卜饼的做法极其简单，既不必炒或煮，也不用油炸。先把三色萝卜洗净切丝，放入油、盐等，用筷子搅拌均匀，萝卜饼的原料便做成了。最关键的功夫是擀面。高手往往把面擀得薄如白纸，拌好的萝卜丝儿铺到饼上后，得再折叠两三次，要求饼熟之后表皮是透明的，能透过表皮看见萝卜丝儿。最后用刀切成块状，饼便做好了。
column2: Luóbobǐng de zuòfǎ jíqí jiǎndān, jì búbì chǎo huò zhǔ, yě búyòng yóuzhá. Xiān bǎ sān sè luóbo xǐjìng qiē sī, fàngrù yóu, yán děng, yòng kuàizi jiǎobàn jūnyún, luóbobǐng de yuánliào biàn zuòchéng le. Zuì guānjiàn de gōngfu shì gǎn miàn. Gāoshǒu wǎngwǎng bǎ miàn gǎn de báo rú bái zhǐ, bànhǎo de luóbo sīr pūdào bǐng shang hòu, děi zài zhédié liǎng sān cì, yāoqiú bǐng shú zhīhòu biǎopí shì tòumíng de, néng tòuguò biǎopí kànjiàn luóbo sīr. Zuìhòu yòng dāo qiēchéng kuàizhuàng, bǐng biàn zuòhǎo le.
column3: Radish pancakes are extremely simple to make: there's no need to stir-fry or boil them, nor to deep-fry them. First wash the three colors of radish and cut them into shreds, add oil, salt and so on, and mix evenly with chopsticks—and the filling is ready. The most crucial skill is rolling out the dough. Experts often roll it as thin as white paper. After the mixed radish shreds are spread on the dough, it must be folded two or three more times; when cooked, the skin should be transparent so you can see the radish shreds through it. Finally, cut it into pieces with a knife, and the pancakes are ready.

column1: 接下来，拿一个平底锅，先在锅里淋一圈油，待油锅烫手时，将切好的萝卜饼一块一块地放进锅里。盖锅前须放进一些温水，预防糊底。火最好用文火，等能闻到香味时，便可开锅了。萝卜饼要趁热吃，喜欢口味重的，还可以加少许酱油和醋。刚出锅的萝卜饼，香味扑鼻，外焦里嫩，吃上一口，便让人永远忘不了。
column2: Jiē xialai, ná yí ge píngdǐguō, xiān zài guō li lín yì quān yóu, dài yóuguō tàng shǒu shí, jiāng qiēhǎo de luóbobǐng yí kuài yí kuài de fàngjìn guō li. Gài guō qián xū fàngjìn yìxiē wēnshuǐ, yùfáng hú dǐ. Huǒ zuìhǎo yòng wénhuǒ, děng néng wéndào xiāngwèi shí, biàn kě kāi guō le. Luóbobǐng yào chèn rè chī, xǐhuan kǒuwèi zhòng de, hái kěyǐ jiā shǎoxǔ jiàngyóu hé cù. Gāng chū guō de luóbobǐng, xiāngwèi pū bí, wài jiāo lǐ nèn, chī shang yì kǒu, biàn ràng rén yǒngyuǎn wàng bu liǎo.
column3: Next, take a frying pan and first drizzle a circle of oil into it. When the oil is hot enough to burn your hand, put the cut pancakes into the pan piece by piece. Before covering the pan, add some warm water to keep the bottom from burning. Low heat is best; when you can smell the aroma, you can open the lid. Radish pancakes should be eaten hot, and those who like stronger flavors can add a little soy sauce and vinegar. Fresh out of the pan, the pancakes smell wonderful, crispy outside and tender inside—one bite and you'll never forget them.

column1: 如今，美食家们对吃提出了更高的要求。他们不仅要观色、闻香、尝味、赏形，而且还要求食物具有养生方面的特色。我想，家乡的萝卜饼完全具备这几个方面的条件，人们不是常说吗：“鱼生火，肉生病，青菜萝卜保平安”，养生的功能，让我更加喜爱它了。
column2: Rújīn, měishíjiāmen duì chī tíchū le gèng gāo de yāoqiú. Tāmen bùjǐn yào guān sè, wén xiāng, cháng wèi, shǎng xíng, érqiě hái yāoqiú shíwù jùyǒu yǎngshēng fāngmiàn de tèsè. Wǒ xiǎng, jiāxiāng de luóbobǐng wánquán jùbèi zhè jǐ ge fāngmiàn de tiáojiàn, rénmen bú shì cháng shuō ma: "Yú shēng huǒ, ròu shēng bìng, qīngcài luóbo bǎo píng'ān", yǎngshēng de gōngnéng, ràng wǒ gèngjiā xǐ'ài tā le.
column3: Nowadays, food lovers have higher demands when it comes to eating. They want not only to look at the color, smell the aroma, taste the flavor and admire the shape, but also for food to be good for health. I think my hometown's radish pancakes fully meet all these conditions. Don't people often say, "Fish causes internal heat, meat causes illness, but greens and radishes keep you safe and well"? Its health benefits make me love it even more.

column1: 小人书，是一种以书的形式出版的连环画。在二十世纪五六十年代，那时候生活很单调，没有网络，没有动画片，读小人书是儿童最主要的娱乐之一。不仅小孩子爱看，还有无数的青少年和大人也爱看。
column2: Xiǎorénshū, shì yì zhǒng yǐ shū de xíngshì chūbǎn de liánhuánhuà. Zài èrshí shìjì wǔ liùshí niándài, nà shíhou shēnghuó hěn dāndiào, méiyǒu wǎngluò, méiyǒu dònghuàpiàn, dú xiǎorénshū shì értóng zuì zhǔyào de yúlè zhī yī. Bùjǐn xiǎoháizi ài kàn, hái yǒu wúshù de qīngshàonián hé dàren yě ài kàn.
column3: Xiaorenshu (little picture books) are comic strips published in book form. In the 1950s and 1960s, life was monotonous—there was no internet and no cartoons—and reading these picture books was one of children's main forms of entertainment. Not only children loved them; countless teenagers and adults did too.

column1: 随着小人书的流行，出现了从事租书业务的小人书摊，这对于那些想看又买不起书的人来说，只用很少的钱就能看一本，毫无疑问是件大好事。
column2: Suízhe xiǎorénshū de liúxíng, chūxiàn le cóngshì zū shū yèwù de xiǎorénshū tān, zhè duìyú nàxiē xiǎng kàn yòu mǎi bu qǐ shū de rén lái shuō, zhǐ yòng hěn shǎo de qián jiù néng kàn yì běn, háowú yíwèn shì jiàn dà hǎoshì.
column3: As picture books became popular, picture-book stalls that rented out books appeared. For people who wanted to read but couldn't afford to buy books, being able to read one for very little money was without doubt a great thing.

column1: 记得小时候，我家附近就有个小人书摊，就是一进街口靠墙的一个小棚子，里面用几块砖头支着粗糙的木头板子供人们坐着看书。棚子里有一张床板摆着各种题材的小人书，墙边还拉了几根绳子，一本本书翻开搭在上面，五颜六色的，很好看。为了减少损坏程度，每本小人书都用牛皮纸加了层封皮，封皮上用毛笔写上书名，整齐漂亮的毛笔字能充分地显示出书摊主人的文化水平。摊主是位上了年纪、身材瘦小的老人，总是穿着一件灰色长衫，静静地坐在一边，陪着看书的人们。
column2: Jìde xiǎoshíhou, wǒ jiā fùjìn jiù yǒu ge xiǎorénshū tān, jiù shì yí jìn jiēkǒu kào qiáng de yí ge xiǎo péngzi, lǐmiàn yòng jǐ kuài zhuāntou zhīzhe cūcāo de mùtou bǎnzi gōng rénmen zuòzhe kàn shū. Péngzi li yǒu yì zhāng chuángbǎn bǎizhe gè zhǒng tícái de xiǎorénshū, qiáng biān hái lā le jǐ gēn shéngzi, yì běnběn shū fānkāi dā zài shàngmiàn, wǔyán liùsè de, hěn hǎokàn. Wèile jiǎnshǎo sǔnhuài chéngdù, měi běn xiǎorénshū dōu yòng niúpízhǐ jiā le céng fēngpí, fēngpí shang yòng máobǐ xiě shang shūmíng, zhěngqí piàoliang de máobǐzì néng chōngfèn de xiǎnshì chū shūtān zhǔrén de wénhuà shuǐpíng. Tānzhǔ shì wèi shàng le niánji, shēncái shòuxiǎo de lǎorén, zǒngshì chuānzhe yí jiàn huīsè chángshān, jìngjìng de zuò zài yìbiān, péizhe kàn shū de rénmen.
column3: I remember that when I was little there was a picture-book stall near my home: a small shed against the wall just inside the entrance to the street, where a few bricks propped up rough wooden boards for people to sit on while reading. Inside the shed, a bed board displayed picture books on all kinds of subjects, and several ropes were strung along the wall with books hung open over them, colorful and lovely to look at. To reduce wear and tear, each book had an extra cover of brown kraft paper with the title written on it in brush calligraphy; the neat, beautiful brushwork showed just how cultured the stall owner was. The owner was a small, thin old man who always wore a long gray gown and sat quietly to one side, keeping the readers company.

column1: 在这里看书的人大部分是附近住户的孩子，也有一些喜欢小人书的成人。租借小人书很便宜，在摊里看，每册1分钱，选好书坐下就看，看完连书带钱交给摊主；假如借走回家看，则每本每天2分钱，挑好书后交给摊主，摊主仔细地将租书人的姓名、地址和所借小人书的书名登记在本子上，收了租金就可以拿走了，第二天还书时再把记录一个一个地画掉，还书手续就算是办理好了。印象中似乎没有什么押金，全凭信用。我每天放学回家总要经过这家书摊，都要进去看看。
column2: Zài zhèli kàn shū de rén dà bùfen shì fùjìn zhùhù de háizi, yě yǒu yìxiē xǐhuan xiǎorénshū de chéngrén. Zūjiè xiǎorénshū hěn piányi, zài tān li kàn, měi cè yì fēn qián, xuǎnhǎo shū zuòxià jiù kàn, kànwán lián shū dài qián jiāo gěi tānzhǔ; jiǎrú jièzǒu huí jiā kàn, zé měi běn měitiān liǎng fēn qián, tiāohǎo shū hòu jiāo gěi tānzhǔ, tānzhǔ zǐxì de jiāng zū shū rén de xìngmíng, dìzhǐ hé suǒ jiè xiǎorénshū de shūmíng dēngjì zài běnzi shang, shōu le zūjīn jiù kěyǐ názǒu le, dì-èr tiān huán shū shí zài bǎ jìlù yí ge yí ge de huàdiào, huán shū shǒuxù jiù suànshì bànlǐ hǎo le. Yìnxiàng zhōng sìhū méiyǒu shénme yājīn, quán píng xìnyòng. Wǒ měitiān fàngxué huí jiā zǒng yào jīngguò zhè jiā shūtān, dōu yào jìnqu kànkan.
column3: Most of the readers here were children from nearby households, along with some adults who liked picture books. Renting them was cheap: reading at the stall cost one fen per book—you picked a book, sat down and read, and when you finished you handed the book and the money to the owner. If you borrowed one to read at home, it was two fen per book per day: you chose your books and gave them to the owner, who carefully recorded the borrower's name, address and the titles in a notebook; once you paid the rent you could take them away. When you returned the books the next day, he crossed out the records one by one, and the return was complete. As I recall there was no deposit at all—it was all based on trust. Every day on my way home from school I passed this stall, and I always went in to have a look.

column1: 然而，这种影响了数代人的小人书，如今只能在北京的潘家园、护国寺等地的旧书摊上找到，一些印刷精美、有特色的作品则身价大涨，成了收藏品，甚至进了博物馆。小人书和小人书摊已成为历史的记忆。
column2: Rán'ér, zhè zhǒng yǐngxiǎng le shù dài rén de xiǎorénshū, rújīn zhǐ néng zài Běijīng de Pānjiāyuán, Hùguósì děng dì de jiù shūtān shang zhǎodào, yìxiē yìnshuā jīngměi, yǒu tèsè de zuòpǐn zé shēnjià dà zhǎng, chéng le shōucángpǐn, shènzhì jìn le bówùguǎn. Xiǎorénshū hé xiǎorénshū tān yǐ chéngwéi lìshǐ de jìyì.
column3: However, these picture books that influenced several generations can now only be found at secondhand book stalls in places like Panjiayuan and Huguosi in Beijing. Some finely printed, distinctive ones have soared in value, becoming collectors' items and even ending up in museums. Picture books and picture-book stalls have become a memory of history.

column1: 1972年，22岁的理查德·希尔斯爱上了中文，但是他感觉汉字很复杂，汉字的一笔一画没有任何逻辑，只能死记硬背。一个偶然的机会，他发现如果了解汉字的来源和演变过程，再学习它就变得轻松、容易。但是他遗憾地发现，几乎没有一本英文书能充分解释汉字的字源。
column2: Yī jiǔ qī èr nián, èrshí'èr suì de Lǐchádé Xī'ěrsī àishang le Zhōngwén, dànshì tā gǎnjué Hànzì hěn fùzá, Hànzì de yì bǐ yí huà méiyǒu rènhé luójí, zhǐ néng sǐjì yìngbèi. Yí ge ǒurán de jīhuì, tā fāxiàn rúguǒ liǎojiě Hànzì de láiyuán hé yǎnbiàn guòchéng, zài xuéxí tā jiù biàn de qīngsōng, róngyì. Dànshì tā yíhàn de fāxiàn, jīhū méiyǒu yì běn Yīngwén shū néng chōngfèn jiěshì Hànzì de zìyuán.
column3: In 1972, 22-year-old Richard Sears fell in love with Chinese, but he felt Chinese characters were very complicated—their strokes seemed to follow no logic at all, and he could only memorize them by rote. By chance, he discovered that if he understood the origins and evolution of characters, learning them became easy and relaxed. But to his regret, he found that there was almost no English book that fully explained the origins of Chinese characters.

column1: 1994年，理查德得了心脏病，当时医生说他剩下的时间可能不多了。那时，他开始思考自己的人生：“我该怎么办？我该做什么？”“如果只能活24小时，我会打电话和朋友们说再见；如果我还能活一年，我要抓紧时间尽快把《说文解字》电脑化。”就这样，一部部古汉字经典进入他的资料库，仅仅复印、人工整理和把这些资料输入电脑就用了8年。2002年元旦，战胜疾病的他决定把自己创办的网站公开，让更多喜欢中文的人在学习汉字时，不再像他最初那样学得那么痛苦。
column2: Yī jiǔ jiǔ sì nián, Lǐchádé dé le xīnzàngbìng, dāngshí yīshēng shuō tā shèngxià de shíjiān kěnéng bù duō le. Nà shí, tā kāishǐ sīkǎo zìjǐ de rénshēng: "Wǒ gāi zěnme bàn? Wǒ gāi zuò shénme?" "Rúguǒ zhǐ néng huó èrshísì xiǎoshí, wǒ huì dǎ diànhuà hé péngyoumen shuō zàijiàn; rúguǒ wǒ hái néng huó yì nián, wǒ yào zhuājǐn shíjiān jǐnkuài bǎ "Shuōwén Jiězì" diànnǎohuà." Jiù zhèyàng, yí bùbù gǔ Hànzì jīngdiǎn jìnrù tā de zīliàokù, jǐnjǐn fùyìn, réngōng zhěnglǐ hé bǎ zhèxiē zīliào shūrù diànnǎo jiù yòng le bā nián. Èr líng líng èr nián Yuándàn, zhànshèng jíbìng de tā juédìng bǎ zìjǐ chuàngbàn de wǎngzhàn gōngkāi, ràng gèng duō xǐhuan Zhōngwén de rén zài xuéxí Hànzì shí, bú zài xiàng tā zuìchū nàyàng xué de nàme tòngkǔ.
column3: In 1994, Richard developed heart disease, and his doctor said he might not have much time left. He began to reflect on his life: "What should I do? What should I be doing?" "If I only had 24 hours to live, I'd call my friends to say goodbye; if I still had a year, I'd hurry to computerize the Shuowen Jiezi as quickly as possible." And so, one classic of ancient Chinese characters after another went into his database; just photocopying, sorting by hand and entering the material into the computer took eight years. On New Year's Day 2002, having beaten his illness, he decided to make the website he had created public, so that more people who love Chinese wouldn't have to suffer the way he did at first when learning characters.

column1: 2011年，有人把他的故事放到微博上，引起了广泛关注，他也因此被网友亲切地称呼为“汉字叔叔”。
column2: Èr líng yī yī nián, yǒu rén bǎ tā de gùshi fàngdào Wēibó shang, yǐnqǐ le guǎngfàn guānzhù, tā yě yīncǐ bèi wǎngyǒu qīnqiè de chēnghu wéi "Hànzì shūshu".
column3: In 2011, someone posted his story on Weibo, where it attracted wide attention, and netizens affectionately nicknamed him "Uncle Hanzi" (Uncle Chinese Characters).

column1: 打开汉字叔叔克服种种困难、花光全部积蓄创办的网站，可以看到他收集整理的近10万个汉字，包含了它们演变的全部字形，当然也包括繁体字形和简体字形，还有普通话和部分方言读音、英文释义等内容，被网友称赞为“有图有真相”。更让人佩服的是，汉字叔叔将网站上的内容全部开放给网友免费下载。
column2: Dǎkāi Hànzì shūshu kèfú zhǒngzhǒng kùnnan, huāguāng quánbù jīxù chuàngbàn de wǎngzhàn, kěyǐ kàndào tā shōují zhěnglǐ de jìn shí wàn ge Hànzì, bāohán le tāmen yǎnbiàn de quánbù zìxíng, dāngrán yě bāokuò fántǐ zìxíng hé jiǎntǐ zìxíng, hái yǒu pǔtōnghuà hé bùfen fāngyán dúyīn, Yīngwén shìyì děng nèiróng, bèi wǎngyǒu chēngzàn wéi "yǒu tú yǒu zhēnxiàng". Gèng ràng rén pèifu de shì, Hànzì shūshu jiāng wǎngzhàn shang de nèiróng quánbù kāifàng gěi wǎngyǒu miǎnfèi xiàzài.
column3: Open the website that Uncle Hanzi created after overcoming all kinds of difficulties and spending all his savings, and you can see nearly 100,000 Chinese characters he collected and organized, including every form they took as they evolved—traditional and simplified forms of course—along with Mandarin and some dialect pronunciations, English definitions and more. Netizens praised it as "pictures as proof." Even more admirable, Uncle Hanzi made all the content on the site free for netizens to download.

column1: 现在，有很多单位向理查德发出了工作邀请，而理查德选择了去北京师范大学教书，因为那里也有人在做汉字识别查询的研究。在北师大，他除了教物理，还有充分的时间继续研究他的汉字，完善他的网站。
column2: Xiànzài, yǒu hěn duō dānwèi xiàng Lǐchádé fāchū le gōngzuò yāoqǐng, ér Lǐchádé xuǎnzé le qù Běijīng Shīfàn Dàxué jiāoshū, yīnwèi nàli yě yǒu rén zài zuò Hànzì shíbié cháxún de yánjiū. Zài Běishīdà, tā chúle jiāo wùlǐ, hái yǒu chōngfèn de shíjiān jìxù yánjiū tā de Hànzì, wánshàn tā de wǎngzhàn.
column3: Now many organizations have offered Richard jobs, and he chose to teach at Beijing Normal University, because people there are also doing research on Chinese character recognition and lookup. At BNU, besides teaching physics, he has plenty of time to continue studying his characters and improving his website.

column1: 在中国，60多岁已经是退休的年纪了。但汉字叔叔每天的日程却安排得很满。他说：“我不会退休，我还要继续追求我的梦想，我要‘活到老，学到老’。”
column2: Zài Zhōngguó, liùshí duō suì yǐjīng shì tuìxiū de niánjì le. Dàn Hànzì shūshu měitiān de rìchéng què ānpái de hěn mǎn. Tā shuō: "Wǒ bú huì tuìxiū, wǒ hái yào jìxù zhuīqiú wǒ de mèngxiǎng, wǒ yào 'huó dào lǎo, xué dào lǎo'."
column3: In China, being over sixty is already retirement age. But Uncle Hanzi's daily schedule is packed. He says, "I won't retire. I'm going to keep pursuing my dream—I want to 'keep learning as long as I live.'"

column1: 很多家长可能过分强调阅读的作用，觉得多读书就能够把作文写得特别好。这个观点是不客观、不全面的，我们需要转变自己的观念。
column2: Hěn duō jiāzhǎng kěnéng guòfèn qiángdiào yuèdú de zuòyòng, juéde duō dú shū jiù nénggòu bǎ zuòwén xiě de tèbié hǎo. Zhège guāndiǎn shì bú kèguān, bù quánmiàn de, wǒmen xūyào zhuǎnbiàn zìjǐ de guānniàn.
column3: Many parents may overemphasize the role of reading, believing that reading a lot will make their children write especially good compositions. This view is neither objective nor complete, and we need to change our thinking.

column1: 我曾经听一位美国的小学老师说，他们十分重视和学生一起讨论问题。比如，他们讨论过《卖火柴的小女孩儿》是写给谁看的，还讨论过灰姑娘的故事。老师讲完故事之后，问同学们：灰姑娘一旦进了这个王宫，成为王子的心上人，她的梦想实现了，一切幸福都属于她之后，这时她应该怎样对待她的继母，应该怎样对待她的两个姐姐？
column2: Wǒ céngjīng tīng yí wèi Měiguó de xiǎoxué lǎoshī shuō, tāmen shífēn zhòngshì hé xuésheng yìqǐ tǎolùn wèntí. Bǐrú, tāmen tǎolùnguo "Mài Huǒchái de Xiǎo Nǚháir" shì xiě gěi shéi kàn de, hái tǎolùnguo Huīgūniang de gùshi. Lǎoshī jiǎngwán gùshi zhīhòu, wèn tóngxuémen: Huīgūniang yídàn jìn le zhège wánggōng, chéngwéi wángzǐ de xīnshàngrén, tā de mèngxiǎng shíxiàn le, yíqiè xìngfú dōu shǔyú tā zhīhòu, zhè shí tā yīnggāi zěnyàng duìdài tā de jìmǔ, yīnggāi zěnyàng duìdài tā de liǎng ge jiějie?
column3: I once heard an American elementary school teacher say that they place great importance on discussing questions together with students. For example, they discussed who "The Little Match Girl" was written for, and they also discussed the story of Cinderella. After telling the story, the teacher asked the class: once Cinderella has entered the palace and become the prince's beloved, and her dream has come true and all happiness is hers, how should she treat her stepmother, and how should she treat her two stepsisters?

column1: 为什么要讨论这个问题呢？因为这是一种情感教育。老师和学生通过讨论得出的结论是：一个已经拥有巨大幸福的人，应该原谅和理解那些伤害过自己的人。另外还要承认人性中一些先天的不完美，就是说作为一个母亲，在自己的亲生女儿和不是亲生的灰姑娘之间，难免会更疼爱自己亲生的女儿，很难完全平等地对待她们。可能你觉得继母很自私，但这种行为有自然倾向的理由，与道德没有必然的关系。
column2: Wèishénme yào tǎolùn zhège wèntí ne? Yīnwèi zhè shì yì zhǒng qínggǎn jiàoyù. Lǎoshī hé xuésheng tōngguò tǎolùn déchū de jiélùn shì: yí ge yǐjīng yōngyǒu jùdà xìngfú de rén, yīnggāi yuánliàng hé lǐjiě nàxiē shānghàiguo zìjǐ de rén. Lìngwài hái yào chéngrèn rénxìng zhōng yìxiē xiāntiān de bù wánměi, jiùshì shuō zuòwéi yí ge mǔqīn, zài zìjǐ de qīnshēng nǚ'ér hé bú shì qīnshēng de Huīgūniang zhījiān, nánmiǎn huì gèng téng'ài zìjǐ qīnshēng de nǚ'ér, hěn nán wánquán píngděng de duìdài tāmen. Kěnéng nǐ juéde jìmǔ hěn zìsī, dàn zhè zhǒng xíngwéi yǒu zìrán qīngxiàng de lǐyóu, yǔ dàodé méiyǒu bìrán de guānxi.
column3: Why discuss this question? Because it is a kind of emotional education. The conclusion the teacher and students reached through discussion was that a person who already has great happiness should forgive and understand those who have hurt them. They should also acknowledge some innate imperfections in human nature: as a mother, between her own daughter and Cinderella, who is not her own child, it is hard not to love her own daughter more, and hard to treat them completely equally. You may think the stepmother is selfish, but this behavior has a reason in natural inclination and is not necessarily a matter of morality.

column1: 自从我听说了这件事，就开始思考应该如何阅读，除了阅读还应该做什么。你看这个老师在讲童话的时候，已经在有意识地把这种情感影响，甚至把人性的价值判断，都给了孩子们。如果只是单纯地主张阅读而不强调思考，那是片面的。
column2: Zìcóng wǒ tīngshuō le zhè jiàn shì, jiù kāishǐ sīkǎo yīnggāi rúhé yuèdú, chúle yuèdú hái yīnggāi zuò shénme. Nǐ kàn zhège lǎoshī zài jiǎng tónghuà de shíhou, yǐjīng zài yǒu yìshí de bǎ zhè zhǒng qínggǎn yǐngxiǎng, shènzhì bǎ rénxìng de jiàzhí pànduàn, dōu gěi le háizimen. Rúguǒ zhǐshì dānchún de zhǔzhāng yuèdú ér bù qiángdiào sīkǎo, nà shì piànmiàn de.
column3: Ever since I heard about this, I've been thinking about how one should read and what else one should do besides reading. You see, when this teacher told a fairy tale, he was already consciously passing on this emotional influence—and even value judgments about human nature—to the children. Simply advocating reading without stressing thinking is one-sided.

column1: “知识”两个字我始终认为它要分开来谈的。“知”就是知晓，“识”就是认识。所谓“知晓”就是别人告诉你、说给你听、要求你记住的那一部分。但只有这一部分是不够的，还要有认识、思考。
column2: Zhīshi liǎng ge zì wǒ shǐzhōng rènwéi tā yào fēnkāi lái tán de. "Zhī" jiù shì zhīxiǎo, "shí" jiù shì rènshi. Suǒwèi "zhīxiǎo" jiù shì biéren gàosu nǐ, shuō gěi nǐ tīng, yāoqiú nǐ jìzhù de nà yí bùfen. Dàn zhǐyǒu zhè yí bùfen shì búgòu de, hái yào yǒu rènshi, sīkǎo.
column3: I've always believed that the two characters of "zhishi" (knowledge) should be discussed separately. "Zhi" means knowing about something, and "shi" means understanding it. "Knowing" is the part that others tell you, explain to you and ask you to remember. But that part alone is not enough; you also need understanding and thinking.

column1: 文文从小是个乖乖女，学习刻苦，遵守纪律。大事小事，尽管妈妈表示也要征求她的意见，但上哪所学校、念什么专业，甚至跟什么人交朋友，基本上都是妈妈说了算。
column2: Wénwen cóngxiǎo shì ge guāiguāinǚ, xuéxí kèkǔ, zūnshǒu jìlǜ. Dàshì xiǎoshì, jǐnguǎn māma biǎoshì yě yào zhēngqiú tā de yìjiàn, dàn shàng nǎ suǒ xuéxiào, niàn shénme zhuānyè, shènzhì gēn shénme rén jiāo péngyou, jīběn shang dōu shì māma shuō le suàn.
column3: Wenwen had been a good, obedient girl since childhood—hardworking at school and well-disciplined. In matters big and small, although her mother said she would also ask for her opinion, which school to attend, what to major in, and even whom to be friends with were basically all her mother's decision.

column1: 可是到了大学阶段，亲爱的女儿竟然违反了乖乖女的各种规矩，越来越有自己的主见，越来越能干、独立了。尽管她的成绩仍然是第一名，但她不再甘于当“好学生”：她逃课去听各种讲座，出席欧盟商会的鸡尾酒会，做志愿者，拍电影，学摄影，泡酒吧，参加了学生会并担任了学生会主席，还组织各种社会活动。妈妈以前要她当外交官的计划，在她眼里“实在没什么意思”，她觉得经商才是自己的目标。
column2: Kěshì dào le dàxué jiēduàn, qīn'ài de nǚ'ér jìngrán wéifǎn le guāiguāinǚ de gè zhǒng guīju, yuèláiyuè yǒu zìjǐ de zhǔjiàn, yuèláiyuè nénggàn, dúlì le. Jǐnguǎn tā de chéngjì réngrán shì dì-yī míng, dàn tā bú zài gānyú dāng "hǎo xuésheng": tā táokè qù tīng gè zhǒng jiǎngzuò, chūxí Ōuméng Shānghuì de jīwěijiǔ huì, zuò zhìyuànzhě, pāi diànyǐng, xué shèyǐng, pào jiǔbā, cānjiā le xuéshēnghuì bìng dānrèn le xuéshēnghuì zhǔxí, hái zǔzhī gè zhǒng shèhuì huódòng. Māma yǐqián yào tā dāng wàijiāoguān de jìhuà, zài tā yǎn li "shízài méi shénme yìsi", tā juéde jīngshāng cái shì zìjǐ de mùbiāo.
column3: But in college, her dear daughter unexpectedly broke all the rules of the good girl, growing more and more opinionated, capable and independent. Although she was still first in her class, she was no longer content to be a "good student": she skipped classes to attend all kinds of lectures, went to cocktail parties held by the EU Chamber of Commerce, volunteered, made films, learned photography, hung out in bars, joined the student union and became its president, and organized all sorts of social activities. Her mother's earlier plan for her to become a diplomat seemed to her "really pointless"; she felt that business was her true goal.

column1: 她放弃了本系保送研究生、放弃了各种工作的面试，坚持要去国外留学，结果12所世界名牌大学录取了她。当面临是否选择牛津大学时，她们全家开会，爸爸妈妈认为应该去，但文文跟他们的意见不一致，她坚持要去美国。
column2: Tā fàngqì le běn xì bǎosòng yánjiūshēng, fàngqì le gè zhǒng gōngzuò de miànshì, jiānchí yào qù guówài liúxué, jiéguǒ shí'èr suǒ shìjiè míngpái dàxué lùqǔ le tā. Dāng miànlín shìfǒu xuǎnzé Niújīn Dàxué shí, tāmen quánjiā kāihuì, bàba māma rènwéi yīnggāi qù, dàn Wénwen gēn tāmen de yìjiàn bù yízhì, tā jiānchí yào qù Měiguó.
column3: She gave up a guaranteed place in her department's graduate program and all kinds of job interviews, insisting on studying abroad—and as a result she was accepted by 12 world-famous universities.
