column1: 我们每个人都有过粗心大意的时候，令人警觉的是，这也可能成为被伤害的原因。一次赛前热身，主办方特意做了警示牌，警告运动员不要在球门里训练，有位运动员一时疏忽正好踩在了警示牌上，由于重心不稳，以致扭伤了脚；还有位同样疏忽的运动员，在折叠熨衣板时肩膀受伤；某国国脚有一次不仅摔破了嘴唇，还磕掉了门牙，当时他仅仅是想从汽车里拽出高尔夫球具。
column2: Wǒmen měi ge rén dōu yǒu guo cūxīn dàyì de shíhou, lìng rén jǐngjué de shì, zhè yě kěnéng chéngwéi bèi shānghài de yuányīn. Yí cì sài qián rèshēn, zhǔbànfāng tèyì zuò le jǐngshìpái, jǐnggào yùndòngyuán búyào zài qiúmén li xùnliàn, yǒu wèi yùndòngyuán yìshí shūhu zhènghǎo cǎi zài le jǐngshìpái shang, yóuyú zhòngxīn bù wěn, yǐzhì niǔshāng le jiǎo; hái yǒu wèi tóngyàng shūhu de yùndòngyuán, zài zhédié yùnyībǎn shí jiānbǎng shòushāng; mǒu guó guójiǎo yǒu yí cì bùjǐn shuāipò le zuǐchún, hái kēdiào le ményá, dāngshí tā jǐnjǐn shì xiǎng cóng qìchē li zhuài chū gāo'ěrfū qiújù.
column3: All of us have been careless at times, and what should put us on guard is that this too can be a cause of injury. During one pre-match warm-up, the organizers made a warning sign specifically telling athletes not to train in the goal; one athlete, in a moment of carelessness, stepped right on the sign, lost his balance and sprained his foot. Another equally careless athlete hurt his shoulder while folding an ironing board. And one national-team player not only split his lip but also knocked out a front tooth—when all he was trying to do was pull his golf clubs out of the car.

column1: 汉语有个词叫乐极生悲，说的就应该是下面这位球员：在打进一球后，他冲入观众席和球迷一起庆祝，结果结婚戒指连同他的手指一起挂在了围栏上，手指受重伤。更让他恼火的是，不了解情况的主裁判还给了他一张黄牌，真可谓雪上加霜。
column2: Hànyǔ yǒu ge cí jiào lèjí shēngbēi, shuō de jiù yīnggāi shì xiàmiàn zhè wèi qiúyuán: zài dǎjìn yì qiú hòu, tā chōngrù guānzhòngxí hé qiúmí yìqǐ qìngzhù, jiéguǒ jiéhūn jièzhi liántóng tā de shǒuzhǐ yìqǐ guà zài le wéilán shang, shǒuzhǐ shòu zhòngshāng. Gèng ràng tā nǎohuǒ de shì, bù liǎojiě qíngkuàng de zhǔcáipàn hái gěi le tā yì zhāng huángpái, zhēn kěwèi xuěshàng jiāshuāng.
column3: Chinese has an expression, "extreme joy turns to sorrow", which must describe the following player: after scoring a goal, he rushed into the stands to celebrate with the fans, and his wedding ring, together with his finger, got caught on the railing, seriously injuring the finger. Even more infuriating for him, the referee, who didn't know what had happened, also gave him a yellow card—truly adding insult to injury.

column1: 最荒唐的受伤当属某国国脚。他的脚指甲旁边长了个血泡，他决定自己处置。各种工具他都看不上，最后选中的竟然是电钻，由于用力过猛，把脚弄破了，以致感染，遭受了难以想象的痛苦。看来医生也不是谁想当就能当的，虽然在真正的医生眼里这只是个微不足道的小手术。
column2: Zuì huāngtáng de shòushāng dāng shǔ mǒu guó guójiǎo. Tā de jiǎozhǐjia pángbiān zhǎng le ge xuèpào, tā juédìng zìjǐ chǔzhì. Gè zhǒng gōngjù tā dōu kàn bu shàng, zuìhòu xuǎnzhòng de jìngrán shì diànzuàn, yóuyú yònglì guò měng, bǎ jiǎo nòngpò le, yǐzhì gǎnrǎn, zāoshòu le nányǐ xiǎngxiàng de tòngkǔ. Kànlái yīshēng yě bú shì shéi xiǎng dāng jiù néng dāng de, suīrán zài zhēnzhèng de yīshēng yǎn li zhè zhǐ shì ge wēibùzúdào de xiǎo shǒushù.
column3: The most absurd injury has to belong to a certain national-team player. A blood blister formed next to his toenail, and he decided to deal with it himself. He didn't think much of any of the usual tools, and in the end what he chose was—an electric drill. Because he pushed too hard, he wounded his foot, which became infected, and he suffered unimaginable pain. It seems not just anyone can be a doctor, even though in a real doctor's eyes this is only a trivial minor operation.

column1: 其实离奇伤害不仅存在于运动员当中，它也紧紧跟随着我们每一个人，只要你疏忽、大意。
column2: Qíshí líqí shānghài bùjǐn cúnzài yú yùndòngyuán dāngzhōng, tā yě jǐnjǐn gēnsuízhe wǒmen měi yí ge rén, zhǐyào nǐ shūhu, dàyì.
column3: In fact, bizarre injuries don't exist only among athletes; they follow every one of us closely, as long as we're careless and inattentive.

column1: 三国时期，东吴大将周瑜觉得自己很有才，却总比不过诸葛亮，心里一直不服气。一天，周瑜请来了诸葛亮，说：“我们就要跟曹操的军队打仗了。水上作战，用什么武器最好？”诸葛亮说：“弓箭。”周瑜说：“这话不假。可现在我们缺箭，当务之急是赶造十万支箭，造箭的事就由您承办吧。”诸葛亮说：“您委托的事，当然要办好。箭什么时候用？”周瑜说：“即将交战，十天怎么样？”诸葛亮说：“时间紧迫，三天也行。”周瑜说：“这是公务，可不能开玩笑。”诸葛亮说：“三天造不好箭，愿受惩罚。”周瑜很高兴，设宴款待诸葛亮。诸葛亮临走时叮嘱周瑜：“三天以后，请派人到江边来搬箭。”
column2: Sānguó shíqī, Dōngwú dàjiàng Zhōu Yú juéde zìjǐ hěn yǒu cái, què zǒng bǐ bu guò Zhūgě Liàng, xīnli yìzhí bù fúqì. Yì tiān, Zhōu Yú qǐngláile Zhūgě Liàng, shuō: "Wǒmen jiù yào gēn Cáo Cāo de jūnduì dǎzhàng le. Shuǐ shang zuòzhàn, yòng shénme wǔqì zuì hǎo?" Zhūgě Liàng shuō: "Gōngjiàn." Zhōu Yú shuō: "Zhè huà bù jiǎ. Kě xiànzài wǒmen quē jiàn, dāngwù zhī jí shì gǎnzào shíwàn zhī jiàn, zào jiàn de shì jiù yóu nín chéngbàn ba." Zhūgě Liàng shuō: "Nín wěituō de shì, dāngrán yào bànhǎo. Jiàn shénme shíhou yòng?" Zhōu Yú shuō: "Jíjiāng jiāozhàn, shí tiān zěnmeyàng?" Zhūgě Liàng shuō: "Shíjiān jǐnpò, sān tiān yě xíng." Zhōu Yú shuō: "Zhè shì gōngwù, kě bù néng kāi wánxiào." Zhūgě Liàng shuō: "Sān tiān zào bu hǎo jiàn, yuàn shòu chéngfá." Zhōu Yú hěn gāoxìng, shè yàn kuǎndài Zhūgě Liàng. Zhūgě Liàng lín zǒu shí dīngzhǔ Zhōu Yú: "Sān tiān yǐhòu, qǐng pài rén dào jiāngbiān lái bān jiàn."
column3: During the Three Kingdoms period, Zhou Yu, a great general of Eastern Wu, thought himself very talented, yet he could never outdo Zhuge Liang, and he always resented it. One day Zhou Yu invited Zhuge Liang over and said, "We are about to go to war with Cao Cao's army. In a battle on the water, what weapon is best?" Zhuge Liang said, "Bows and arrows." Zhou Yu said, "That's true. But right now we are short of arrows; the most urgent task is to rush out a hundred thousand of them. I'll leave the making of the arrows to you." Zhuge Liang said, "Whatever you entrust to me, I will of course do well. When are the arrows needed?" Zhou Yu said, "Battle is imminent. How about ten days?" Zhuge Liang said, "Time is pressing. Three days will do." Zhou Yu said, "This is official business—no joking." Zhuge Liang said, "If I can't make the arrows in three days, I'm willing to be punished." Zhou Yu was delighted and held a banquet in Zhuge Liang's honor. As he was leaving, Zhuge Liang urged Zhou Yu: "In three days, please send men to the riverbank to carry the arrows away."

column1: 鲁肃对周瑜说：“十万支箭，三天怎么造得成？诸葛亮不会说话不算数吧？”周瑜说：“我又没有逼迫他，是他自己说的。我得吩咐下属，造箭用的材料，不要给他准备齐全，也不能供应充足，故意给他拖延时间。到期限造不出箭，他就活该受罚了。你去探听探听，他是怎么打算的，回来向我汇报。”
column2: Lǔ Sù duì Zhōu Yú shuō: "Shíwàn zhī jiàn, sān tiān zěnme zào de chéng? Zhūgě Liàng bú huì shuōhuà bú suànshù ba?" Zhōu Yú shuō: "Wǒ yòu méiyǒu bīpò tā, shì tā zìjǐ shuō de. Wǒ děi fēnfù xiàshǔ, zào jiàn yòng de cáiliào, bú yào gěi tā zhǔnbèi qíquán, yě bù néng gōngyìng chōngzú, gùyì gěi tā tuōyán shíjiān. Dào qīxiàn zào bu chū jiàn, tā jiù huógāi shòu fá le. Nǐ qù tàntīng tàntīng, tā shì zěnme dǎsuan de, huí lai xiàng wǒ huìbào."
column3: Lu Su said to Zhou Yu, "A hundred thousand arrows—how can they possibly be made in three days? Surely Zhuge Liang won't go back on his word?" Zhou Yu said, "It's not as if I forced him; he said it himself. I'll instruct my subordinates not to prepare all the materials he needs for the arrows, and not to supply enough of them either, deliberately wasting his time. When the deadline comes and he can't produce the arrows, he'll deserve his punishment. Go and find out what he's planning, then come back and report to me."

column1: 鲁肃去探望诸葛亮，见面寒暄过后，诸葛亮说：“三天，要十万支箭，你得帮帮我。”鲁肃说：“你不要为难我，我怎么帮得了你？”诸葛亮说：“你借给我二十条船，每条船上要三十名士兵。船用黑布遮挡严密，再把草捆成捆儿，共要一千个，排在船的侧面，我有用。不过这是机密，你得替我保密，不要走漏消息，否则我性命难保。”
column2: Lǔ Sù qù tànwàng Zhūgě Liàng, jiànmiàn hánxuān guòhòu, Zhūgě Liàng shuō: "Sān tiān, yào shíwàn zhī jiàn, nǐ děi bāngbang wǒ." Lǔ Sù shuō: "Nǐ bú yào wéinán wǒ, wǒ zěnme bāng de liǎo nǐ?" Zhūgě Liàng shuō: "Nǐ jiè gěi wǒ èrshí tiáo chuán, měi tiáo chuán shang yào sānshí míng shìbīng. Chuán yòng hēi bù zhēdǎng yánmì, zài bǎ cǎo kǔnchéng kǔnr, gòng yào yìqiān ge, pái zài chuán de cèmiàn, wǒ yǒu yòng. Búguò zhè shì jīmì, nǐ děi tì wǒ bǎomì, bú yào zǒulòu xiāoxi, fǒuzé wǒ xìngmìng nán bǎo."
column3: Lu Su went to visit Zhuge Liang. After they had exchanged greetings, Zhuge Liang said, "Three days for a hundred thousand arrows—you have to help me." Lu Su said, "Don't put me in a difficult position. How could I help you?" Zhuge Liang said, "Lend me twenty boats, with thirty soldiers on each. Cover the boats tightly with black cloth, and tie straw into bundles—a thousand in all—and line them up along the sides of the boats. I have a use for them. But this is a secret; you must keep it for me and not leak a word, or my life will be in danger."

column1: 鲁肃答应了，回来报告周瑜，果然没提借船的事，只说造箭的材料诸葛亮都不用。周瑜沉思良久，猜不出诸葛亮的意图，只好等着。
column2: Lǔ Sù dāying le, huí lai bàogào Zhōu Yú, guǒrán méi tí jiè chuán de shì, zhǐ shuō zào jiàn de cáiliào Zhūgě Liàng dōu bú yòng. Zhōu Yú chénsī liángjiǔ, cāi bu chū Zhūgě Liàng de yìtú, zhǐhǎo děngzhe.
column3: Lu Su agreed. When he went back to report to Zhou Yu, sure enough, he didn't mention borrowing the boats; he only said that Zhuge Liang wasn't using any of the materials for making arrows. Zhou Yu pondered for a long time but couldn't guess what Zhuge Liang intended, so he had no choice but to wait.

column1: 鲁肃私自弄来二十条快船，按诸葛亮说的安排妥当。头两天，诸葛亮那儿毫无动静，第三天过了午夜，诸葛亮把鲁肃请到船上，说：“和我一起去取箭。”之后只只用绳索把船连在一起，朝曹操占领的北岸开去。
column2: Lǔ Sù sīzì nònglái èrshí tiáo kuài chuán, àn Zhūgě Liàng shuō de ānpái tuǒdang. Tóu liǎng tiān, Zhūgě Liàng nàr háowú dòngjing, dì-sān tiān guòle wǔyè, Zhūgě Liàng bǎ Lǔ Sù qǐngdào chuán shang, shuō: "Hé wǒ yìqǐ qù qǔ jiàn." Zhīhòu zhīzhī yòng shéngsuǒ bǎ chuán lián zài yìqǐ, cháo Cáo Cāo zhànlǐng de běi'àn kāiqu.
column3: Lu Su privately got hold of twenty fast boats and arranged everything just as Zhuge Liang had said. For the first two days there was no sign of activity at all from Zhuge Liang. On the third day, after midnight, Zhuge Liang invited Lu Su onto a boat and said, "Come with me to fetch the arrows." Then the boats were tied together one by one with ropes and set off toward the north bank occupied by Cao Cao.

column1: 此时，大雾封锁了江面，不远处什么都看不清，船悄悄地靠近了曹操的驻扎地。士兵在诸葛亮指定的地点，将船头朝西，船尾朝东，一字摆开。船上的士兵奋力擂鼓，齐声高喊，声音能多响亮就多响亮。鲁肃吃惊地说：“曹兵出来怎么办？”诸葛亮笑答：“雾这么大，曹操不敢派兵出来。”鲁肃跟诸葛亮来到船上，看到舱中已摆下酒菜，只得心神不定地与诸葛亮饮酒。
column2: Cǐshí, dà wù fēngsuǒle jiāngmiàn, bù yuǎn chù shénme dōu kàn bu qīng, chuán qiāoqiāo de kàojìnle Cáo Cāo de zhùzhādì. Shìbīng zài Zhūgě Liàng zhǐdìng de dìdiǎn, jiāng chuántóu cháo xī, chuánwěi cháo dōng, yízì bǎikāi. Chuán shang de shìbīng fènlì léi gǔ, qíshēng gāo hǎn, shēngyīn néng duō xiǎngliàng jiù duō xiǎngliàng. Lǔ Sù chījīng de shuō: "Cáo bīng chūlai zěnme bàn?" Zhūgě Liàng xiào dá: "Wù zhème dà, Cáo Cāo bù gǎn pài bīng chūlai." Lǔ Sù gēn Zhūgě Liàng láidào chuán shang, kàndào cāng zhōng yǐ bǎixià jiǔcài, zhǐdé xīnshén búdìng de yǔ Zhūgě Liàng yǐn jiǔ.
column3: At that moment a heavy fog blanketed the river, and nothing could be seen even a short distance away. The boats quietly approached Cao Cao's encampment. At the spot Zhuge Liang had designated, the soldiers turned the boats bows to the west and sterns to the east and spread them out in a single line. The soldiers on board beat the drums with all their might and shouted in unison, as loudly as they possibly could. Lu Su said in alarm, "What if Cao's troops come out?" Zhuge Liang answered with a smile, "With fog this thick, Cao Cao won't dare send troops out." Lu Su followed Zhuge Liang into the boat and saw that wine and dishes had already been laid out in the cabin, so he had no choice but to drink with Zhuge Liang, ill at ease.

column1: 曹操听到鼓声和叫喊声响成一片，吩咐下属：“江上大雾茫茫，我们弄不清情况，不要轻易出兵。”于是，调动了上万名弓箭手一齐朝传来鼓声的方位放箭，箭像雨点一样落在船上。一会儿，诸葛亮下令把船掉过来，船头朝东，船尾朝西。士兵们情绪高涨，依旧擂鼓高喊，逼近曹军去受箭。
column2: Cáo Cāo tīngdào gǔshēng hé jiàohǎnshēng xiǎngchéng yí piàn, fēnfù xiàshǔ: "Jiāng shang dà wù mángmáng, wǒmen nòng bu qīng qíngkuàng, bú yào qīngyì chū bīng." Yúshì, diàodòngle shàng wàn míng gōngjiànshǒu yìqí cháo chuánlái gǔshēng de fāngwèi fàng jiàn, jiàn xiàng yǔdiǎn yíyàng luò zài chuán shang. Yíhuìr, Zhūgě Liàng xiàlìng bǎ chuán diào guolai, chuántóu cháo dōng, chuánwěi cháo xī. Shìbīngmen qíngxù gāozhǎng, yījiù léi gǔ gāo hǎn, bījìn Cáo jūn qù shòu jiàn.
column3: Hearing the drumbeats and shouting blend into one great din, Cao Cao instructed his subordinates: "The river is shrouded in thick fog and we can't make out what's going on. Don't send out troops rashly." So he mobilized more than ten thousand archers to shoot arrows all at once in the direction the drumming came from, and the arrows fell on the boats like raindrops. After a while, Zhuge Liang ordered the boats turned around, bows to the east and sterns to the west. The soldiers, in high spirits, kept beating the drums and shouting, closing in on Cao's army to take more arrows.

column1: 凌晨，雾还笼罩着江面，船两边的草捆儿上插满了箭。诸葛亮命令士兵启程返航。曹操知道上当了，可诸葛亮的船已经走远了。
column2: Língchén, wù hái lǒngzhàozhe jiāngmiàn, chuán liǎng biān de cǎokǔnr shang chāmǎnle jiàn. Zhūgě Liàng mìnglìng shìbīng qǐchéng fǎnháng. Cáo Cāo zhīdao shàngdàng le, kě Zhūgě Liàng de chuán yǐjīng zǒuyuǎn le.
column3: In the small hours of the morning, fog still hung over the river, and the straw bundles on both sides of the boats were stuck full of arrows. Zhuge Liang ordered the soldiers to set off on the return voyage. Cao Cao realized he had been tricked, but Zhuge Liang's boats were already far away.

column1: 二十条船靠岸的时候，周瑜派来搬箭的人也到了。大致算了算，船上的箭共有十万多支，诸葛亮圆满完成了任务。
column2: Èrshí tiáo chuán kào'àn de shíhou, Zhōu Yú pàilái bān jiàn de rén yě dào le. Dàzhì suànle suàn, chuán shang de jiàn gòng yǒu shíwàn duō zhī, Zhūgě Liàng yuánmǎn wánchéngle rènwu.
column3: When the twenty boats reached the shore, the men Zhou Yu had sent to carry the arrows arrived too. A rough count showed more than a hundred thousand arrows on the boats in all. Zhuge Liang had completed his task perfectly.

column1: 鲁肃见了周瑜，告诉他借箭的经过。周瑜叹着气说：“唉，他真是天才，确实比我高明！”
column2: Lǔ Sù jiànle Zhōu Yú, gàosu tā jiè jiàn de jīngguò. Zhōu Yú tànzhe qì shuō: "Ài, tā zhēn shì tiāncái, quèshí bǐ wǒ gāomíng!"
column3: Lu Su went to see Zhou Yu and told him how the arrows had been "borrowed." Zhou Yu sighed and said, "Ah, he truly is a genius—he really is cleverer than I am!"

column1: 传说古代有个爱书如命的读书人，每当他捧起书本就像是走进了知识的海洋，天文地理、儒家经典、传记散文、历代诗词，都会使他着迷。历史文化的长期熏陶，使他思维敏捷，胸怀宽广。冬季使人不堪忍受的严寒以及炎热夏天蚊子的骚扰都没有影响他读书的热情，唯独让他发愁的是家境贫寒，日子过得艰难，晚上看书别说蜡烛了，就是灯油也要节省着用。
column2: Chuánshuō gǔdài yǒu ge ài shū rú mìng de dúshūrén, měi dāng tā pěngqǐ shūběn jiù xiàng shì zǒujìnle zhīshi de hǎiyáng, tiānwén dìlǐ, Rújiā jīngdiǎn, zhuànjì sǎnwén, lìdài shīcí, dōu huì shǐ tā zháomí. Lìshǐ wénhuà de chángqī xūntáo, shǐ tā sīwéi mǐnjié, xiōnghuái kuānguǎng. Dōngjì shǐ rén bùkān rěnshòu de yánhán yǐjí yánrè xiàtiān wénzi de sāorǎo dōu méiyǒu yǐngxiǎng tā dúshū de rèqíng, wéidú ràng tā fāchóu de shì jiājìng pínhán, rìzi guò de jiānnán, wǎnshang kàn shū bié shuō làzhú le, jiùshì dēngyóu yě yào jiéshěngzhe yòng.
column3: Legend has it that in ancient times there was a scholar who loved books as much as life itself. Whenever he picked up a book, it was as if he had walked into an ocean of knowledge: astronomy and geography, the Confucian classics, biographies and prose, poetry from every dynasty—all of it held him spellbound. Long immersion in history and culture made his mind quick and his heart broad. Neither the unbearable cold of winter nor the harassment of mosquitoes in the hot summer dampened his passion for reading. The only thing that troubled him was that his family was poor and life was hard; to read at night, never mind candles, he had to be sparing even with lamp oil.

column1: 又是一个闷热的夏夜，窗外阵阵热浪袭来，汗珠顺着脸往下流，脸上痒痒的，像有蚂蚁在爬，他用手擦了擦汗，依然沉醉在书本里。由于坐得太久，他的颈椎有些麻木，屁股酸痛，他晃了晃头，用手揉了揉麻木的脖子，挪了挪屁股，换个姿势，顿时麻木的部位恢复了知觉，他依旧沉浸在读书的快乐中。是啊，只要有书读，挨饿受冻他都不怕；只要有书陪伴，他就感觉幸福、美满，像是生活在天堂。
column2: Yòu shì yí ge mēnrè de xià yè, chuāng wài zhènzhèn rèlàng xílái, hànzhū shùnzhe liǎn wǎng xià liú, liǎn shang yǎngyang de, xiàng yǒu mǎyǐ zài pá, tā yòng shǒu cāle cā hàn, yīrán chénzuì zài shūběn li. Yóuyú zuò de tài jiǔ, tā de jǐngzhuī yǒuxiē mámù, pìgu suāntòng, tā huàngle huàng tóu, yòng shǒu róule róu mámù de bózi, nuóle nuó pìgu, huàn ge zīshì, dùnshí mámù de bùwèi huīfùle zhījué, tā yījiù chénjìn zài dúshū de kuàilè zhōng. Shì a, zhǐyào yǒu shū dú, ái'è shòudòng tā dōu bú pà; zhǐyào yǒu shū péibàn, tā jiù gǎnjué xìngfú, měimǎn, xiàng shì shēnghuó zài tiāntáng.
column3: It was another sultry summer night. Waves of heat rolled in from outside the window, and beads of sweat ran down his face; his face itched as if ants were crawling on it. He wiped the sweat away with his hand and stayed absorbed in his book. Because he had been sitting so long, his neck had gone a bit numb and his backside ached. He shook his head, rubbed his numb neck, and shifted in his seat to change position; at once feeling returned to the numb spots, and he went on immersed in the joy of reading. Indeed, as long as he had books to read, he feared neither hunger nor cold; as long as he had books for company, he felt happy and content, as if living in paradise.

column1: 忽然，油灯无力地跳了两下，无声地熄灭了，眼前顿时陷入了黑暗。糟了，一定是灯油没有了，他有些泄气。黑暗中他瞪起双眼，极力使自己尽快适应眼前的黑暗。他拿起油灯在耳边摇了摇，灯油瓶空了。他放下灯，绝望地凝视着眼前的茫茫黑暗，不知道怎样打发这个漫漫长夜。
column2: Hūrán, yóudēng wúlì de tiàole liǎng xià, wúshēng de xīmiè le, yǎnqián dùnshí xiànrùle hēi'àn. Zāo le, yídìng shì dēngyóu méiyǒu le, tā yǒuxiē xièqì. Hēi'àn zhōng tā dèngqǐ shuāngyǎn, jílì shǐ zìjǐ jǐnkuài shìyìng yǎnqián de hēi'àn. Tā náqǐ yóudēng zài ěrbiān yáole yáo, dēngyóupíng kōng le. Tā fàngxià dēng, juéwàng de níngshìzhe yǎnqián de mángmáng hēi'àn, bù zhīdào zěnyàng dǎfa zhège mànmàn chángyè.
column3: Suddenly the oil lamp flickered feebly twice and went out without a sound, and everything before him was plunged into darkness. Oh no—the lamp oil must have run out. He felt a little deflated. In the dark he opened his eyes wide, trying hard to get used to the darkness as quickly as possible. He picked up the oil lamp and shook it beside his ear: the oil bottle was empty. He put down the lamp and stared in despair at the vast darkness before him, not knowing how to while away this long, endless night.

column1: 屋子里闷热的空气像是凝固了，烦躁在他身体中蔓延开来，他努力克制着自己的情绪，默默地背诵着刚刚读过的古诗，在头脑中编织着诗中描绘的动人画面，可这种强制的办法没有效果，于是，他打开房门走入了沉沉夜色。
column2: Wūzi li mēnrè de kōngqì xiàng shì nínggù le, fánzào zài tā shēntǐ zhōng mànyán kāilai, tā nǔlì kèzhìzhe zìjǐ de qíngxù, mòmò de bèisòngzhe gānggāng dúguo de gǔshī, zài tóunǎo zhōng biānzhīzhe shī zhōng miáohuì de dòngrén huàmiàn, kě zhè zhǒng qiángzhì de bànfǎ méiyǒu xiàoguǒ, yúshì, tā dǎkāi fángmén zǒurùle chénchén yèsè.
column3: The stuffy air in the room seemed to have congealed, and restlessness spread through his body. He tried hard to keep his emotions in check, silently reciting the ancient poems he had just read and weaving in his mind the moving scenes they described. But this forced method didn't work, so he opened the door and walked out into the deep night.

column1: 夏日的夜十分美丽，一闪一闪的星星镶嵌在夜空中，偶尔还会吹来一阵凉风。他漫步在田野中，欣赏着美丽的夜景，忽然他被眼前的情形吸引住了，只见一大群萤火虫在低空盘旋飞舞，来来回回地飞。萤火虫的尾巴都有亮光在闪烁，成为黑暗中唯一耀眼的光芒。
column2: Xiàrì de yè shífēn měilì, yì shǎn yì shǎn de xīngxing xiāngqiàn zài yèkōng zhōng, ǒu'ěr hái huì chuīlái yí zhèn liángfēng. Tā mànbù zài tiányě zhōng, xīnshǎngzhe měilì de yèjǐng, hūrán tā bèi yǎnqián de qíngxíng xīyǐn zhù le, zhǐ jiàn yí dà qún yínghuǒchóng zài dīkōng pánxuán fēiwǔ, láilái huíhuí de fēi. Yínghuǒchóng de wěiba dōu yǒu liàngguāng zài shǎnshuò, chéngwéi hēi'àn zhōng wéiyī yàoyǎn de guāngmáng.
column3: Summer nights are beautiful. Twinkling stars were set in the night sky, and every now and then a cool breeze blew by. He strolled through the fields, enjoying the lovely night scene, when suddenly his attention was caught by the sight before him: a large swarm of fireflies was circling and dancing low in the air, flying back and forth. Light flickered on each firefly's tail, the only dazzling glow in the darkness.

column1: 他跟在萤火虫后面。忽然一只萤火虫飞到了眼前，他伸手一捞，把它握在了手心，摊开手掌，哇，萤火虫还老老实实地待在那里，尾部依旧闪着亮光，也许那亮光只能用毫米计算，可却还算明亮。瞬间，他头脑中迸发出一个想法：“如果将许多萤火虫集中在一起，不就成灯了吗？”他决定试一试。他找了个薄布做的布囊，抓了一些萤火虫放在里面，然后将袋口扎住，把口袋吊起来，一个“灯笼”就做成啦，虽然没有油灯亮，看书还是勉强可以的，从此，萤火虫做成的“灯”就夜夜陪伴着他。
column2: Tā gēn zài yínghuǒchóng hòumiàn. Hūrán yì zhī yínghuǒchóng fēidàole yǎnqián, tā shēn shǒu yì lāo, bǎ tā wò zài le shǒuxīn, tānkāi shǒuzhǎng, wa, yínghuǒchóng hái lǎolǎoshíshí de dāi zài nàli, wěibù yījiù shǎnzhe liàngguāng, yěxǔ nà liàngguāng zhǐ néng yòng háomǐ jìsuàn, kě què hái suàn míngliàng. Shùnjiān, tā tóunǎo zhōng bèngfā chū yí ge xiǎngfǎ: "Rúguǒ jiāng xǔduō yínghuǒchóng jízhōng zài yìqǐ, bú jiù chéng dēng le ma?" Tā juédìng shì yi shì. Tā zhǎole ge báo bù zuò de bùnáng, zhuāle yìxiē yínghuǒchóng fàng zài lǐmiàn, ránhòu jiāng dàikǒu zāzhù, bǎ kǒudai diào qilai, yí ge "dēnglong" jiù zuòchéng la, suīrán méiyǒu yóudēng liàng, kàn shū háishi miǎnqiǎng kěyǐ de, cóngcǐ, yínghuǒchóng zuòchéng de "dēng" jiù yèyè péibànzhe tā.
column3: He followed the fireflies. Suddenly one flew right in front of him; he reached out, scooped it up, and held it in his palm. When he opened his hand—wow, the firefly was still sitting there obediently, its tail still glowing. Maybe that glow could only be measured in millimeters, but it was fairly bright. In an instant an idea burst into his head: "If I gathered lots of fireflies together, wouldn't that make a lamp?" He decided to give it a try. He found a pouch made of thin cloth, caught some fireflies and put them inside, tied the opening shut, and hung the bag up. A "lantern" was made! Although it wasn't as bright as an oil lamp, it was just about enough to read by. From then on, the "lamp" made of fireflies kept him company night after night.

column1: 他虽然不是天才，没有过人的天赋，但是日复一日的努力，使他的学识与日俱增，最后终于成为知名学者。
column2: Tā suīrán bú shì tiāncái, méiyǒu guòrén de tiānfù, dànshì rìfù yírì de nǔlì, shǐ tā de xuéshí yǔrì jùzēng, zuìhòu zhōngyú chéngwéi zhīmíng xuézhě.
column3: Although he was no genius and had no exceptional talent, his effort day after day made his learning grow with each passing day, and in the end he became a renowned scholar.

column1: 生活贫困并不可怕，可怕的是思想贫困、精神贫困、智慧贫困。贫困的经历在有些人那儿可以成为财富，成为奋斗拼搏的动力和源泉。
column2: Shēnghuó pínkùn bìng bù kěpà, kěpà de shì sīxiǎng pínkùn, jīngshén pínkùn, zhìhuì pínkùn. Pínkùn de jīnglì zài yǒuxiē rén nàr kěyǐ chéngwéi cáifù, chéngwéi fèndòu pīnbó de dònglì hé yuánquán.
column3: Material poverty is not frightening in itself; what is frightening is poverty of thought, of spirit, and of wisdom. For some people, the experience of poverty can become a kind of wealth—a driving force and a source of strength for striving and fighting on.

column1: 战国后期，秦国最强。秦王得知赵王得到一块叫“和氏璧”的宝玉，传话给赵王，说愿用十五座城换和氏璧。赵王左右为难，不知如何答复秦王：答应吧，怕上当受骗——给了和氏璧，拿不到城；不答应吧，又怕得罪秦国。于是，赶忙召集大臣商议对策。
column2: Zhànguó hòuqī, Qín guó zuì qiáng. Qín wáng dézhī Zhào wáng dédào yí kuài jiào "Héshìbì" de bǎoyù, chuánhuà gěi Zhào wáng, shuō yuàn yòng shíwǔ zuò chéng huàn Héshìbì. Zhào wáng zuǒyòu wéinán, bù zhī rúhé dáfù Qín wáng: dāying ba, pà shàngdàng shòupiàn — gěile Héshìbì, ná bu dào chéng; bù dāying ba, yòu pà dézuì Qín guó. Yúshì, gǎnmáng zhàojí dàchén shāngyì duìcè.
column3: In the late Warring States period, the state of Qin was the strongest. When the King of Qin learned that the King of Zhao had obtained a precious jade called the "He Shi Bi," he sent word to the King of Zhao that he was willing to trade fifteen cities for it. The King of Zhao was in a dilemma and didn't know how to answer: if he agreed, he feared being cheated—he would hand over the jade and never get the cities; if he refused, he feared offending Qin. So he hurriedly summoned his ministers to discuss what to do.

column1: 大臣们也没有好办法。有人提议，蔺相如见多识广，有勇有谋，可以听听他怎么说。赵王请来了蔺相如，并亲自向他请教。蔺相如说：“秦强赵弱，论实力，我们不答应不行；秦以十五座城换一块玉，也算慷慨，并未亏待赵国，若不答应，过错在赵；若将和氏璧送去，秦不交出城来，那么错就在秦了，因此我们只有送和氏璧。”赵王说：“那就请先生即刻动身前去磋商。”蔺相如说：“大王派我去，是我的荣幸。此去秦国，秦若是交了城，我便把璧留下；不交城，我一定完璧归赵。”
column2: Dàchénmen yě méiyǒu hǎo bànfǎ. Yǒu rén tíyì, Lìn Xiàngrú jiànduō shíguǎng, yǒu yǒng yǒu móu, kěyǐ tīngting tā zěnme shuō. Zhào wáng qǐngláile Lìn Xiàngrú, bìng qīnzì xiàng tā qǐngjiào. Lìn Xiàngrú shuō: "Qín qiáng Zhào ruò, lùn shílì, wǒmen bù dāying bùxíng; Qín yǐ shíwǔ zuò chéng huàn yí kuài yù, yě suàn kāngkǎi, bìng wèi kuīdài Zhào guó, ruò bù dāying, guòcuò zài Zhào; ruò jiāng Héshìbì sòngqu, Qín bù jiāo chū chéng lai, nàme cuò jiù zài Qín le, yīncǐ wǒmen zhǐyǒu sòng Héshìbì." Zhào wáng shuō: "Nà jiù qǐng xiānsheng jíkè dòngshēn qiánqù cuōshāng." Lìn Xiàngrú shuō: "Dàwáng pài wǒ qù, shì wǒ de róngxìng. Cǐ qù Qín guó, Qín ruòshì jiāole chéng, wǒ biàn bǎ bì liúxia; bù jiāo chéng, wǒ yídìng wánbì guīzhào."
column3: The ministers had no good ideas either. Someone suggested that Lin Xiangru was widely experienced and both brave and resourceful, so they might hear what he had to say. The King of Zhao sent for Lin Xiangru and personally asked his advice. Lin Xiangru said, "Qin is strong and Zhao is weak. In terms of strength, we can't refuse. Qin offering fifteen cities for one piece of jade is generous enough and doesn't treat Zhao unfairly; if we refuse, the fault lies with Zhao. If we send the jade and Qin doesn't hand over the cities, then the fault lies with Qin. So we have no choice but to send the jade." The King of Zhao said, "Then please set out at once, sir, to negotiate." Lin Xiangru said, "It is my honor that Your Majesty sends me. On this trip to Qin, if Qin hands over the cities, I will leave the jade there; if not, I will surely return the jade intact to Zhao."

column1: 蔺相如带着和氏璧到了秦国，转达了赵王的问候，把玉献给了秦王。秦王对着和氏璧左看右看，爱不释手。蔺相如等了半天不见秦王提换城之事，心想果然是个圈套，可璧在秦王手里，怎么把璧拿回来呢？左思右想之后，他对秦王说：“这璧有点儿小毛病，请大王把璧归还于我，我指给大王看。”秦王把璧递给蔺相如。蔺相如从容地站在殿中央，手抱和氏璧说：“大王派人到赵国，说用十五座城换赵国的璧。赵王派我将璧送来。可大王您好像并没有兑现的诚意。如今璧在我手里，想不交城拿走璧，那是妄想。”蔺相如发誓，如若逼他，就将自己的头和璧一起撞碎在柱子上，秦王看到的将是他的尸体和破碎的玉。秦王连忙说：“别误会，我怎么会撒谎呢？”忙命大臣拿出地图，把十五座城指给蔺相如看。蔺相如还是不敢相信秦王，说：“赵王送璧之前，举行了隆重的仪式：沐浴更衣，戒掉荤腥，只吃素食，以示庄严。我并非无理取闹，也不是冒犯大王。大王如真心换璧，亦请举行同样的仪式，我才敢把璧献给您。”
column2: Lìn Xiàngrú dàizhe Héshìbì dàole Qín guó, zhuǎndále Zhào wáng de wènhòu, bǎ yù xiàn gěile Qín wáng. Qín wáng duìzhe Héshìbì zuǒ kàn yòu kàn, àibúshìshǒu. Lìn Xiàngrú děngle bàntiān bú jiàn Qín wáng tí huàn chéng zhī shì, xīn xiǎng guǒrán shì ge quāntào, kě bì zài Qín wáng shǒu li, zěnme bǎ bì ná huilai ne? Zuǒsī yòuxiǎng zhīhòu, tā duì Qín wáng shuō: "Zhè bì yǒudiǎnr xiǎo máobing, qǐng dàwáng bǎ bì guīhuán yú wǒ, wǒ zhǐ gěi dàwáng kàn." Qín wáng bǎ bì dì gěi Lìn Xiàngrú. Lìn Xiàngrú cóngróng de zhàn zài diàn zhōngyāng, shǒu bào Héshìbì shuō: "Dàwáng pài rén dào Zhào guó, shuō yòng shíwǔ zuò chéng huàn Zhào guó de bì. Zhào wáng pài wǒ jiāng bì sònglai. Kě dàwáng nín hǎoxiàng bìng méiyǒu duìxiàn de chéngyì. Rújīn bì zài wǒ shǒu li, xiǎng bù jiāo chéng ná zǒu bì, nà shì wàngxiǎng." Lìn Xiàngrú fāshì, rúruò bī tā, jiù jiāng zìjǐ de tóu hé bì yìqǐ zhuàngsuì zài zhùzi shang, Qín wáng kàndào de jiāng shì tā de shītǐ hé pòsuì de yù. Qín wáng liánmáng shuō: "Bié wùhuì, wǒ zěnme huì sāhuǎng ne?" Máng mìng dàchén ná chū dìtú, bǎ shíwǔ zuò chéng zhǐ gěi Lìn Xiàngrú kàn. Lìn Xiàngrú háishi bù gǎn xiāngxìn Qín wáng, shuō: "Zhào wáng sòng bì zhīqián, jǔxíngle lóngzhòng de yíshì: mùyù gēngyī, jièdiào hūnxīng, zhǐ chī sùshí, yǐ shì zhuāngyán. Wǒ bìngfēi wúlǐ qǔnào, yě bú shì màofàn dàwáng. Dàwáng rú zhēnxīn huàn bì, yì qǐng jǔxíng tóngyàng de yíshì, wǒ cái gǎn bǎ bì xiàn gěi nín."
column3: Lin Xiangru brought the jade to Qin, conveyed the King of Zhao's greetings, and presented the jade to the King of Qin. The King of Qin examined it this way and that and couldn't bear to put it down. Lin Xiangru waited a long time without the king mentioning the exchange of cities, and thought to himself that it was a trap after all. But the jade was in the king's hands—how could he get it back? After thinking it over and over, he said to the King of Qin, "This jade has a small flaw. Please give it back to me, Your Majesty, and I will point it out to you." The King of Qin handed the jade to Lin Xiangru. Lin Xiangru calmly stood in the middle of the hall, holding the jade in his arms, and said, "Your Majesty sent men to Zhao saying you would exchange fifteen cities for Zhao's jade. The King of Zhao sent me to deliver it. But Your Majesty seems to have no sincere intention of keeping your word. Now the jade is in my hands; if you think you can take it without handing over the cities, that is wishful thinking." Lin Xiangru swore that if he were pressed, he would smash his head together with the jade against a pillar, and all the King of Qin would see would be his corpse and broken jade. The King of Qin hastily said, "Don't misunderstand—how could I lie?" He quickly ordered his ministers to bring out a map and pointed out the fifteen cities to Lin Xiangru. Lin Xiangru still didn't dare trust the King of Qin and said, "Before sending the jade, the King of Zhao held a solemn ceremony: he bathed and changed his clothes, gave up meat and fish, and ate only vegetarian food, to show his reverence. I am not being unreasonable, nor do I mean to offend Your Majesty. If Your Majesty sincerely wishes to exchange for the jade, please also hold the same ceremony; only then will I dare present it to you."

column1: 秦王想，璧都到了我这儿，我还怕他跑了不成？就说：“好，就依你。”蔺相如回到住处，立刻派人打扮成商人的模样，偷偷越过边境，把璧送回了赵国，并嘱咐身边的人，不可泄露秘密。五天后，秦王率领众大臣举行仪式，蔺相如坦然地对秦王说：“秦国仗着国力雄厚，一贯霸道，不讲信用，声誉不好，事情我就不一一列举了，今天，我怕大王您不履行承诺，已经把璧送回了赵国。”秦王听后大怒，说：“我堂堂秦王，还会骗你不成？你这不是歪曲我的意思吗？”
column2: Qín wáng xiǎng, bì dōu dàole wǒ zhèr, wǒ hái pà tā pǎo le bù chéng? Jiù shuō: "Hǎo, jiù yī nǐ." Lìn Xiàngrú huídào zhùchù, lìkè pài rén dǎban chéng shāngrén de múyàng, tōutōu yuèguò biānjìng, bǎ bì sònghuíle Zhào guó, bìng zhǔfù shēnbiān de rén, bùkě xièlòu mìmì. Wǔ tiān hòu, Qín wáng shuàilǐng zhòng dàchén jǔxíng yíshì, Lìn Xiàngrú tǎnrán de duì Qín wáng shuō: "Qín guó zhàngzhe guólì xiónghòu, yíguàn bàdào, bù jiǎng xìnyòng, shēngyù bù hǎo, shìqing wǒ jiù bù yīyī lièjǔ le, jīntiān, wǒ pà dàwáng nín bù lǚxíng chéngnuò, yǐjīng bǎ bì sònghuíle Zhào guó." Qín wáng tīng hòu dà nù, shuō: "Wǒ tángtáng Qín wáng, hái huì piàn nǐ bù chéng? Nǐ zhè bú shì wāiqū wǒ de yìsi ma?"
column3: The King of Qin thought, "The jade is already here with me—am I afraid it will run away?" So he said, "Fine, as you wish." Lin Xiangru returned to his lodgings and immediately sent someone disguised as a merchant to slip across the border and take the jade back to Zhao, and he told those around him not to let the secret out. Five days later, the King of Qin led his ministers in the ceremony. Lin Xiangru calmly said to him, "Relying on its great national strength, Qin has always been domineering and has never kept faith; its reputation is poor—I won't list the cases one by one. Today, fearing that Your Majesty would not keep your promise, I have already sent the jade back to Zhao." On hearing this the King of Qin flew into a rage and said, "I am the mighty King of Qin—would I cheat you? Aren't you twisting my meaning?"

column1: 蔺相如理直气壮地说：“众所周知，秦强赵弱。天下只可能强国欺负弱国，不可能弱国压迫强国。大王真要那块璧的话，不要光口头说，请先把十五座城割让给赵国，赵得到十五座城，绝不敢不把璧交出来。”
column2: Lìn Xiàngrú lǐzhí qìzhuàng de shuō: "Zhòngsuǒzhōuzhī, Qín qiáng Zhào ruò. Tiānxià zhǐ kěnéng qiángguó qīfu ruòguó, bù kěnéng ruòguó yāpò qiángguó. Dàwáng zhēn yào nà kuài bì dehuà, bú yào guāng kǒutóu shuō, qǐng xiān bǎ shíwǔ zuò chéng gēràng gěi Zhào guó, Zhào dédào shíwǔ zuò chéng, jué bù gǎn bù bǎ bì jiāo chulai."
column3: Lin Xiangru said boldly, with justice on his side, "Everyone knows that Qin is strong and Zhao is weak. In this world, a strong state may bully a weak one, but a weak state cannot oppress a strong one. If Your Majesty really wants the jade, don't just talk about it—please first cede the fifteen cities to Zhao. Once Zhao has the fifteen cities, it would never dare not hand over the jade."

column1: 秦王听蔺相如说得在理，只得装出一副高姿态说：“不就是一块玉嘛，秦赵两国总不能为这点儿小事闹出隔阂，再起争端。”
column2: Qín wáng tīng Lìn Xiàngrú shuō de zàilǐ, zhǐdé zhuāng chū yí fù gāo zītài shuō: "Bú jiù shì yí kuài yù ma, Qín Zhào liǎng guó zǒng bù néng wèi zhè diǎnr xiǎoshì nào chū géhé, zài qǐ zhēngduān."
column3: Hearing that Lin Xiangru's words made sense, the King of Qin had no choice but to put on a magnanimous air and say, "It's only a piece of jade. Qin and Zhao surely can't let such a trifle drive a wedge between them and start another dispute."

column1: 蔺相如归赵以后，秦国再也没有提过以城换玉的事情。
column2: Lìn Xiàngrú guī Zhào yǐhòu, Qín guó zài yě méiyǒu tíguo yǐ chéng huàn yù de shìqing.
column3: After Lin Xiangru returned to Zhao, Qin never again brought up exchanging cities for the jade.

column1: 俞伯牙从小酷爱音乐，他的琴声优美动听，犹如高山流水一般。虽然大家都赞美他琴弹得好，却从没有人能真正领会他琴声的内涵，他多想找到自己的知音啊！
column2: Yú Bóyá cóngxiǎo kù'ài yīnyuè, tā de qínshēng yōuměi dòngtīng, yóurú gāoshān liúshuǐ yìbān. Suīrán dàjiā dōu zànměi tā qín tán de hǎo, què cóng méiyǒu rén néng zhēnzhèng lǐnghuì tā qínshēng de nèihán, tā duō xiǎng zhǎodào zìjǐ de zhīyīn a!
column3: Yu Boya had loved music passionately since childhood. His zither playing was beautiful and moving, like high mountains and flowing water. Although everyone praised his playing, no one had ever truly grasped the meaning of his music. How he longed to find someone who truly understood it!

column1: 一个中秋之夜，他乘船来到江边，偶遇风浪，船停在了一个类似港湾的地方。晚上，风浪渐渐平息，天气晴朗，江水清澈，景色十分迷人。望着空中的明月，俞伯牙来了兴致，拿出琴弹了起来，一会儿他就沉醉在了音乐之中。忽然他看到一个人雕塑一样站在岸边，似乎听得出了神。俞伯牙一个不留神，“哟”的一声，琴弦绷断了一根。这时，听琴的人大声说：“先生不必在意，我是个打柴的，回家晚了，走到这里听到您在弹琴，觉得琴声美妙，不由得站在这里听了起来。”
column2: Yí ge Zhōngqiū zhī yè, tā chéng chuán láidào jiāngbiān, ǒu yù fēnglàng, chuán tíng zài le yí ge lèisì gǎngwān de dìfang. Wǎnshang, fēnglàng jiànjiàn píngxī, tiānqì qínglǎng, jiāngshuǐ qīngchè, jǐngsè shífēn mírén. Wàngzhe kōng zhōng de míngyuè, Yú Bóyá láile xìngzhì, ná chū qín tánle qilai, yíhuìr tā jiù chénzuì zài le yīnyuè zhī zhōng. Hūrán tā kàndào yí ge rén diāosù yíyàng zhàn zài ànbiān, sìhū tīng de chūle shén. Yú Bóyá yí ge bù liúshén, "yō" de yì shēng, qínxián bēngduànle yì gēn. Zhè shí, tīng qín de rén dàshēng shuō: "Xiānsheng búbì zàiyì, wǒ shì ge dǎ chái de, huí jiā wǎn le, zǒudào zhèli tīngdào nín zài tán qín, juéde qínshēng měimiào, bùyóude zhàn zài zhèli tīngle qilai."
column3: One Mid-Autumn night, he traveled by boat to a riverbank. Caught in wind and waves, the boat stopped at a spot like a small harbor. In the evening the wind and waves gradually died down; the sky was clear, the river water limpid, and the scenery enchanting. Gazing at the bright moon in the sky, Yu Boya was in the mood to play. He took out his zither and began, and soon he was lost in the music. Suddenly he saw a man standing on the bank like a statue, apparently listening spellbound. In a moment of inattention—"twang!"—one of Yu Boya's strings snapped. Just then the listener called out, "Don't mind me, sir. I'm a woodcutter on my way home late. When I got here I heard you playing, and the music was so beautiful that I couldn't help stopping to listen."

column1: 俞伯牙借着月光仔细打量，见那人身旁放着刚刚砍伐来的木柴，果然是个打柴的。俞伯牙心想：一个打柴的怎么能听懂我的琴呢？偏僻的山野还有这么不平凡的人？于是他问：“你既然懂琴，那就请说说，我弹的是什么曲子？”打柴人说：“先生刚才弹的乐谱是孔子为感叹他的弟子而创作的，只可惜，您弹到第四句的时候琴弦断了。”俞伯牙不禁感叹，民间真有精通音乐之人，难能可贵！他迫不及待地想和打柴人好好聊聊。
column2: Yú Bóyá jièzhe yuèguāng zǐxì dǎliang, jiàn nà rén shēnpáng fàngzhe gānggāng kǎnfá lái de mùchái, guǒrán shì ge dǎ chái de. Yú Bóyá xīn xiǎng: yí ge dǎ chái de zěnme néng tīng dǒng wǒ de qín ne? Piānpì de shānyě hái yǒu zhème bù píngfán de rén? Yúshì tā wèn: "Nǐ jìrán dǒng qín, nà jiù qǐng shuōshuo, wǒ tán de shì shénme qǔzi?" Dǎ chái rén shuō: "Xiānsheng gāngcái tán de yuèpǔ shì Kǒngzǐ wèi gǎntàn tā de dìzǐ ér chuàngzuò de, zhǐ kěxī, nín tándào dì-sì jù de shíhou qínxián duàn le." Yú Bóyá bùjīn gǎntàn, mínjiān zhēn yǒu jīngtōng yīnyuè zhī rén, nánnéng kěguì! Tā pòbùjídài de xiǎng hé dǎ chái rén hǎohāo liáoliao.
column3: By the moonlight Yu Boya looked the man over carefully and saw freshly cut firewood lying beside him—he really was a woodcutter. Yu Boya thought to himself: how could a woodcutter understand my music? Could there be such an extraordinary person out in these remote hills? So he asked, "Since you understand the zither, tell me: what piece was I playing?" The woodcutter said, "The piece you just played was composed by Confucius in lament for one of his disciples. What a pity that your string broke when you reached the fourth line." Yu Boya couldn't help exclaiming to himself that there really were people among the common folk who were masters of music—how rare and precious! He couldn't wait to have a good long talk with the woodcutter.

column1: 打柴人应邀上了船，看到俞伯牙的琴，赞道：“真是好琴。”接着又说起瑶琴的来历，俞伯牙不禁心生钦佩。接着俞伯牙又为打柴人演奏了几曲，请他辨识其中之意。当他的琴声雄壮豪迈的时候，打柴人说：“这旋律表达了高山的雄伟壮观。有气势，有气魄！”当琴声曲折激越、节奏短促时，打柴人说：“这旋律表达的是波涛汹涌，浪花飞溅，气概非凡！”当琴声变得清新流畅时，打柴人说：“这旋律表达的是无尽的流水。”俞伯牙惊喜万分，过去没人能听懂他琴声的含义，没想到在这荒凉之地，竟觅到自己久寻不遇的知音，不仅能领会其意，还能领悟其神。
column2: Dǎ chái rén yìngyāo shàngle chuán, kàndào Yú Bóyá de qín, zàn dào: "Zhēn shì hǎo qín." Jiēzhe yòu shuōqǐ yáoqín de láilì, Yú Bóyá bùjīn xīn shēng qīnpèi. Jiēzhe Yú Bóyá yòu wèi dǎ chái rén yǎnzòule jǐ qǔ, qǐng tā biànshí qízhōng zhī yì. Dāng tā de qínshēng xióngzhuàng háomài de shíhou, dǎ chái rén shuō: "Zhè xuánlǜ biǎodále gāoshān de xióngwěi zhuàngguān. Yǒu qìshì, yǒu qìpò!" Dāng qínshēng qūzhé jīyuè, jiézòu duǎncù shí, dǎ chái rén shuō: "Zhè xuánlǜ biǎodá de shì bōtāo xiōngyǒng, lànghuā fēijiàn, qìgài fēifán!" Dāng qínshēng biàn de qīngxīn liúchàng shí, dǎ chái rén shuō: "Zhè xuánlǜ biǎodá de shì wújìn de liúshuǐ." Yú Bóyá jīngxǐ wànfēn, guòqù méi rén néng tīng dǒng tā qínshēng de hányì, méi xiǎngdào zài zhè huāngliáng zhī dì, jìng mìdào zìjǐ jiǔ xún bú yù de zhīyīn, bùjǐn néng lǐnghuì qí yì, hái néng lǐngwù qí shén.
column3: The woodcutter accepted the invitation and came aboard. Seeing Yu Boya's zither, he praised it: "A truly fine instrument." Then he went on to tell the history of the yaoqin, and Yu Boya couldn't help feeling admiration. Next, Yu Boya played several more pieces for the woodcutter and asked him to identify their meaning. When the music was grand and bold, the woodcutter said, "This melody expresses the majesty and grandeur of high mountains. What power, what spirit!" When the music twisted and surged with short, quick rhythms, he said, "This melody expresses surging waves and flying spray—what extraordinary spirit!" When the music became fresh and flowing, he said, "This melody expresses endless flowing water." Yu Boya was overjoyed. In the past no one had been able to understand the meaning of his music; he never imagined that in this desolate place he would find the kindred spirit he had long sought in vain—someone who could not only grasp its meaning but also sense its very soul.

column1: 打柴人叫钟子期，两人在月下侃侃而谈，越谈越投机。黎明将至，钟子期告辞，并与俞伯牙约定，来年中秋还在这里相见。
column2: Dǎ chái rén jiào Zhōng Zǐqī, liǎng rén zài yuè xià kǎnkǎn'értán, yuè tán yuè tóujī. Límíng jiāng zhì, Zhōng Zǐqī gàocí, bìng yǔ Yú Bóyá yuēdìng, láinián Zhōngqiū hái zài zhèli xiāngjiàn.
column3: The woodcutter's name was Zhong Ziqi. The two talked freely under the moon, getting along better the more they talked. As dawn approached, Zhong Ziqi took his leave and agreed with Yu Boya to meet here again at next year's Mid-Autumn Festival.

column1: 第二年中秋这天，俞伯牙如约来到了老地方，从黄昏等到夜幕降临，一直不见钟子期到来，他有些诧异，开始用琴声呼唤钟子期，可还是见不到钟子期的影子。该不是有了什么变故吧？俞伯牙焦急万分。
column2: Dì-èr nián Zhōngqiū zhè tiān, Yú Bóyá rúyuē láidàole lǎo dìfang, cóng huánghūn děngdào yèmù jiànglín, yìzhí bú jiàn Zhōng Zǐqī dàolái, tā yǒuxiē chàyì, kāishǐ yòng qínshēng hūhuàn Zhōng Zǐqī, kě háishi jiàn bu dào Zhōng Zǐqī de yǐngzi. Gāi bú shì yǒule shénme biàngù ba? Yú Bóyá jiāojí wànfēn.
column3: On Mid-Autumn Day the following year, Yu Boya came to the old spot as agreed. He waited from dusk until night fell, but Zhong Ziqi never came. Somewhat surprised, he began calling to Zhong Ziqi with the sound of his zither, but there was still no sign of him. Could something have happened to him? Yu Boya was extremely anxious.

column1: 第二天，俞伯牙向一位老人打听他的好友，老人告诉他，钟子期染病，辞世已有段时间了。临走前，他留下遗言，把坟墓修在江边，到八月十五，好听俞伯牙弹琴。老人的话使俞伯牙泪流不止，他来到钟子期坟前，弹了一曲《高山流水》，曲终，他把心爱的琴摔了个粉碎，悲伤地说：“琴向来是要弹给知音听的，如今我唯一的知音已不在人世，这琴还弹给谁听呢？”
column2: Dì-èr tiān, Yú Bóyá xiàng yí wèi lǎorén dǎting tā de hǎoyǒu, lǎorén gàosu tā, Zhōng Zǐqī rǎnbìng, císhì yǐ yǒu duàn shíjiān le. Lín zǒu qián, tā liúxia yíyán, bǎ fénmù xiū zài jiāngbiān, dào bā yuè shíwǔ, hǎo tīng Yú Bóyá tán qín. Lǎorén de huà shǐ Yú Bóyá lèi liú bù zhǐ, tā láidào Zhōng Zǐqī fén qián, tánle yì qǔ "Gāoshān Liúshuǐ", qǔ zhōng, tā bǎ xīn'ài de qín shuāile ge fěnsuì, bēishāng de shuō: "Qín xiànglái shì yào tán gěi zhīyīn tīng de, rújīn wǒ wéiyī de zhīyīn yǐ bú zài rénshì, zhè qín hái tán gěi shéi tīng ne?"
column3: The next day, Yu Boya asked an old man about his friend. The old man told him that Zhong Ziqi had fallen ill and had passed away some time ago. Before he died, he left word that his grave be built by the river so that on the fifteenth day of the eighth month he could hear Yu Boya play. The old man's words brought endless tears to Yu Boya's eyes. He went to Zhong Ziqi's grave and played "High Mountains and Flowing Water." When the piece ended, he smashed his beloved zither to pieces and said sorrowfully, "A zither has always been meant to be played for one who truly understands it. Now that my only kindred spirit is no longer in this world, who would I play it for?"

column1: 故事有些凄凉，但两位知音的深情厚谊感动了后人，至今人们还用“知音”来形容朋友之间真挚而纯洁的情谊。
column2: Gùshi yǒuxiē qīliáng, dàn liǎng wèi zhīyīn de shēnqíng hòuyì gǎndòngle hòurén, zhìjīn rénmen hái yòng "zhīyīn" lái xíngróng péngyou zhījiān zhēnzhì ér chúnjié de qíngyì.
column3: The story is a sad one, but the deep friendship between these two kindred spirits has moved later generations. To this day people still use the word "zhiyin" (one who knows the tune) to describe a sincere and pure friendship.

column1: （一）大脑能“听”出笑声的真假
column2: (Yī) Dànǎo néng "tīng" chū xiàoshēng de zhēnjiǎ
column3: (1) The brain can "hear" whether laughter is real or fake

column1: 真是岂有此理，难道我们听到庸俗、不上档次的笑话假笑两声、敷衍一下也不可以吗？可是，好像确实不行。诸位，如果你不想难堪，不想让别人发现你发出的是虚伪、违背心意的笑声，你可以回避，可以不表态，可以把话题岔开，可以装聋装哑，但不要画蛇添足，违心地笑。因为只要你笑，不管你多机灵，不管你掩饰得多么周密，别人都能看出你的笑是真心实意，还是虚情假意、装模作样。有人不禁要问，人是通过什么途径识别“笑”背后的真实情感呢？研究者发现，我们在听到发自内心的笑声和虚假的笑声时，大脑会呈现出完全不同的反应。
column2: Zhēn shì qǐyǒucǐlǐ, nándào wǒmen tīngdào yōngsú, bú shàng dàngcì de xiàohua jiǎ xiào liǎng shēng, fūyǎn yíxià yě bù kěyǐ ma? Kěshì, hǎoxiàng quèshí bùxíng. Zhūwèi, rúguǒ nǐ bù xiǎng nánkān, bù xiǎng ràng biérén fāxiàn nǐ fāchū de shì xūwěi, wéibèi xīnyì de xiàoshēng, nǐ kěyǐ huíbì, kěyǐ bù biǎotài, kěyǐ bǎ huàtí chàkāi, kěyǐ zhuāng lóng zhuāng yǎ, dàn bú yào huàshé tiānzú, wéixīn de xiào. Yīnwèi zhǐyào nǐ xiào, bùguǎn nǐ duō jīling, bùguǎn nǐ yǎnshì de duōme zhōumì, biérén dōu néng kàn chū nǐ de xiào shì zhēnxīn shíyì, háishi xūqíng jiǎyì, zhuāngmú zuòyàng. Yǒu rén bùjīn yào wèn, rén shì tōngguò shénme tújìng shíbié "xiào" bèihòu de zhēnshí qínggǎn ne? Yánjiūzhě fāxiàn, wǒmen zài tīngdào fāzì nèixīn de xiàoshēng hé xūjiǎ de xiàoshēng shí, dànǎo huì chéngxiàn chū wánquán bùtóng de fǎnyìng.
column3: How absurd! Do you mean we can't even fake a couple of laughs to humor someone when we hear a vulgar, tasteless joke? Yet it seems we really can't. Ladies and gentlemen, if you don't want to be embarrassed or have others discover that your laughter is insincere and against your true feelings, you can avoid the situation, decline to react, change the subject, or play deaf and dumb—but don't overdo it by laughing against your will. Because as soon as you laugh, no matter how clever you are or how carefully you cover it up, others can tell whether your laughter is heartfelt or false and put on. Some will naturally ask: how do people detect the true feelings behind a laugh? Researchers have found that when we hear genuine laughter and fake laughter, the brain responds in completely different ways.

column1: 假笑声会激活大脑中用于破译情感信息的特定区域，同时大脑会自动分析假笑的缘故，假笑者想隐瞒什么，以及假笑者的意向；诚挚的笑声则会激活大脑中与积极情绪相关的区域。为了证实这一理论，一丝不苟的研究者让志愿者倾听网站视频中的笑声，同时记录他们大脑的反应，并将志愿者听到真笑与假笑时大脑的反应做对比。测试结果一目了然，志愿者在预先未被告知测试目的的情况下，仅凭直觉就能准确地分辨出假笑声。天呀，人的大脑中竟然深藏着一双能够探测他人喜悦之情真伪的眼睛！
column2: Jiǎ xiàoshēng huì jīhuó dànǎo zhōng yòngyú pòyì qínggǎn xìnxī de tèdìng qūyù, tóngshí dànǎo huì zìdòng fēnxī jiǎ xiào de yuángù, jiǎ xiào zhě xiǎng yǐnmán shénme, yǐjí jiǎ xiào zhě de yìxiàng; chéngzhì de xiàoshēng zé huì jīhuó dànǎo zhōng yǔ jījí qíngxù xiāngguān de qūyù. Wèile zhèngshí zhè yì lǐlùn, yìsī bùgǒu de yánjiūzhě ràng zhìyuànzhě qīngtīng wǎngzhàn shìpín zhōng de xiàoshēng, tóngshí jìlù tāmen dànǎo de fǎnyìng, bìng jiāng zhìyuànzhě tīngdào zhēn xiào yǔ jiǎ xiào shí dànǎo de fǎnyìng zuò duìbǐ. Cèshì jiéguǒ yímù liǎorán, zhìyuànzhě zài yùxiān wèi bèi gàozhī cèshì mùdì de qíngkuàng xià, jǐn píng zhíjué jiù néng zhǔnquè de fēnbiàn chū jiǎ xiàoshēng. Tiān ya, rén de dànǎo zhōng jìngrán shēn cángzhe yì shuāng nénggòu tàncè tārén xǐyuè zhī qíng zhēnwěi de yǎnjing!
column3: Fake laughter activates specific areas of the brain used to decode emotional information; at the same time the brain automatically analyzes why the person is faking it, what they are trying to hide, and what their intentions are. Sincere laughter, on the other hand, activates areas of the brain associated with positive emotions. To confirm this theory, meticulous researchers had volunteers listen to laughter in online videos while recording their brain responses, and compared the brain's responses to real and fake laughter. The results were crystal clear: without being told the purpose of the test beforehand, the volunteers could accurately pick out fake laughter by intuition alone. Goodness—hidden deep in the human brain is a pair of eyes that can detect whether someone else's joy is genuine or not!

column1: 研究者指出：“人类大脑对于笑声中所隐含的社会和情感信息非常敏感，这不完全是智商问题。当志愿者听到笑声时，会开启大脑中与心智相关的区域，从而获知他人的情感或精神状态，有些志愿者还动用了大脑中控制运动和感知的部分，进而更精准地提炼出真假笑声背后的信息。”
column2: Yánjiūzhě zhǐchū: "Rénlèi dànǎo duìyú xiàoshēng zhōng suǒ yǐnhán de shèhuì hé qínggǎn xìnxī fēicháng mǐngǎn, zhè bù wánquán shì zhìshāng wèntí. Dāng zhìyuànzhě tīngdào xiàoshēng shí, huì kāiqǐ dànǎo zhōng yǔ xīnzhì xiāngguān de qūyù, cóng'ér huòzhī tārén de qínggǎn huò jīngshén zhuàngtài, yǒuxiē zhìyuànzhě hái dòngyòngle dànǎo zhōng kòngzhì yùndòng hé gǎnzhī de bùfen, jìn'ér gèng jīngzhǔn de tíliàn chū zhēn jiǎ xiàoshēng bèihòu de xìnxī."
column3: The researchers pointed out: "The human brain is very sensitive to the social and emotional information hidden in laughter, and this isn't entirely a matter of IQ. When volunteers hear laughter, they switch on areas of the brain related to the mind, thereby perceiving other people's emotional or mental state. Some volunteers also engaged the parts of the brain that control movement and perception, allowing them to extract the information behind real and fake laughter even more precisely."

column1: （二）笑未必是最佳良药
column2: (Èr) Xiào wèibì shì zuì jiā liángyào
column3: (2) Laughter is not necessarily the best medicine

column1: 中国人喜欢听相声，因为它逗笑。
column2: Zhōngguórén xǐhuan tīng xiàngsheng, yīnwèi tā dòuxiào.
column3: Chinese people like listening to crosstalk because it makes them laugh.

column1: “笑有益于健康”几乎得到了全世界的认可，“笑一笑十年少”“一笑解千愁”不仅被大家认可，甚至被一些人当作生活的座右铭。中国人深信开怀大笑也好，哈哈傻笑也罢，哪怕是私下里偷偷地笑，都会是生活中最通用，而且管用的治病良方。
column2: Xiào yǒuyì yú jiànkāng jīhū dédàole quán shìjiè de rènkě, "xiào yi xiào shí nián shào" "yí xiào jiě qiān chóu" bùjǐn bèi dàjiā rènkě, shènzhì bèi yìxiē rén dàngzuò shēnghuó de zuòyòumíng. Zhōngguórén shēnxìn kāihuái dàxiào yěhǎo, hāhā shǎxiào yěbà, nǎpà shì sīxià li tōutōu de xiào, dōu huì shì shēnghuó zhōng zuì tōngyòng, érqiě guǎnyòng de zhì bìng liángfāng.
column3: Laughter is good for your health is accepted almost all over the world. Sayings like "A smile makes you ten years younger" and "One laugh dispels a thousand worries" are not only widely accepted but even taken by some as mottos to live by. Chinese people firmly believe that whether it's a hearty laugh, a silly chuckle, or even laughing secretly to yourself, laughter is the most universal and effective cure in life.

column1: 有研究证实，笑可以调节情绪，可以促进血液循环和腹肌收缩，100次捧腹大笑所吸收的氧气相当于用桨划船10分钟的吸氧量。有人做过这样的试验，开怀大笑一整天，可以燃烧掉2000卡路里，从而帮助消耗脂肪，减轻体重，同时，笑有助于缓解动脉硬化，有助于消除紧张感，这就是笑有利于健康的实质性的证据。
column2: Yǒu yánjiū zhèngshí, xiào kěyǐ tiáojié qíngxù, kěyǐ cùjìn xuèyè xúnhuán hé fùjī shōusuō, yìbǎi cì pěngfù dàxiào suǒ xīshōu de yǎngqì xiāngdāng yú yòng jiǎng huá chuán shí fēnzhōng de xī yǎng liàng. Yǒu rén zuòguo zhèyàng de shìyàn, kāihuái dàxiào yì zhěng tiān, kěyǐ ránshāo diào liǎngqiān kǎlùlǐ, cóng'ér bāngzhù xiāohào zhīfáng, jiǎnqīng tǐzhòng, tóngshí, xiào yǒuzhù yú huǎnjiě dòngmài yìnghuà, yǒuzhù yú xiāochú jǐnzhānggǎn, zhè jiù shì xiào yǒulì yú jiànkāng de shízhìxìng de zhèngjù.
column3: Research has confirmed that laughter can regulate mood and promote blood circulation and the contraction of the abdominal muscles; the oxygen taken in by 100 belly laughs equals the amount taken in by rowing a boat for 10 minutes. Someone has done an experiment showing that laughing heartily for a whole day can burn 2,000 calories, which helps burn fat and lose weight. At the same time, laughter helps ease hardening of the arteries and helps relieve tension. This is the substantive evidence that laughter is good for health.

column1: 然而，笑，真的是人生旅途中的最佳良药吗？答案似乎不是那么肯定。有研究人员表示，笑也不是有百益而无一害的，有时它还会产生副作用。有医生就碰到过这样的案例：有人在肆无忌惮地笑过后因心跳加速而昏迷，而大笑到“几乎笑破肚皮”可能会导致疝气、心脏不舒服，甚至损坏人体健康。新的研究结果对笑“有百益而无一害”的观点提出了挑战，似乎更倾向于笑不是坏事，但分寸要掌握得恰到好处。可是多数人还是深信，笑的是非无须探讨，任何形式的幽默，伤害风险都不高，其收益则是显而易见的，况且，真是好朋友在一起，高兴了，起起哄，或是遇到了开心事，哪里还顾得上斟酌分寸掌握得恰当不恰当呢？
column2: Rán'ér, xiào, zhēn de shì rénshēng lǚtú zhōng de zuì jiā liángyào ma? Dá'àn sìhū bú shì nàme kěndìng. Yǒu yánjiū rényuán biǎoshì, xiào yě bú shì yǒu bǎi yì ér wú yí hài de, yǒushí tā hái huì chǎnshēng fùzuòyòng. Yǒu yīshēng jiù pèngdàoguo zhèyàng de ànlì: yǒu rén zài sìwújìdàn de xiàoguo hòu yīn xīntiào jiāsù ér hūnmí, ér dàxiào dào "jīhū xiàopò dùpí" kěnéng huì dǎozhì shànqì, xīnzàng bù shūfu, shènzhì sǔnhuài réntǐ jiànkāng. Xīn de yánjiū jiéguǒ duì xiào "yǒu bǎi yì ér wú yí hài" de guāndiǎn tíchūle tiǎozhàn, sìhū gèng qīngxiàng yú xiào bú shì huàishì, dàn fēncun yào zhǎngwò de qiàdào hǎochù. Kěshì duōshù rén háishi shēnxìn, xiào de shìfēi wúxū tàntǎo, rènhé xíngshì de yōumò, shānghài fēngxiǎn dōu bù gāo, qí shōuyì zé shì xiǎn'éryìjiàn de, kuàngqiě, zhēn shì hǎo péngyou zài yìqǐ, gāoxìng le, qǐqihòng, huòshì yùdàole kāixīn shì, nǎli hái gù de shàng zhēnzhuó fēncun zhǎngwò de qiàdàng bú qiàdàng ne?
column3: But is laughter really the best medicine on life's journey? The answer doesn't seem so certain. Some researchers say that laughter isn't all benefit and no harm; sometimes it has side effects. Doctors have come across cases like this: someone fainted from a racing heart after laughing unrestrainedly, and laughing so hard you "nearly split your sides" can lead to hernias and heart discomfort, and can even damage your health. The new findings challenge the view that laughter "has a hundred benefits and no harm," and seem to lean toward the idea that laughing isn't a bad thing, but it should be done in just the right measure. Yet most people still firmly believe there's no need to debate the rights and wrongs of laughter: humor of any kind carries little risk of harm, while its benefits are obvious. Besides, when good friends get together and are having fun, joking around, or when something happy happens, who has time to weigh whether they're laughing in the right measure?

column1: 对普通人来说，睡觉只是惯例，可是对于患有顽固失眠症的人来说，睡觉却成了难得的奢侈。
column2: Duì pǔtōng rén lái shuō, shuìjiào zhǐ shì guànlì, kěshì duìyú huàn yǒu wángù shīmiánzhèng de rén lái shuō, shuìjiào què chéngle nándé de shēchǐ.
column3: For ordinary people, sleep is just routine, but for those with stubborn insomnia, sleep has become a rare luxury.

column1: 近日，中国发布的睡眠指数总得分66.5分，超过36.2%的居民得分低于及格线60分。统计数字显示，睡眠指数的得分随着城市层级的升高而下降，一线城市的平均睡眠指数为60.3分，三线城市为61.4分，而农村和小城镇得分均在70分以上。可见，当前失眠症正扰乱着人们的情绪，摧残着城市人群的健康。
column2: Jìnrì, Zhōngguó fābù de shuìmián zhǐshù zǒng défēn liùshíliù diǎn wǔ fēn, chāoguò bǎi fēn zhī sānshíliù diǎn èr de jūmín défēn dī yú jígéxiàn liùshí fēn. Tǒngjì shùzì xiǎnshì, shuìmián zhǐshù de défēn suízhe chéngshì céngjí de shēnggāo ér xiàjiàng, yī xiàn chéngshì de píngjūn shuìmián zhǐshù wéi liùshí diǎn sān fēn, sān xiàn chéngshì wéi liùshíyī diǎn sì fēn, ér nóngcūn hé xiǎo chéngzhèn défēn jūn zài qīshí fēn yǐshàng. Kějiàn, dāngqián shīmiánzhèng zhèng rǎoluànzhe rénmen de qíngxù, cuīcánzhe chéngshì rénqún de jiànkāng.
column3: Recently, China published a sleep index with an overall score of 66.5, and more than 36.2% of residents scored below the passing line of 60. The statistics show that sleep index scores fall as city tier rises: the average sleep index in first-tier cities is 60.3, in third-tier cities 61.4, while rural areas and small towns all score above 70. Clearly, insomnia is currently disturbing people's moods and ravaging the health of city dwellers.

column1: 调查发现，该睡时不睡，是影响成人健康睡眠的重要因素。手机和平板电脑的普及，使睡前上网的习惯日渐盛行，不少人临睡前再过过网瘾成了常态。而电子产品严重的光污染不仅影响了人体褪黑素的正常分泌，还会使人体生物钟后移，结果就是晚上睡不着，早上睡不醒。
column2: Diàochá fāxiàn, gāi shuì shí bú shuì, shì yǐngxiǎng chéngrén jiànkāng shuìmián de zhòngyào yīnsù. Shǒujī hé píngbǎn diànnǎo de pǔjí, shǐ shuì qián shàngwǎng de xíguàn rìjiàn shèngxíng, bù shǎo rén lín shuì qián zài guòguo wǎngyǐn chéngle chángtài. Ér diànzǐ chǎnpǐn yánzhòng de guāng wūrǎn bùjǐn yǐngxiǎngle réntǐ tuìhēisù de zhèngcháng fēnmì, hái huì shǐ réntǐ shēngwùzhōng hòu yí, jiéguǒ jiù shì wǎnshang shuì bu zháo, zǎoshang shuì bu xǐng.
column3: Surveys have found that not going to bed when you should is an important factor affecting adults' healthy sleep. With the spread of mobile phones and tablets, the habit of going online before bed has become increasingly common, and for many people indulging their internet addiction one last time before sleep has become the norm. The severe light pollution from electronic devices not only disrupts the body's normal secretion of melatonin but also shifts the body clock later, with the result that people can't fall asleep at night and can't wake up in the morning.

column1: 褪黑素是什么？据研究，褪黑素是保证人体健康的重要物质之一，它的职能包括增强人体免疫力、抗衰老、调剂睡眠等。当人体内褪黑素分泌不正常时，人体细胞组织和器官的作用和活动能力都会受到影响，各种疾病，包括恶性肿瘤，也就是我们常说的癌症，就会随之而来。
column2: Tuìhēisù shì shénme? Jù yánjiū, tuìhēisù shì bǎozhèng réntǐ jiànkāng de zhòngyào wùzhì zhī yī, tā de zhínéng bāokuò zēngqiáng réntǐ miǎnyìlì, kàng shuāilǎo, tiáojì shuìmián děng. Dāng réntǐ nèi tuìhēisù fēnmì bú zhèngcháng shí, réntǐ xìbāo zǔzhī hé qìguān de zuòyòng hé huódòng nénglì dōu huì shòudào yǐngxiǎng, gè zhǒng jíbìng, bāokuò èxìng zhǒngliú, yě jiù shì wǒmen cháng shuō de áizhèng, jiù huì suí zhī ér lái.
column3: What is melatonin? According to research, melatonin is one of the important substances that keep the body healthy. Its functions include boosting immunity, fighting aging, and regulating sleep. When the body's melatonin secretion is abnormal, the functioning and activity of the body's cells, tissues, and organs are all affected, and various diseases—including malignant tumors, what we commonly call cancer—follow.

column1: 除了睡不着，还有人睡不好。中国有睡眠障碍的人约为38.2%，因此，在中国专治睡眠障碍的医生总是供不应求。
column2: Chúle shuì bu zháo, hái yǒu rén shuì bu hǎo. Zhōngguó yǒu shuìmián zhàng'ài de rén yuē wéi bǎi fēn zhī sānshíbā diǎn èr, yīncǐ, zài Zhōngguó zhuān zhì shuìmián zhàng'ài de yīshēng zǒngshì gōngbùyìngqiú.
column3: Besides those who can't fall asleep, there are people who sleep badly. About 38.2% of people in China have sleep disorders, so in China doctors specializing in sleep disorders are always in short supply.

column1: 睡眠障碍表现为入睡困难，头在枕头上，就是睡不着，翻来覆去瞎折腾，心烦意乱得无法容忍，白天又老是犯困。此外，入睡后噩梦连连，一会儿踢腿，一会儿挥拳头，不时大声叫喊，也是睡眠障碍的典型症状。
column2: Shuìmián zhàng'ài biǎoxiàn wéi rùshuì kùnnan, tóu zài zhěntou shang, jiùshì shuì bu zháo, fānlái fùqù xiā zhēteng, xīnfán yìluàn de wúfǎ róngrěn, báitiān yòu lǎoshì fànkùn. Cǐwài, rùshuì hòu èmèng liánlián, yíhuìr tī tuǐ, yíhuìr huī quántou, bùshí dàshēng jiàohǎn, yě shì shuìmián zhàng'ài de diǎnxíng zhèngzhuàng.
column3: Sleep disorders show up as difficulty falling asleep: your head is on the pillow but you just can't sleep, tossing and turning restlessly, so agitated you can't stand it, and then you're always drowsy during the day. In addition, having one nightmare after another once asleep—kicking one moment, swinging your fists the next, and shouting out loud from time to time—is also a typical symptom of sleep disorders.

column1: 睡眠不足会使人气色不好，行为能力偏离正常轨道，据悉，一个17～19个小时没睡觉的人，其行为能力与一个血液中酒精浓度为0.05%的人不相上下。即便一周内每天少睡两个小时，疲劳也会累积在一起，并在不适宜的场合引发事故，我们曾见过这样一个不可思议的案例，一位技术熟练的老司机把车开上了逆行道，而这就是疲劳驾驶造成的。
column2: Shuìmián bùzú huì shǐ rén qìsè bù hǎo, xíngwéi nénglì piānlí zhèngcháng guǐdào, jùxī, yí ge shíqī dào shíjiǔ ge xiǎoshí méi shuìjiào de rén, qí xíngwéi nénglì yǔ yí ge xuèyè zhōng jiǔjīng nóngdù wéi bǎi fēn zhī líng diǎn líng wǔ de rén bùxiāng shàngxià. Jíbiàn yì zhōu nèi měi tiān shǎo shuì liǎng ge xiǎoshí, píláo yě huì lěijī zài yìqǐ, bìng zài bú shìyí de chǎnghé yǐnfā shìgù, wǒmen céng jiànguo zhèyàng yí ge bùkě sīyì de ànlì, yí wèi jìshù shúliàn de lǎo sījī bǎ chē kāishàngle nìxíngdào, ér zhè jiù shì píláo jiàshǐ zàochéng de.
column3: Lack of sleep gives people a poor complexion and throws their ability to function off its normal track. Reportedly, a person who hasn't slept for 17 to 19 hours performs about as well as someone with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.05%. Even sleeping just two hours less each day for a week lets fatigue build up and can cause accidents at the wrong moment. We once saw an incredible case in which a skilled, experienced driver drove into the oncoming lane—and this was caused by driving while fatigued.

column1: 此外，长期睡眠不足还会使人注意力下降、表情茫然、丢三落四、情绪起伏不定，动不动就发呆，继而记性越来越差，到了更严重的地步，会思维混乱，健康状况逐步恶化，进而诱发慢性疾病，总而言之，睡眠好坏对人体健康举足轻重，因此，医生呼吁，不要对失眠症状无动于衷，要弄清病因，并根据不同情况竭尽全力进行治疗。
column2: Cǐwài, chángqī shuìmián bùzú hái huì shǐ rén zhùyìlì xiàjiàng, biǎoqíng mángrán, diūsān làsì, qíngxù qǐfú búdìng, dòngbudòng jiù fādāi, jì'ér jìxing yuè lái yuè chà, dàole gèng yánzhòng de dìbù, huì sīwéi hùnluàn, jiànkāng zhuàngkuàng zhúbù èhuà, jìn'ér yòufā mànxìng jíbìng, zǒng'éryánzhī, shuìmián hǎohuài duì réntǐ jiànkāng jǔzú qīngzhòng, yīncǐ, yīshēng hūyù, bú yào duì shīmián zhèngzhuàng wúdòngyúzhōng, yào nòngqīng bìngyīn, bìng gēnjù bùtóng qíngkuàng jiéjìn quánlì jìnxíng zhìliáo.
column3: In addition, long-term sleep deprivation also lowers people's concentration, leaving them with a blank expression, forgetful, moody, and prone to staring into space at the slightest thing; then their memory gets worse and worse. In more serious cases, their thinking becomes confused, their health gradually deteriorates, and chronic diseases may follow. In short, the quality of sleep is crucial to health. Doctors therefore urge people not to be indifferent to insomnia symptoms, but to find out the cause and do everything possible to treat it according to each situation.

column1: 不可否认的是，很多人原本睡眠是没有问题的，导致问题的根源多多少少与不健康的生活方式有关，因此，对付失眠症的方法就是纠正不好的生活习惯，不要糟蹋自己的身体，不要自己迫害自己，不要让坏习惯毁灭我们的健康。
column2: Bùkě fǒurèn de shì, hěn duō rén yuánběn shuìmián shì méiyǒu wèntí de, dǎozhì wèntí de gēnyuán duōduō shǎoshǎo yǔ bú jiànkāng de shēnghuó fāngshì yǒuguān, yīncǐ, duìfu shīmiánzhèng de fāngfǎ jiù shì jiūzhèng bù hǎo de shēnghuó xíguàn, bú yào zāota zìjǐ de shēntǐ, bú yào zìjǐ pòhài zìjǐ, bú yào ràng huài xíguàn huǐmiè wǒmen de jiànkāng.
column3: It cannot be denied that many people originally had no problem sleeping; the root of the problem is more or less related to an unhealthy lifestyle. So the way to deal with insomnia is to correct bad living habits: don't abuse your body, don't torment yourself, and don't let bad habits destroy our health.

column1: 记者：王老师，欢迎您到我们节目来做客。今天来的都是您的忠实观众，大家特别愿意和您这样的大专家进行交流。
column2: Jìzhě: Wáng lǎoshī, huānyíng nín dào wǒmen jiémù lái zuòkè. Jīntiān lái de dōu shì nín de zhōngshí guānzhòng, dàjiā tèbié yuànyì hé nín zhèyàng de dà zhuānjiā jìnxíng jiāoliú.
column3: Reporter: Teacher Wang, welcome to our program. Everyone here today is a loyal fan of yours, and they're especially eager to talk with a great expert like you.

column1: 王老师：“专家”不敢当，有这样的机会，我也很高兴。
column2: Wáng lǎoshī: "Zhuānjiā" bù gǎndāng, yǒu zhèyàng de jīhuì, wǒ yě hěn gāoxìng.
column3: Teacher Wang: I don't deserve to be called an "expert," but I'm very glad to have this opportunity.

column1: 记者：那天采访您，在公园走廊那儿，您和您徒弟是练气功还是练太极剑呢？
column2: Jìzhě: Nà tiān cǎifǎng nín, zài gōngyuán zǒuláng nàr, nín hé nín túdì shì liàn qìgōng háishi liàn tàijíjiàn ne?
column3: Reporter: The day we interviewed you, over in the park corridor, were you and your apprentices practicing qigong or tai chi sword?

column1: 王老师：哦，不是徒弟，是气功协会的气功爱好者。
column2: Wáng lǎoshī: Ò, bú shì túdì, shì Qìgōng Xiéhuì de qìgōng àihàozhě.
column3: Teacher Wang: Oh, they aren't apprentices—they're qigong enthusiasts from the Qigong Association.

column1: 记者：你们的气功不是那种力量一爆发，能瞬间把好几块砖就给劈开的啊？
column2: Jìzhě: Nǐmen de qìgōng bú shì nà zhǒng lìliang yí bàofā, néng shùnjiān bǎ hǎo jǐ kuài zhuān jiù gěi pīkāi de a?
column3: Reporter: Isn't your qigong the kind where you unleash a burst of power and split several bricks in an instant?

column1: 王老师：那只是气功的一种。气功还是中国独特的健身方法之一，可以增强体质，促进慢性病康复，还可以辅助治疗某些疾病。
column2: Wáng lǎoshī: Nà zhǐ shì qìgōng de yì zhǒng. Qìgōng hái shì Zhōngguó dútè de jiànshēn fāngfǎ zhī yī, kěyǐ zēngqiáng tǐzhì, cùjìn mànxìngbìng kāngfù, hái kěyǐ fǔzhù zhìliáo mǒuxiē jíbìng.
column3: Teacher Wang: That's just one type of qigong. Qigong is also one of China's unique ways of keeping fit: it can strengthen the constitution, help people recover from chronic illnesses, and assist in treating certain diseases.

column1: 记者：看来我是误解气功了。最近有个调查，广大群众的健身意识在逐年提升。对于健康，您能对我们说点儿什么吗？
column2: Jìzhě: Kànlái wǒ shì wùjiě qìgōng le. Zuìjìn yǒu ge diàochá, guǎngdà qúnzhòng de jiànshēn yìshi zài zhúnián tíshēng. Duìyú jiànkāng, nín néng duì wǒmen shuō diǎnr shénme ma?
column3: Reporter: It seems I misunderstood qigong. A recent survey shows that the general public's awareness of fitness is rising year by year. Can you tell us something about health?

column1: 王老师：健康的新概念不仅是不生病，还包括心理健康和社会交往方面的能力，甚至有人提出健康五要素，包括身体、情绪、智力、精神和社交，这五个方面共同构成健康的完美状态。有句名言：生命在于运动，其实健康也在于运动。当然要达到健康的目的，还要讲究运动的方法。
column2: Wáng lǎoshī: Jiànkāng de xīn gàiniàn bùjǐn shì bù shēngbìng, hái bāokuò xīnlǐ jiànkāng hé shèhuì jiāowǎng fāngmiàn de nénglì, shènzhì yǒu rén tíchū jiànkāng wǔ yàosù, bāokuò shēntǐ, qíngxù, zhìlì, jīngshén hé shèjiāo, zhè wǔ ge fāngmiàn gòngtóng gòuchéng jiànkāng de wánměi zhuàngtài. Yǒu jù míngyán: shēngmìng zàiyú yùndòng, qíshí jiànkāng yě zàiyú yùndòng. Dāngrán yào dádào jiànkāng de mùdì, hái yào jiǎngjiu yùndòng de fāngfǎ.
column3: Teacher Wang: The new concept of health isn't just not getting sick; it also includes mental health and the ability to interact socially. Some people have even proposed five elements of health—body, emotions, intellect, spirit, and social life—which together make up a perfect state of health. There's a famous saying: life lies in movement. In fact, health lies in movement too. Of course, to achieve good health, you also have to pay attention to how you exercise.

column1: 记者：那您就着重跟我们谈谈运动的学问吧。
column2: Jìzhě: Nà nín jiù zhuózhòng gēn wǒmen tántan yùndòng de xuéwen ba.
column3: Reporter: Then please focus on telling us about the know-how of exercise.

column1: 王老师：要健康，首要问题是勤于运用大脑，人的大脑不用也会生锈。大家知道，人脑左半球主管抽象思维，右半球主管形象思维，二者有分工有联系。左右脑交替使用，思维常可以放射出新的火花。著名科学家钱学森的夫人是音乐家，钱学森的很多重要科学理论不是端端正正地坐在桌子前面想出来的，而是听过音乐之后冒出来的。科学运用左右脑，工作的高效和防止脑衰就成为了可能。大脑潜力巨大，它是人体衰退最慢的器官。一些养生著作中指出，人用脑越勤，大脑各神经细胞之间的联系越多，形成的条件反射也越多。
column2: Wáng lǎoshī: Yào jiànkāng, shǒuyào wèntí shì qínyú yùnyòng dànǎo, rén de dànǎo bú yòng yě huì shēngxiù. Dàjiā zhīdào, rénnǎo zuǒ bànqiú zhǔguǎn chōuxiàng sīwéi, yòu bànqiú zhǔguǎn xíngxiàng sīwéi, èrzhě yǒu fēngōng yǒu liánxì. Zuǒ yòu nǎo jiāotì shǐyòng, sīwéi cháng kěyǐ fàngshè chū xīn de huǒhuā. Zhùmíng kēxuéjiā Qián Xuésēn de fūrén shì yīnyuèjiā, Qián Xuésēn de hěn duō zhòngyào kēxué lǐlùn bú shì duānduānzhèngzhèng de zuò zài zhuōzi qiánmiàn xiǎng chulai de, ér shì tīngguo yīnyuè zhīhòu mào chulai de. Kēxué yùnyòng zuǒ yòu nǎo, gōngzuò de gāoxiào hé fángzhǐ nǎo shuāi jiù chéngwéi le kěnéng. Dànǎo qiánlì jùdà, tā shì réntǐ shuāituì zuì màn de qìguān. Yìxiē yǎngshēng zhùzuò zhōng zhǐchū, rén yòng nǎo yuè qín, dànǎo gè shénjīng xìbāo zhījiān de liánxì yuè duō, xíngchéng de tiáojiàn fǎnshè yě yuè duō.
column3: Teacher Wang: To be healthy, the top priority is to use your brain diligently—an unused brain will rust, too. As everyone knows, the left hemisphere of the human brain governs abstract thinking and the right governs imagistic thinking; the two divide the work but are connected. Using the left and right brain alternately often makes your thinking throw off new sparks. The wife of the famous scientist Qian Xuesen was a musician, and many of Qian Xuesen's important scientific theories weren't worked out sitting upright at a desk—they popped up after he'd listened to music. By using the left and right brain scientifically, working efficiently and preventing brain decline become possible. The brain has enormous potential; it's the organ in the body that declines the slowest. Some books on health preservation point out that the more diligently you use your brain, the more connections form between its nerve cells, and the more conditioned reflexes develop.

column1: 记者：大脑就像我们身体的指挥中心，大脑不健康，人就谈不上健康。
column2: Jìzhě: Dànǎo jiù xiàng wǒmen shēntǐ de zhǐhuī zhōngxīn, dànǎo bú jiànkāng, rén jiù tán bu shàng jiànkāng.
column3: Reporter: The brain is like our body's command center—if the brain isn't healthy, a person can hardly be called healthy.

column1: 王老师：对。其次呢，运动贵在坚持。懒惰是人天生的弱点，所以不要迁就自己，要以坚定的意志、坚韧的精神克服惰性，下狠心咬牙坚持，绝不能半途而废。
column2: Wáng lǎoshī: Duì. Qícì ne, yùndòng guì zài jiānchí. Lǎnduò shì rén tiānshēng de ruòdiǎn, suǒyǐ bú yào qiānjiù zìjǐ, yào yǐ jiāndìng de yìzhì, jiānrèn de jīngshén kèfú duòxìng, xià hěnxīn yǎoyá jiānchí, jué bù néng bàntú érfèi.
column3: Teacher Wang: Right. Second, the key to exercise is persistence. Laziness is a weakness people are born with, so don't indulge yourself. Overcome inertia with firm will and a tenacious spirit, make up your mind, grit your teeth and keep going—never give up halfway.

column1: 记者：王老师，您怎么好像在说我呢？我就不想虐待自己，所以很难坚持。
column2: Jìzhě: Wáng lǎoshī, nín zěnme hǎoxiàng zài shuō wǒ ne? Wǒ jiù bù xiǎng nüèdài zìjǐ, suǒyǐ hěn nán jiānchí.
column3: Reporter: Teacher Wang, how come it sounds like you're talking about me? I just don't want to torture myself, so it's hard for me to stick with it.

column1: 王老师：怎么会是虐待呢？你以后联系我，我带你锻炼。咱们有计划，有落实。运动健身归根到底是自己的事，胡乱对付其实是在骗自己，坚持运动也是培养人的意志力、完善人格的过程。
column2: Wáng lǎoshī: Zěnme huì shì nüèdài ne? Nǐ yǐhòu liánxì wǒ, wǒ dài nǐ duànliàn. Zánmen yǒu jìhuà, yǒu luòshí. Yùndòng jiànshēn guīgēn dàodǐ shì zìjǐ de shì, húluàn duìfu qíshí shì zài piàn zìjǐ, jiānchí yùndòng yě shì péiyǎng rén de yìzhìlì, wánshàn réngé de guòchéng.
column3: Teacher Wang: How could it be torture? Get in touch with me later and I'll train with you. We'll have a plan and follow through on it. In the end, exercising to keep fit is your own business; doing it sloppily is really just fooling yourself. Sticking with exercise is also a process of building willpower and perfecting one's character.

column1: 记者：看来运动真不是小事，还间接体现着我们的品行呢。
column2: Jìzhě: Kànlái yùndòng zhēn bú shì xiǎoshì, hái jiànjiē tǐxiànzhe wǒmen de pǐnxíng ne.
column3: Reporter: So exercise really is no small matter—it even indirectly reflects our moral character.

column1: 王老师：另外，冬季健身好处很多，可以提高人的御寒能力；冬天阳光中的紫外线对人体有消毒作用，还能促进对钙的吸收；冬天空气中二氧化碳浓度比夏天低，所以冬天运动对身体更为有利；运动还可以使人心情舒畅。许多保健食品都宣扬能够促进健康，其实运动才是维护健康最好的方法。
column2: Wáng lǎoshī: Lìngwài, dōngjì jiànshēn hǎochù hěn duō, kěyǐ tígāo rén de yùhán nénglì; dōngtiān yángguāng zhōng de zǐwàixiàn duì réntǐ yǒu xiāodú zuòyòng, hái néng cùjìn duì gài de xīshōu; dōngtiān kōngqì zhōng èryǎnghuàtàn nóngdù bǐ xiàtiān dī, suǒyǐ dōngtiān yùndòng duì shēntǐ gèng wéi yǒulì; yùndòng hái kěyǐ shǐ rén xīnqíng shūchàng. Xǔduō bǎojiàn shípǐn dōu xuānyáng nénggòu cùjìn jiànkāng, qíshí yùndòng cái shì wéihù jiànkāng zuì hǎo de fāngfǎ.
column3: Teacher Wang: Also, exercising in winter has many benefits. It can improve your resistance to cold; the ultraviolet rays in winter sunlight have a disinfecting effect on the body and also promote calcium absorption; the concentration of carbon dioxide in the air is lower in winter than in summer, so exercising in winter is even better for the body; and exercise can also lift your mood. Many health foods claim to promote health, but in fact exercise is the best way to maintain it.

column1: 记者：运动对皮肤是不是也有好处？
column2: Jìzhě: Yùndòng duì pífū shì bu shì yě yǒu hǎochù?
column3: Reporter: Is exercise good for the skin too?

column1: 王老师：运动能令全身排汗，毛孔内的垃圾及多余油脂会被排走，皮肤自然会更好。
column2: Wáng lǎoshī: Yùndòng néng lìng quánshēn páihàn, máokǒng nèi de lājī jí duōyú yóuzhī huì bèi páizǒu, pífū zìrán huì gèng hǎo.
column3: Teacher Wang: Exercise makes your whole body sweat, flushing out the dirt and excess oil in your pores, so naturally your skin gets better.

column1: 记者：运动是不是也要讲究科学？
column2: Jìzhě: Yùndòng shì bu shì yě yào jiǎngjiu kēxué?
column3: Reporter: Does exercise also need to be done scientifically?

column1: 王老师：当然。运动健身要循序渐进，不要急于求成；不适合自己身体状况的剧烈运动或大幅度动作尽量别勉强。
column2: Wáng lǎoshī: Dāngrán. Yùndòng jiànshēn yào xúnxù jiànjìn, bú yào jíyú qiúchéng; bú shìhé zìjǐ shēntǐ zhuàngkuàng de jùliè yùndòng huò dà fúdù dòngzuò jǐnliàng bié miǎnqiǎng.
column3: Teacher Wang: Of course. Exercise should progress step by step—don't rush for quick results. Try not to force yourself into strenuous exercise or large movements that don't suit your physical condition.

column1: 记者：运动之后，我们常常觉得又渴又饿，运动和饮食之间有什么讲究吗？
column2: Jìzhě: Yùndòng zhīhòu, wǒmen chángcháng juéde yòu kě yòu è, yùndòng hé yǐnshí zhījiān yǒu shénme jiǎngjiu ma?
column3: Reporter: After exercising we often feel both thirsty and hungry. Is there anything to keep in mind about exercise and diet?

column1: 王老师：锻炼后是肌肉细胞的“进食时间”，它们渴望得到足够的蛋白质、水和维生素。运动后的两小时，是补充营养的最佳时机。
column2: Wáng lǎoshī: Duànliàn hòu shì jīròu xìbāo de "jìnshí shíjiān", tāmen kěwàng dédào zúgòu de dànbáizhì, shuǐ hé wéishēngsù. Yùndòng hòu de liǎng xiǎoshí, shì bǔchōng yíngyǎng de zuì jiā shíjī.
column3: Teacher Wang: After a workout it's "mealtime" for the muscle cells—they crave enough protein, water, and vitamins. The two hours after exercise are the best time to replenish nutrition.

column1: 记者：王老师，您真不愧是这方面的专家，以后要是能定期和您做些交流就好了。
column2: Jìzhě: Wáng lǎoshī, nín zhēn búkuì shì zhè fāngmiàn de zhuānjiā, yǐhòu yàoshi néng dìngqī hé nín zuò xiē jiāoliú jiù hǎo le.
column3: Reporter: Teacher Wang, you truly are an expert in this field. It would be great if we could talk with you regularly from now on.

column1: 王老师：这是我的联系方式，以后我们可以多联络。希望大家回去以后坚持锻炼，多多保重。
column2: Wáng lǎoshī: Zhè shì wǒ de liánxì fāngshì, yǐhòu wǒmen kěyǐ duō liánluò. Xīwàng dàjiā huí qu yǐhòu jiānchí duànliàn, duōduō bǎozhòng.
column3: Teacher Wang: Here's my contact information—let's keep in touch. I hope everyone keeps exercising after going home, and takes good care of yourselves.

column1: 到今天为止，我们的社会对好男人的标准从没有改变过：男人要有责任心，为人正直、宽容、刚直，不背叛朋友；男人要上进，有抱负，有魄力；男人要谦虚、诚实、大方；男人要有修养，心胸开阔，处境艰难而不退缩，面对打击而不脆弱；男人是生活中的榜样，家庭的靠山，社会的支柱。总之，男人要顶天立地，光彩照人，要有男人的气概。
column2: Dào jīntiān wéizhǐ, wǒmen de shèhuì duì hǎo nánrén de biāozhǔn cóng méiyǒu gǎibiàn guo: nánrén yào yǒu zérènxīn, wéirén zhèngzhí, kuānróng, gāngzhí, bú bèipàn péngyou; nánrén yào shàngjìn, yǒu bàofù, yǒu pòlì; nánrén yào qiānxū, chéngshí, dàfang; nánrén yào yǒu xiūyǎng, xīnxiōng kāikuò, chǔjìng jiānnán ér bú tuìsuō, miànduì dǎjī ér bú cuìruò; nánrén shì shēnghuó zhōng de bǎngyàng, jiātíng de kàoshān, shèhuì de zhīzhù. Zǒngzhī, nánrén yào dǐngtiān lìdì, guāngcǎi zhàorén, yào yǒu nánrén de qìgài.
column3: To this day, our society's standard for a good man has never changed: a man should have a sense of responsibility, be upright, tolerant, and unbending, and never betray his friends; a man should be driven, ambitious, and bold; a man should be modest, honest, and generous; a man should be cultivated and broad-minded, not shrinking back in hard times or crumbling under blows; a man is a role model in life, the family's pillar of support, and a mainstay of society. In short, a man should stand tall between heaven and earth, shine brilliantly, and have a manly spirit.

column1: 不仅如此，男人们从小受到的教育就是“男儿有泪不轻弹”，意思是说，理智的男子汉再悲伤也不轻易哭泣，爱哭的男人走到哪儿都会被一票否决，因为男人流泪就意味着软弱、没出息，而这种教育是从娃娃时代就潜移默化地在起作用了，他们天天被这样的古训鞭策着。我们的文化赋予了男人高大、坚强的形象，他们在生活中必须扮演强者。
column2: Bùjǐn rúcǐ, nánrénmen cóngxiǎo shòudào de jiàoyù jiù shì "nán'ér yǒu lèi bù qīng tán", yìsi shì shuō, lǐzhì de nánzǐhàn zài bēishāng yě bù qīngyì kūqì, ài kū de nánrén zǒu dào nǎr dōu huì bèi yìpiào fǒujué, yīnwèi nánrén liúlèi jiù yìwèizhe ruǎnruò, méi chūxi, ér zhè zhǒng jiàoyù shì cóng wáwa shídài jiù qiányí mòhuà de zài qǐ zuòyòng le, tāmen tiāntiān bèi zhèyàng de gǔxùn biāncèzhe. Wǒmen de wénhuà fùyǔ le nánrén gāodà, jiānqiáng de xíngxiàng, tāmen zài shēnghuó zhōng bìxū bànyǎn qiángzhě.
column3: Not only that, but from childhood men are taught that "a real man doesn't shed tears lightly," meaning that a rational man, however sad, doesn't cry easily, and a man who cries a lot will be rejected out of hand wherever he goes, because a man shedding tears signifies weakness and worthlessness. This upbringing has been working on them subtly since they were little kids, and they're spurred on by such ancient teachings every day. Our culture has given men a tall, strong image, and they must play the strong one in life.

column1: 男人们为了不被鄙视，不被讥笑，为了远离那些恶心、不体面的词汇，千百次谆谆叮嘱自己：伤心是软弱的表现，哪怕遭受打击、面对失败、受尽委屈，也一定要坚强，这是什么时候都不能含糊的。
column2: Nánrénmen wèile bú bèi bǐshì, bú bèi jīxiào, wèile yuǎnlí nàxiē ěxin, bù tǐmiàn de cíhuì, qiān bǎi cì zhūnzhūn dīngzhǔ zìjǐ: shāngxīn shì ruǎnruò de biǎoxiàn, nǎpà zāoshòu dǎjī, miànduì shībài, shòujìn wěiqu, yě yídìng yào jiānqiáng, zhè shì shénme shíhou dōu bù néng hánhu de.
column3: So as not to be despised or mocked, and to stay far away from those disgusting, undignified labels, men earnestly remind themselves hundreds and thousands of times: being sad is a sign of weakness; even when struck by setbacks, facing failure, or suffering every kind of injustice, you must be strong—and this is something you can never be vague about.

column1: 实际情况是，“男儿有泪不轻弹”是社会文化赋予男人的一种束缚。男人不是魔鬼，也不是神仙，他们也是有血有肉、有健全情感的人。男人也有喜怒哀乐，也需要关怀，也需要温柔的抚慰，否则，再有力的肩膀也有被压塌的时候。事实表明，长期的压抑、隐忍对健康只有坏处，没有好处，反之，以适当的方式将情绪释放一下，人的心绪才会变得平和。
column2: Shíjì qíngkuàng shì, "nán'ér yǒu lèi bù qīng tán" shì shèhuì wénhuà fùyǔ nánrén de yì zhǒng shùfù. Nánrén bú shì móguǐ, yě bú shì shénxiān, tāmen yě shì yǒuxuè yǒuròu, yǒu jiànquán qínggǎn de rén. Nánrén yě yǒu xǐ nù āi lè, yě xūyào guānhuái, yě xūyào wēnróu de fǔwèi, fǒuzé, zài yǒulì de jiānbǎng yě yǒu bèi yātā de shíhou. Shìshí biǎomíng, chángqī de yāyì, yǐnrěn duì jiànkāng zhǐ yǒu huàichu, méiyǒu hǎochù, fǎnzhī, yǐ shìdàng de fāngshì jiāng qíngxù shìfàng yíxià, rén de xīnxù cái huì biànde pínghé.
column3: In reality, "a real man doesn't shed tears lightly" is a constraint that social culture places on men. Men are neither devils nor gods; they too are flesh-and-blood people with full emotions. Men also feel joy, anger, sorrow, and happiness, and they too need care and gentle comfort—otherwise even the strongest shoulders will eventually collapse under the weight. Facts show that long-term repression and holding things in do nothing but harm to health; on the contrary, only by releasing emotions in an appropriate way can a person's state of mind become calm.

column1: 其实，眼泪是情绪释放的一种形式，人在情绪抑郁时会分泌一种被称为痛苦激素的物质，它会让人情绪低落、无精打采，眼泪恰恰可以将它排出体外。通常人们哭泣后，在情绪强度上会降低40%，如果不能利用眼泪把情绪压力转移掉，则会影响身体健康。
column2: Qíshí, yǎnlèi shì qíngxù shìfàng de yì zhǒng xíngshì, rén zài qíngxù yìyù shí huì fēnmì yì zhǒng bèi chēngwéi tòngkǔ jīsù de wùzhì, tā huì ràng rén qíngxù dīluò, wújīng dǎcǎi, yǎnlèi qiàqià kěyǐ jiāng tā páichū tǐ wài. Tōngcháng rénmen kūqì hòu, zài qíngxù qiángdù shang huì jiàngdī bǎi fēn zhī sìshí, rúguǒ bù néng lìyòng yǎnlèi bǎ qíngxù yālì zhuǎnyí diào, zé huì yǐngxiǎng shēntǐ jiànkāng.
column3: In fact, tears are one form of emotional release. When people are depressed, they secrete a substance called a "pain hormone" that leaves them feeling low and listless, and tears happen to be exactly what can flush it out of the body. Usually, after people cry, the intensity of their emotions drops by 40%. If you can't use tears to get rid of emotional stress, it will affect your physical health.

column1: 中医认为，忧伤肺。当人难过、想哭的时候，喉咙里会觉得不舒服。喉咙直接通肺，喉咙不舒服，就是肺部受刺激了；人哭起来常常会一把鼻涕一把泪，之所以会流鼻涕，也是肺受了刺激。一旦悲伤难过没有了，也就不再流鼻涕了，喉咙也会舒适起来。这说明，悲伤难过对肺会有影响。伤心难过之际，不妨痛哭。哭完了，一切都得到了修复。因此，不发给男人宣泄情绪的许可证不是正道，男人也有流泪的权利。我们倡导要给男人释放情绪的空间，男人流泪本在情理之中。
column2: Zhōngyī rènwéi, yōu shāng fèi. Dāng rén nánguò, xiǎng kū de shíhou, hóulong li huì juéde bù shūfu. Hóulong zhíjiē tōng fèi, hóulong bù shūfu, jiù shì fèibù shòu cìjī le; rén kū qilai chángcháng huì yì bǎ bítì yì bǎ lèi, zhīsuǒyǐ huì liú bítì, yě shì fèi shòu le cìjī. Yídàn bēishāng nánguò méiyǒu le, yě jiù bú zài liú bítì le, hóulong yě huì shūshì qilai. Zhè shuōmíng, bēishāng nánguò duì fèi huì yǒu yǐngxiǎng. Shāngxīn nánguò zhī jì, bùfáng tòngkū. Kū wán le, yíqiè dōu dédào le xiūfù. Yīncǐ, bù fā gěi nánrén xuānxiè qíngxù de xǔkězhèng bú shì zhèngdào, nánrén yě yǒu liúlèi de quánlì. Wǒmen chàngdǎo yào gěi nánrén shìfàng qíngxù de kōngjiān, nánrén liúlèi běn zài qínglǐ zhī zhōng.
column3: Traditional Chinese medicine holds that grief harms the lungs. When people are sad and want to cry, their throat feels uncomfortable. The throat leads straight to the lungs, so a sore throat means the lungs are being stimulated; when people cry they often have a runny nose along with their tears, and the reason the nose runs is also that the lungs have been stimulated. Once the grief and sadness are gone, the nose stops running and the throat feels comfortable again. This shows that grief and sadness affect the lungs. When you're heartbroken, you might as well have a good cry. Once you've cried, everything is restored. Therefore, refusing to grant men a license to vent their emotions is not the right way; men also have the right to cry. We advocate giving men room to release their emotions—a man shedding tears is only natural and reasonable.

column1: 不过，宣泄归宣泄，宣泄时忌讳哭泣时间过长，一般不要超过15分钟，压抑的心情得到发泄、缓解后就不要再哭，否则对身体反而有害。因为人的胃肠机能对情绪极为敏感，忧愁悲伤或哭泣时间过长，胃的运动会减慢，会影响食欲，甚至引起其他胃部疾病。
column2: Búguò, xuānxiè guī xuānxiè, xuānxiè shí jìhuì kūqì shíjiān guò cháng, yìbān bú yào chāoguò shíwǔ fēnzhōng, yāyì de xīnqíng dédào fāxiè, huǎnjiě hòu jiù bú yào zài kū, fǒuzé duì shēntǐ fǎn'ér yǒuhài. Yīnwèi rén de wèicháng jīnéng duì qíngxù jí wéi mǐngǎn, yōuchóu bēishāng huò kūqì shíjiān guò cháng, wèi de yùndòng huì jiǎnmàn, huì yǐngxiǎng shíyù, shènzhì yǐnqǐ qítā wèibù jíbìng.
column3: However, venting is one thing, but when venting you should avoid crying for too long—generally no more than 15 minutes. Once your pent-up feelings have been released and eased, stop crying; otherwise it will actually harm your body. That's because the stomach and intestines are extremely sensitive to emotion: if you're worried and sad or cry for too long, your stomach's movement slows down, which affects your appetite and can even cause other stomach ailments.

column1: 释放情绪除了哭泣，还应在想法上做调整：扔掉外界对男人流泪的鄙视，因为这种鄙视只是一种狭隘的偏见。不要阻挠男人流泪，男人流泪不等于软弱无用，也并不丧失尊严。男人本身也不必理睬别人说三道四，谁都不能长久地淹没在忧伤、难过的情绪中。偶尔具有负面情绪不是什么坏事，它能让我们更了解自己，让我们成长，让我们更深刻地体悟到什么是快乐。
column2: Shìfàng qíngxù chúle kūqì, hái yīng zài xiǎngfǎ shang zuò tiáozhěng: rēngdiào wàijiè duì nánrén liúlèi de bǐshì, yīnwèi zhè zhǒng bǐshì zhǐ shì yì zhǒng xiá'ài de piānjiàn. Bú yào zǔnáo nánrén liúlèi, nánrén liúlèi bù děngyú ruǎnruò wúyòng, yě bìng bú sàngshī zūnyán. Nánrén běnshēn yě búbì lǐcǎi biérén shuōsān dàosì, shéi dōu bù néng chángjiǔ de yānmò zài yōushāng, nánguò de qíngxù zhōng. Ǒu'ěr jùyǒu fùmiàn qíngxù bú shì shénme huàishì, tā néng ràng wǒmen gèng liǎojiě zìjǐ, ràng wǒmen chéngzhǎng, ràng wǒmen gèng shēnkè de tǐwù dào shénme shì kuàilè.
column3: Besides crying, releasing emotions also requires adjusting your thinking: throw away the outside world's contempt for men who cry, because that contempt is just a narrow-minded prejudice. Don't stop men from crying—a man crying doesn't mean he's weak and useless, nor does he lose his dignity. Men themselves needn't pay attention to others' gossip, either; nobody can stay drowned in sorrow and sadness forever. Having negative emotions now and then isn't a bad thing: it helps us understand ourselves better, helps us grow, and lets us realize more deeply what happiness is.

column1: 须知，真正的个人成长往往来自于痛苦、磨难，而非快乐，不要抹杀掉痛苦在我们成长中的功劳。既然悲伤无可避免，就应该好好面对悲伤，不要妄想生命中从不出现这样的过程和阶段。毕竟，快乐往往是短暂的，人生岁月中更多地伴随着的是灰暗的情绪，而它却可以沉淀出智慧。
