column2: Xūzhī, zhēnzhèng de gèrén chéngzhǎng wǎngwǎng láizì yú tòngkǔ, mónàn, ér fēi kuàilè, bú yào mǒshā diào tòngkǔ zài wǒmen chéngzhǎng zhōng de gōngláo. Jìrán bēishāng wú kě bìmiǎn, jiù yīnggāi hǎohāo miànduì bēishāng, bú yào wàngxiǎng shēngmìng zhōng cóng bù chūxiàn zhèyàng de guòchéng hé jiēduàn. Bìjìng, kuàilè wǎngwǎng shì duǎnzàn de, rénshēng suìyuè zhōng gèng duō de bànsuízhe de shì huī'àn de qíngxù, ér tā què kěyǐ chéndiàn chū zhìhuì.
column3: Keep in mind that real personal growth often comes from pain and hardship, not from happiness—don't erase the credit pain deserves for our growth. Since sorrow can't be avoided, we should face it properly instead of wishfully thinking that such phases will never appear in our lives. After all, happiness is often fleeting; what accompanies us more through the years of life are gloomy emotions, yet from them wisdom can settle out.

column1: 为期三天的假期，我和儿时的好友结伴去西安旅行。
column2: Wéiqī sān tiān de jiàqī, wǒ hé érshí de hǎoyǒu jiébàn qù Xī'ān lǚxíng.
column3: For a three-day holiday, my childhood friend and I traveled together to Xi'an.

column1: 去时乘高铁，车程6小时。列车缓缓离开了车站，很快就以征服一切的气势甩开窗外的景致，以300公里的时速跨过了桥梁，穿越了平原。车窗外，模糊的景象夹杂着西北的风沙呼啸而过。坐在宽敞座椅中的人们，享受着齐全的软硬件设施，看电影的看电影，打电话的打电话，更多的则是把自己封闭在小小的手机屏幕中，不是用语言，而是用符号传递着各自的情感。寄情于虚拟世界的网迷们对喧哗的现实流露出的是不屑一顾的冷淡。伴随着“终点站到了”的广播，我和朋友像千千万万旅途中的人们一样，没等车停稳，就兴冲冲地守候在车门口，迫不及待地投入到西安滚滚的人流中。
column2: Qù shí chéng gāotiě, chēchéng liù xiǎoshí. Lièchē huǎnhuǎn líkāi le chēzhàn, hěn kuài jiù yǐ zhēngfú yíqiè de qìshì shuǎikāi chuāng wài de jǐngzhì, yǐ sānbǎi gōnglǐ de shísù kuàguò le qiáoliáng, chuānyuè le píngyuán. Chēchuāng wài, móhu de jǐngxiàng jiāzázhe xīběi de fēngshā hūxiào ér guò. Zuò zài kuānchang zuòyǐ zhōng de rénmen, xiǎngshòuzhe qíquán de ruǎn yìngjiàn shèshī, kàn diànyǐng de kàn diànyǐng, dǎ diànhuà de dǎ diànhuà, gèng duō de zé shì bǎ zìjǐ fēngbì zài xiǎoxiǎo de shǒujī píngmù zhōng, bú shì yòng yǔyán, ér shì yòng fúhào chuándìzhe gèzì de qínggǎn. Jìqíng yú xūnǐ shìjiè de wǎngmímen duì xuānhuá de xiànshí liúlù chū de shì búxiè yígù de lěngdàn. Bànsuízhe "zhōngdiǎnzhàn dào le" de guǎngbō, wǒ hé péngyou xiàng qiānqiānwànwàn lǚtú zhōng de rénmen yíyàng, méi děng chē tíngwěn, jiù xìngchōngchōng de shǒuhòu zài chēmén kǒu, pòbùjídài de tóurù dào Xī'ān gǔngǔn de rénliú zhōng.
column3: On the way there we took the high-speed train—a six-hour ride. The train slowly pulled out of the station and soon, with an air of conquering everything, left the scenery outside the window behind, crossing bridges and plains at 300 kilometers an hour. Outside the window, blurry scenes whistled past mixed with the wind and sand of the northwest. The people sitting in the spacious seats enjoyed the complete hardware and software facilities: those watching movies watched movies, those on the phone talked on the phone, but even more shut themselves inside tiny phone screens, conveying their feelings not with words but with symbols. Internet addicts who poured their feelings into the virtual world showed nothing but disdainful indifference to the noisy real world. As the announcement "We've reached the terminal station" came on, my friend and I, like the countless thousands of other travelers, didn't wait for the train to stop completely before eagerly standing by the door, impatient to throw ourselves into Xi'an's surging crowds.

column1: 三天的旅行很快就结束了，我们回程坐特快，将近13个小时的硬座。列车没有了高铁的威风，不紧不慢地开出了车站，不温不火地匀速前行，仿佛知道一路上将会演绎出许许多多的故事。不久我就发现硬座车厢信号很差无法上网；灯光昏暗无法看书；没有电源，耗尽了电量的手机无法充电；人多嘈杂混乱得睡不着觉，闭塞的车厢里，我们像是回到了50年前。朋友忽然说：“其实有时候吧，我还挺喜欢这种感觉的，只有这时候，人和人之间才有种久违的亲近感，也许是因为我们手头都没有事情，愿意彼此分享和倾听。”之后发生的一切，都像是在证明朋友的话是对的。
column2: Sān tiān de lǚxíng hěn kuài jiù jiéshù le, wǒmen huíchéng zuò tèkuài, jiāngjìn shísān ge xiǎoshí de yìngzuò. Lièchē méiyǒu le gāotiě de wēifēng, bù jǐn bú màn de kāichū le chēzhàn, bù wēn bù huǒ de yúnsù qián xíng, fǎngfú zhīdào yílù shang jiāng huì yǎnyì chū xǔxǔduōduō de gùshi. Bùjiǔ wǒ jiù fāxiàn yìngzuò chēxiāng xìnhào hěn chà wúfǎ shàngwǎng; dēngguāng hūn'àn wúfǎ kàn shū; méiyǒu diànyuán, hàojìn le diànliàng de shǒujī wúfǎ chōngdiàn; rén duō cáozá hùnluàn de shuì bu zháo jiào, bìsè de chēxiāng li, wǒmen xiàng shì huídào le wǔshí nián qián. Péngyou hūrán shuō: "Qíshí yǒu shíhou ba, wǒ hái tǐng xǐhuan zhè zhǒng gǎnjué de, zhǐyǒu zhè shíhou, rén hé rén zhījiān cái yǒu zhǒng jiǔwéi de qīnjìngǎn, yěxǔ shì yīnwèi wǒmen shǒutóu dōu méiyǒu shìqing, yuànyì bǐcǐ fēnxiǎng hé qīngtīng." Zhīhòu fāshēng de yíqiè, dōu xiàng shì zài zhèngmíng péngyou de huà shì duì de.
column3: The three-day trip was over in no time. On the way back we took an express train—nearly 13 hours in a hard seat. The train had none of the high-speed train's grandeur; it left the station unhurriedly and moved forward at a steady, lukewarm pace, as if it knew many, many stories would unfold along the way. Before long I discovered that the signal in the hard-seat carriage was too poor to get online; the lights were too dim to read; there were no power outlets, so phones whose batteries had run out couldn't be charged; and it was so crowded, noisy, and chaotic that no one could sleep. In that cut-off carriage it felt as though we'd gone back 50 years. My friend suddenly said, "Actually, sometimes I really like this feeling. Only at times like this is there a long-lost sense of closeness between people—maybe because none of us has anything at hand, so we're willing to share and listen to each other." Everything that happened afterward seemed to prove my friend right.

column1: 昏暗的灯光下，我和朋友开始聊天儿。她讲起小学的时候，班里颇有正义感的女生李芳芳如何见义勇为，在洪水中英勇救人；我感叹初中时，班里那个贵族气十足的男生，他叫……唉，一时竟忘了他叫什么名字。他16岁到了农村，从播种开始学习，后来长成了个精悍的汉子，改革开放后第一批承包了土地，就此发家致富，他简直就是一代人中的奇迹。我们想起小学的地理老师，讲课的时候总会带出些方言，班里调皮的男生千方百计跟她捣乱，气得老师狼狈不堪，那会儿的我们真是幼稚得可笑。还有，中学我们班那个料事如神的诸葛亮……火车上，我们边回忆边开心地笑着，好像很久很久都没有这么纯粹地开心过了。
column2: Hūn'àn de dēngguāng xià, wǒ hé péngyou kāishǐ liáotiānr. Tā jiǎng qǐ xiǎoxué de shíhou, bān li pō yǒu zhèngyìgǎn de nǚshēng Lǐ Fāngfāng rúhé jiànyì yǒngwéi, zài hóngshuǐ zhōng yīngyǒng jiù rén; wǒ gǎntàn chūzhōng shí, bān li nàge guìzúqì shízú de nánshēng, tā jiào…… ài, yìshí jìng wàng le tā jiào shénme míngzi. Tā shíliù suì dào le nóngcūn, cóng bōzhǒng kāishǐ xuéxí, hòulái zhǎngchéng le ge jīnghàn de hànzi, gǎigé kāifàng hòu dì-yī pī chéngbāo le tǔdì, jiùcǐ fājiā zhìfù, tā jiǎnzhí jiù shì yí dài rén zhōng de qíjì. Wǒmen xiǎngqǐ xiǎoxué de dìlǐ lǎoshī, jiǎngkè de shíhou zǒng huì dàichū xiē fāngyán, bān li tiáopí de nánshēng qiānfāng bǎijì gēn tā dǎoluàn, qì de lǎoshī lángbèi bùkān, nà huìr de wǒmen zhēn shì yòuzhì de kěxiào. Hái yǒu, zhōngxué wǒmen bān nàge liàoshì rúshén de Zhūgě Liàng…… Huǒchē shang, wǒmen biān huíyì biān kāixīn de xiàozhe, hǎoxiàng hěn jiǔ hěn jiǔ dōu méiyǒu zhème chúncuì de kāixīn guo le.
column3: Under the dim light, my friend and I started chatting. She talked about how, in primary school, Li Fangfang, a girl in our class with a strong sense of justice, bravely did the right thing and heroically saved someone in a flood. I reminisced about the boy in our junior high class who had such an aristocratic air—his name was... oh, for a moment I actually forgot what he was called. At sixteen he went to the countryside, started learning from sowing seeds, and later grew into a lean, capable man. After the reform and opening up, he was among the first to contract land, and from then on he built up his family fortune—he was simply a miracle of his generation. We remembered our primary-school geography teacher, who always slipped some dialect into her lessons; the naughty boys in our class did everything they could to make trouble for her, leaving her flustered and exasperated—how laughably childish we were back then. And there was that Zhuge Liang in our middle-school class who could predict everything... On the train, we laughed happily as we reminisced, as if we hadn't been this purely happy for a very, very long time.

column1: 说笑累了，朋友看着窗外，我则观察着周围的人们。坐我对面的像是一对双胞胎姐弟，他们正在聊家常。姐姐轻声细语，回顾着陈年往事：改革开放后的第一年，弟弟考上了大学，瞬间这消息成了方圆百里的爆炸性新闻。那一年过春节弟弟在学校没回家，家里节过得别提多冷清了，对联都懒得贴。虽然弟弟写信来拜年，可全家都觉得没了天伦之乐。那一年除夕、元宵节，不，是整个正月都过得没了生气，妈妈大年初一连寺庙都懒得去，天天感叹孩子翅膀硬了就要飞了，眼神中流露着失落。隔着过道坐着一对新婚的夫妇，新郎新娘一边给大家分发喜糖，一边说他们是旅行结婚的，顿时，整节车厢都热闹起来了，有人提议新郎新娘唱支歌，大家立刻鼓掌响应，那新郎一看就是个老实人，脸憋得通红，说他是社区物业干维修的，就会干活儿，不会唱歌，不过他媳妇不光贤惠，歌也唱得好，就让媳妇代表了。果然新娘张嘴就惊动了整节车厢，掌声、赞美声响成一片，现场简直就像联欢会一样，而我们对面角落里坐着的漫画家，早就用画笔记录下了眼前的一切。
column2: Shuōxiào lèi le, péngyou kànzhe chuāng wài, wǒ zé guānchá zhe zhōuwéi de rénmen. Zuò wǒ duìmiàn de xiàng shì yí duì shuāngbāotāi jiě dì, tāmen zhèngzài liáo jiācháng. Jiějie qīngshēng xìyǔ, huígùzhe chénnián wǎngshì: gǎigé kāifàng hòu de dì-yī nián, dìdi kǎoshàng le dàxué, shùnjiān zhè xiāoxi chéng le fāngyuán bǎi lǐ de bàozhàxìng xīnwén. Nà yì nián guò Chūnjié dìdi zài xuéxiào méi huí jiā, jiā li jié guò de biétí duō lěngqīng le, duìlián dōu lǎnde tiē. Suīrán dìdi xiě xìn lái bàinián, kě quánjiā dōu juéde méi le tiānlún zhī lè. Nà yì nián chúxī, Yuánxiāo Jié, bù, shì zhěnggè zhēngyuè dōu guò de méi le shēngqì, māma dànián chūyī lián sìmiào dōu lǎnde qù, tiāntiān gǎntàn háizi chìbǎng yìng le jiù yào fēi le, yǎnshén zhōng liúlùzhe shīluò. Gézhe guòdào zuòzhe yí duì xīnhūn de fūfù, xīnláng xīnniáng yìbiān gěi dàjiā fēnfā xǐtáng, yìbiān shuō tāmen shì lǚxíng jiéhūn de, dùnshí, zhěng jié chēxiāng dōu rènao qilai le, yǒu rén tíyì xīnláng xīnniáng chàng zhī gē, dàjiā lìkè gǔzhǎng xiǎngyìng, nà xīnláng yí kàn jiù shì ge lǎoshi rén, liǎn biē de tōnghóng, shuō tā shì shèqū wùyè gàn wéixiū de, jiù huì gàn huór, bú huì chàng gē, búguò tā xífu bùguāng xiánhuì, gē yě chàng de hǎo, jiù ràng xífu dàibiǎo le. Guǒrán xīnniáng zhāng zuǐ jiù jīngdòng le zhěng jié chēxiāng, zhǎngshēng, zànměi shēng xiǎngchéng yí piàn, xiànchǎng jiǎnzhí jiù xiàng liánhuānhuì yíyàng, ér wǒmen duìmiàn jiǎoluò li zuòzhe de mànhuàjiā, zǎo jiù yòng huàbǐ jìlù xia le yǎnqián de yíqiè.
column3: Tired of chatting and laughing, my friend gazed out the window while I observed the people around us. Sitting opposite me seemed to be a pair of twins, an older sister and younger brother, chatting about family matters. The sister, speaking softly, looked back on events of long ago: in the first year after the reform and opening up, her brother got into university, and instantly the news became a sensation for a hundred li around. That year he stayed at school over the Spring Festival and didn't come home, and the holiday at home was unbelievably bleak—they couldn't even be bothered to put up the couplets. Although he wrote a letter with New Year's greetings, the whole family felt the joy of family togetherness was gone. That year, New Year's Eve, the Lantern Festival—no, the entire first lunar month—passed lifelessly. On New Year's Day, Mom couldn't even be bothered to go to the temple; every day she sighed that once a child's wings grow strong, he flies away, with a look of loss in her eyes. Across the aisle sat a newlywed couple. While handing out wedding candy to everyone, the bride and groom said they were on a travel wedding, and at once the whole carriage came alive. Someone suggested the couple sing a song, and everyone immediately applauded in support. The groom was obviously an honest sort; his face turned bright red as he said he did maintenance for a residential property management office—he only knew how to work, not sing—but his wife was not only kind and virtuous, she was a good singer too, so he'd let her represent them. Sure enough, as soon as the bride opened her mouth she stunned the whole carriage. Applause and praise rang out all around, and the scene was just like a gala party, while the cartoonist sitting in the corner across from us had long since recorded everything before our eyes with his pen.

column1: 我和朋友不由得感叹，现代交通的确高效，人们随意打发着路上的时间，仓促间投入目的地的怀抱，早就忘了其实沿途的风景也是旅途的一部分，人和人之间无拘无束的交流也是人生最宝贵的财富。若不如此，我们又怎么会读到古人在那一束月光，一叶小舟，或者在那青山绿水间所寄托的情感呢！
column2: Wǒ hé péngyou bùyóude gǎntàn, xiàndài jiāotōng díquè gāoxiào, rénmen suíyì dǎfazhe lù shang de shíjiān, cāngcù jiān tóurù mùdìdì de huáibào, zǎo jiù wàng le qíshí yántú de fēngjǐng yě shì lǚtú de yí bùfen, rén hé rén zhījiān wújū wúshù de jiāoliú yě shì rénshēng zuì bǎoguì de cáifù. Ruò bù rúcǐ, wǒmen yòu zěnme huì dú dào gǔrén zài nà yí shù yuèguāng, yí yè xiǎozhōu, huòzhě zài nà qīngshān lǜshuǐ jiān suǒ jìtuō de qínggǎn ne!
column3: My friend and I couldn't help sighing: modern transportation is indeed efficient. People casually kill time on the road and rush hastily into the arms of their destination, having long forgotten that the scenery along the way is actually part of the journey, and that free and easy communication between people is life's most precious treasure. If it weren't so, how could we ever read the feelings the ancients poured into a beam of moonlight, a small boat, or green mountains and clear waters!

column1: 几十年前，北京街头远不及今天繁华。清晨，朝霞还没铺满天空，一位衣着朴素、性情温和的老人，坐着一辆破旧的公共汽车去上班。到站了，他缓慢地从车上走下来，走过他熟悉的大街小巷，步行到故宫博物院。他就是著名的古陶瓷收藏家、鉴定家孙瀛洲。
column2: Jǐshí nián qián, Běijīng jiētóu yuǎn bù jí jīntiān fánhuá. Qīngchén, zhāoxiá hái méi pūmǎn tiānkōng, yí wèi yīzhuó pǔsù, xìngqíng wēnhé de lǎorén, zuòzhe yí liàng pòjiù de gōnggòng qìchē qù shàngbān. Dào zhàn le, tā huǎnmàn de cóng chē shang zǒu xialai, zǒuguò tā shúxī de dàjiē xiǎoxiàng, bùxíng dào Gùgōng Bówùyuàn. Tā jiù shì zhùmíng de gǔ táocí shōucángjiā, jiàndìngjiā Sūn Yíngzhōu.
column3: Several decades ago, Beijing's streets were nowhere near as bustling as they are today. Early in the morning, before the rosy clouds of dawn had filled the sky, a plainly dressed, mild-tempered old man rode a battered bus to work. At his stop he slowly stepped off and walked through the streets and alleys he knew so well to the Palace Museum. He was the famous collector and connoisseur of ancient ceramics, Sun Yingzhou.

column1: 对于孙瀛洲和他的家人来说，1956年是个值得记忆的年头，那一年孙瀛洲将自己精心收藏的3000余件文物无偿捐赠给了故宫博物院，其中的斗彩三秋杯更是格外引人注目。
column2: Duìyú Sūn Yíngzhōu hé tā de jiārén lái shuō, yī jiǔ wǔ liù nián shì ge zhíde jìyì de niántóu, nà yì nián Sūn Yíngzhōu jiāng zìjǐ jīngxīn shōucáng de sānqiān yú jiàn wénwù wúcháng juānzèng gěi le Gùgōng Bówùyuàn, qízhōng de dòucǎi sānqiūbēi gèng shì géwài yǐnrén zhùmù.
column3: For Sun Yingzhou and his family, 1956 was a year worth remembering. That year, Sun Yingzhou donated more than 3,000 cultural relics he had carefully collected to the Palace Museum free of charge, among which the doucai "Three Autumns" cups were especially eye-catching.

column1: 孙瀛洲的女儿孙女士至今仍记得当年的情景。那些日子，家里人来人往，络绎不绝，人们忙着对捐献的文物包装箱子。那晚，父亲把全家叫到一起，从准备捐出的几百盒珍贵文物中取出一个精致的小盒子，取出两个小瓷杯给全家看。他说这是咱家最值钱的东西，故宫里也没有，明天就捐给故宫了，今天让你们看看。父亲说话时脸上充满了自豪。
column2: Sūn Yíngzhōu de nǚ'ér Sūn nǚshì zhìjīn réng jìde dāngnián de qíngjǐng. Nàxiē rìzi, jiā li rénlái rénwǎng, luòyì bùjué, rénmen mángzhe duì juānxiàn de wénwù bāozhuāng xiāngzi. Nà wǎn, fùqin bǎ quánjiā jiào dào yìqǐ, cóng zhǔnbèi juānchū de jǐbǎi hé zhēnguì wénwù zhōng qǔchū yí ge jīngzhì de xiǎo hézi, qǔchū liǎng ge xiǎo cíbēi gěi quánjiā kàn. Tā shuō zhè shì zán jiā zuì zhíqián de dōngxi, Gùgōng li yě méiyǒu, míngtiān jiù juān gěi Gùgōng le, jīntiān ràng nǐmen kànkan. Fùqin shuōhuà shí liǎn shang chōngmǎn le zìháo.
column3: Sun Yingzhou's daughter, Ms. Sun, still remembers the scene from back then. In those days, people came and went at home in an endless stream, busy packing the donated relics into crates. That evening, her father gathered the whole family together, took an exquisite little box out of the several hundred boxes of precious relics he was preparing to donate, and took out two small porcelain cups to show everyone. He said this was the most valuable thing in the family—even the Palace Museum didn't have one—and that tomorrow it would be donated to the museum, so today he'd let them have a look. As he spoke, his face was full of pride.

column1: 大家专注地看着父亲手里那对造型秀巧，杯体轻灵、洁白的斗彩瓷杯：杯体色调柔和宁静，搭配的图案是两只在山石花草间飞舞的蝴蝶，淡雅清爽，赏心悦目。相传这对杯子是当年皇帝专门下旨烧制的，不是烧给皇后，而是烧给一位爱妃。当时共烧成5对，选出这一对后，其余4对全部销毁，并将烧制杯子的手艺人处死，烧制工艺就此失传，而这对凝聚着先人智慧结晶的杯子也就成了存世孤品。
column2: Dàjiā zhuānzhù de kànzhe fùqin shǒu li nà duì zàoxíng xiùqiǎo, bēitǐ qīnglíng, jiébái de dòucǎi cíbēi: bēitǐ sèdiào róuhé níngjìng, dāpèi de tú'àn shì liǎng zhī zài shānshí huācǎo jiān fēiwǔ de húdié, dànyǎ qīngshuǎng, shǎngxīn yuèmù. Xiāngchuán zhè duì bēizi shì dāngnián huángdì zhuānmén xià zhǐ shāozhì de, bú shì shāo gěi huánghòu, ér shì shāo gěi yí wèi àifēi. Dāngshí gòng shāochéng wǔ duì, xuǎnchū zhè yí duì hòu, qíyú sì duì quánbù xiāohuǐ, bìng jiāng shāozhì bēizi de shǒuyìrén chǔsǐ, shāozhì gōngyì jiùcǐ shīchuán, ér zhè duì níngjùzhe xiānrén zhìhuì jiéjīng de bēizi yě jiù chéng le cúnshì gūpǐn.
column3: Everyone gazed intently at the pair of doucai porcelain cups in their father's hand—delicate in shape, light and pure white: the cups' colors were soft and tranquil, decorated with two butterflies dancing among rocks, flowers, and grass—elegant, fresh, and a delight to the eye. Legend has it that the emperor of the time issued a special decree to have these cups fired, not for the empress but for a favorite concubine. Five pairs were fired in all; after this pair was chosen, the remaining four were all destroyed and the artisans who made them were put to death, so the firing technique was lost from then on, and this pair of cups—the crystallization of our ancestors' wisdom—became the only one of its kind in existence.

column1: 也许有人要问，这位孙瀛洲到底什么来历？家藏竟然如此丰厚？
column2: Yěxǔ yǒu rén yào wèn, zhè wèi Sūn Yíngzhōu dàodǐ shénme láilì? Jiā cáng jìngrán rúcǐ fēnghòu?
column3: Some may ask: what exactly was this Sun Yingzhou's background? How could his family collection be so rich?

column1: 孙瀛洲的籍贯是河北，他13岁到北京，在古玩店做学徒、伙计，之后做过采购、副经理。1923年他自己创业，开办了古玩店。由于经营有方，又收藏有大量珍贵文物，孙瀛洲在当时的古董经营者中很有威望。
column2: Sūn Yíngzhōu de jíguàn shì Héběi, tā shísān suì dào Běijīng, zài gǔwándiàn zuò xuétú, huǒji, zhīhòu zuòguo cǎigòu, fù jīnglǐ. Yī jiǔ èr sān nián tā zìjǐ chuàngyè, kāibàn le gǔwándiàn. Yóuyú jīngyíng yǒu fāng, yòu shōucáng yǒu dàliàng zhēnguì wénwù, Sūn Yíngzhōu zài dāngshí de gǔdǒng jīngyíngzhě zhōng hěn yǒu wēiwàng.
column3: Sun Yingzhou's ancestral home was Hebei. He came to Beijing at 13 and worked as an apprentice and shop assistant in an antique shop, later serving as a purchaser and deputy manager. In 1923 he started his own business and opened an antique shop. Because he ran it well and also had a large collection of precious relics, Sun Yingzhou enjoyed great prestige among the antique dealers of his day.

column1: 孙女士感慨道，尽管当年家中私藏丰厚，但他们生活却非常简朴，甚至有些吝啬，举个例子吧，过年时孩子们吃的糖葫芦都是孙瀛洲自制的。他对孩子尚且如此，对自己的那份节俭也就不难想象了。可是，为了收购绝世珍品斗彩三秋杯，他却是不惜重金。正是这种对陶瓷执着的热爱，使孙瀛洲收藏了数量可观的陶瓷精品。
column2: Sūn nǚshì gǎnkǎi dào, jǐnguǎn dāngnián jiā zhōng sīcáng fēnghòu, dàn tāmen shēnghuó què fēicháng jiǎnpǔ, shènzhì yǒuxiē lìnsè, jǔ ge lìzi ba, guònián shí háizimen chī de tánghúlu dōu shì Sūn Yíngzhōu zìzhì de. Tā duì háizi shàngqiě rúcǐ, duì zìjǐ de nà fèn jiéjiǎn yě jiù bù nán xiǎngxiàng le. Kěshì, wèile shōugòu juéshì zhēnpǐn dòucǎi sānqiūbēi, tā què shì bùxī zhòngjīn. Zhèng shì zhè zhǒng duì táocí zhízhuó de rè'ài, shǐ Sūn Yíngzhōu shōucáng le shùliàng kěguān de táocí jīngpǐn.
column3: Ms. Sun sighed with emotion that although the family's private collection was rich, they lived very frugally—even a bit stingily. For example, the candied haws the children ate at New Year were all homemade by Sun Yingzhou. If he was like this even with his children, his own thriftiness isn't hard to imagine. Yet to acquire the peerless treasure, the doucai "Three Autumns" cups, he spared no expense. It was precisely this devoted love of ceramics that enabled Sun Yingzhou to collect a considerable number of fine ceramic pieces.

column1: 孙瀛洲的子女们说，父亲来到这个世界好像只有一个神圣的使命——保护文物。他全身心投入到文物当中，生活在文物当中。有人问他们怎样看待当年父亲捐赠的义举？要是在今天，你们这些做家属的会支持父亲吗？他们回答：“今天我们也会拥护父亲的选择，就像父亲捐出这些文物不是为了表彰，不是为了荣誉，不是为了奖励，也没想得到什么称号一样，这些东西本就属于国家，属于全人类。”孙家后人很争气，他们不想沾父亲的光，父亲留给他们最大的财富就是高洁的品质。
column2: Sūn Yíngzhōu de zǐnǚmen shuō, fùqin láidào zhège shìjiè hǎoxiàng zhǐ yǒu yí ge shénshèng de shǐmìng—bǎohù wénwù. Tā quánshēnxīn tóurù dào wénwù dāngzhōng, shēnghuó zài wénwù dāngzhōng. Yǒu rén wèn tāmen zěnyàng kàndài dāngnián fùqin juānzèng de yìjǔ? Yàoshi zài jīntiān, nǐmen zhèxiē zuò jiāshǔ de huì zhīchí fùqin ma? Tāmen huídá: "Jīntiān wǒmen yě huì yōnghù fùqin de xuǎnzé, jiù xiàng fùqin juānchū zhèxiē wénwù bú shì wèile biǎozhāng, bú shì wèile róngyù, bú shì wèile jiǎnglì, yě méi xiǎng dédào shénme chēnghào yíyàng, zhèxiē dōngxi běn jiù shǔyú guójiā, shǔyú quán rénlèi." Sūn jiā hòurén hěn zhēngqì, tāmen bù xiǎng zhān fùqin de guāng, fùqin liú gěi tāmen zuì dà de cáifù jiù shì gāojié de pǐnzhì.
column3: Sun Yingzhou's children say their father seemed to have come into this world with only one sacred mission—protecting cultural relics. He threw himself body and soul into relics and lived among them. Someone asked them how they viewed their father's generous act of donation back then: if it were today, would they, as his family, support him? They answered, "Today we would still back our father's choice. Just as he didn't donate these relics for commendation, honor, or reward, and never thought of getting any title, these things belonged to the nation and to all humanity in the first place." Sun's descendants have done him proud: they don't want to ride on their father's coattails, and the greatest treasure he left them is his noble character.

column1: 1956年，孙瀛洲受聘于故宫博物院从事古陶瓷研究、鉴定工作。他很乐意接受这份工作，工作中更是精益求精。孙瀛洲的弟子讲过这样一件事：一次，孙瀛洲让人们把不同时期的瓷器放在一起，其中当然有真品，也有仿品。他背过身，人们打乱摆放次序，他闭着眼睛，转过身来，只用手摸，就准确地一一说出了各件文物的朝代、名称。
column2: Yī jiǔ wǔ liù nián, Sūn Yíngzhōu shòupìn yú Gùgōng Bówùyuàn cóngshì gǔ táocí yánjiū, jiàndìng gōngzuò. Tā hěn lèyì jiēshòu zhè fèn gōngzuò, gōngzuò zhōng gèng shì jīngyì qiújīng. Sūn Yíngzhōu de dìzǐ jiǎngguo zhèyàng yí jiàn shì: yí cì, Sūn Yíngzhōu ràng rénmen bǎ bùtóng shíqī de cíqì fàng zài yìqǐ, qízhōng dāngrán yǒu zhēnpǐn, yě yǒu fǎngpǐn. Tā bèiguo shēn, rénmen dǎluàn bǎifàng cìxù, tā bìzhe yǎnjing, zhuǎn guo shēn lai, zhǐ yòng shǒu mō, jiù zhǔnquè de yīyī shuōchū le gè jiàn wénwù de cháodài, míngchēng.
column3: In 1956, Sun Yingzhou was hired by the Palace Museum to research and authenticate ancient ceramics. He was very happy to take the job and strove for perfection in his work. One of his disciples told this story: once, Sun Yingzhou had people put porcelain from different periods together—genuine pieces as well as imitations, of course. He turned his back, people shuffled the order, and then, with his eyes closed, he turned around and, just by touching them with his hands, accurately named the dynasty and name of each piece one by one.

column1: 在历来假货泛滥的文物界，鉴定家孙瀛洲就是一张最有威信的名片。当代社会，被称为“专家”容易，称为“著名专家”也不难，但称得上“大家”的不多，孙瀛洲就是人人心服口服的国家级别的“大家”。
column2: Zài lìlái jiǎhuò fànlàn de wénwùjiè, jiàndìngjiā Sūn Yíngzhōu jiù shì yì zhāng zuì yǒu wēixìn de míngpiàn. Dāngdài shèhuì, bèi chēngwéi "zhuānjiā" róngyì, chēngwéi "zhùmíng zhuānjiā" yě bù nán, dàn chēng de shàng "dàjiā" de bù duō, Sūn Yíngzhōu jiù shì rénrén xīnfú kǒufú de guójiā jíbié de "dàjiā".
column3: In the world of cultural relics, long flooded with fakes, the connoisseur Sun Yingzhou was the most trusted name of all. In today's society it's easy to be called an "expert," and not hard to be called a "famous expert," but few deserve to be called a "master"—and Sun Yingzhou is a national-level "master" whom everyone acknowledges with sincere admiration.

column1: 孙瀛洲在故宫博物院工作期间将一生所学毫无保留地传授给学生，培养出一批文物鉴定人才，有的已成为当今古陶瓷鉴定的泰斗。
column2: Sūn Yíngzhōu zài Gùgōng Bówùyuàn gōngzuò qījiān jiāng yìshēng suǒ xué háowú bǎoliú de chuánshòu gěi xuésheng, péiyǎng chū yì pī wénwù jiàndìng réncái, yǒude yǐ chéngwéi dāngjīn gǔ táocí jiàndìng de tàidǒu.
column3: While working at the Palace Museum, Sun Yingzhou passed on everything he had learned in his life to his students without reservation, training a group of relic-authentication experts, some of whom have become today's leading authorities on authenticating ancient ceramics.

column1: 年画的起源
column2: Niánhuà de qǐyuán
column3: The Origin of New Year Pictures

column1: 年画是中国画的一种，始于古代的门神画。
column2: Niánhuà shì Zhōngguóhuà de yì zhǒng, shǐ yú gǔdài de ménshénhuà.
column3: New Year pictures are a type of Chinese painting that began with the door-god pictures of ancient times.

column1: 有文献记载：传说很久以前，有一对兄弟，专门监督百鬼，发现罪恶的鬼就捆绑起来，无须揭露恶行，直接去喂老虎。于是有人在门上画上他们兄弟二人的像，用以防鬼，这就是最早的门神画。
column2: Yǒu wénxiàn jìzǎi: chuánshuō hěn jiǔ yǐqián, yǒu yí duì xiōngdì, zhuānmén jiāndū bǎi guǐ, fāxiàn zuì'è de guǐ jiù kǔnbǎng qilai, wúxū jiēlù èxíng, zhíjiē qù wèi lǎohǔ. Yúshì yǒu rén zài mén shang huà shang tāmen xiōngdì èr rén de xiàng, yòngyǐ fáng guǐ, zhè jiù shì zuì zǎo de ménshénhuà.
column3: According to historical records, legend has it that long ago there were two brothers whose special job was to watch over all the ghosts; whenever they found an evil ghost, they tied it up and, without even needing to expose its misdeeds, fed it straight to the tigers. So people painted portraits of the two brothers on their doors to ward off ghosts—these were the earliest door-god pictures.

column1: 随着唐宋两朝经济的发展，文化的昌盛以及民间绘画水平的提高，门神画的内容得以拓展，反映世俗生活题材的作品进入了这一领域。之后，有清朝学者在论述这类画作时正式使用了“年画”一词，自此，以驱逐凶邪、祝福新年吉祥喜庆为内容的画儿就叫年画了。
column2: Suízhe Táng Sòng liǎng cháo jīngjì de fāzhǎn, wénhuà de chāngshèng yǐjí mínjiān huìhuà shuǐpíng de tígāo, ménshénhuà de nèiróng déyǐ tuòzhǎn, fǎnyìng shìsú shēnghuó tícái de zuòpǐn jìnrù le zhè yí lǐngyù. Zhīhòu, yǒu Qīngcháo xuézhě zài lùnshù zhè lèi huàzuò shí zhèngshì shǐyòng le "niánhuà" yì cí, zìcǐ, yǐ qūzhú xiōngxié, zhùfú xīnnián jíxiáng xǐqìng wéi nèiróng de huàr jiù jiào niánhuà le.
column3: With the economic development of the Tang and Song dynasties, the flourishing of culture, and the rising level of folk painting, the content of door-god pictures expanded, and works depicting everyday secular life entered the field. Later, a Qing dynasty scholar formally used the term "New Year picture" when discussing such paintings, and from then on, pictures whose content was driving away evil and wishing for an auspicious, joyful new year were called New Year pictures.

column1: 木版年画
column2: Mùbǎn niánhuà
column3: Woodblock New Year Pictures

column1: 造纸技术的发明是人类文化发展史上一个重要的里程碑。
column2: Zàozhǐ jìshù de fāmíng shì rénlèi wénhuà fāzhǎn shǐ shang yí ge zhòngyào de lǐchéngbēi.
column3: The invention of papermaking was an important milestone in the history of human cultural development.

column1: 有了纸，书写就需要墨水儿，于是有人发明了墨；字画、书信上需要盖章，于是印章开始流行；碑刻、拓印技术被广泛运用，于是有人联想到：这些技术结合起来，不就能印出书来吗！人们尝试把印章扩大成一张纸那么大，叫作“版”，然后把书的内容刻在版上，在版上涂抹上墨，把纸铺到上面，用刷子均匀地刷印，最后将纸揭起，印品就出来了，这就是最早的雕版印刷。虽然雕版印刷中雕刻版面需要大量的人工和材料，但雕版完成后一经开印，就显示出空前的高效率和印刷量大的优越性。
column2: Yǒu le zhǐ, shūxiě jiù xūyào mòshuǐr, yúshì yǒu rén fāmíng le mò; zìhuà, shūxìn shang xūyào gài zhāng, yúshì yìnzhāng kāishǐ liúxíng; bēikè, tàyìn jìshù bèi guǎngfàn yùnyòng, yúshì yǒu rén liánxiǎng dào: zhèxiē jìshù jiéhé qilai, bú jiù néng yìn chū shū lai ma! Rénmen chángshì bǎ yìnzhāng kuòdà chéng yì zhāng zhǐ nàme dà, jiàozuò "bǎn", ránhòu bǎ shū de nèiróng kè zài bǎn shang, zài bǎn shang túmǒ shang mò, bǎ zhǐ pū dào shàngmiàn, yòng shuāzi jūnyún de shuāyìn, zuìhòu jiāng zhǐ jiē qilai, yìnpǐn jiù chūlai le, zhè jiù shì zuì zǎo de diāobǎn yìnshuā. Suīrán diāobǎn yìnshuā zhōng diāokè bǎnmiàn xūyào dàliàng de réngōng hé cáiliào, dàn diāobǎn wánchéng hòu yì jīng kāi yìn, jiù xiǎnshì chū kōngqián de gāo xiàolǜ hé yìnshuāliàng dà de yōuyuèxìng.
column3: Once there was paper, writing required ink, so someone invented ink; calligraphy, paintings, and letters needed to be stamped, so seals came into fashion; stele carving and rubbing techniques were widely used, and so it occurred to someone: if these techniques were combined, couldn't books be printed! People tried enlarging a seal to the size of a sheet of paper, called a "block," then carved the contents of a book onto it, spread ink over the block, laid paper on top, brushed it evenly, and finally peeled the paper off—and out came the printed page. This was the earliest woodblock printing. Although carving the blocks required a great deal of labor and material, once a block was finished and printing began, it showed the unprecedented advantages of high efficiency and large print runs.

column1: 单色印品终究不能满足人们的审美需求，之后就有了彩色套印技术。人们把这种技术运用到年画制作上，木版彩色套印年画就此诞生。
column2: Dānsè yìnpǐn zhōngjiū bù néng mǎnzú rénmen de shěnměi xūqiú, zhīhòu jiù yǒu le cǎisè tàoyìn jìshù. Rénmen bǎ zhè zhǒng jìshù yùnyòng dào niánhuà zhìzuò shang, mùbǎn cǎisè tàoyìn niánhuà jiùcǐ dànshēng.
column3: Single-color prints ultimately couldn't satisfy people's aesthetic needs, and later came color overprinting. People applied this technique to making New Year pictures, and so woodblock color-overprinted New Year pictures were born.

column1: 宋明两代，木版年画从问世走向成熟，之后走进了百姓生活，以至过年贴年画成为了一种风尚，仿佛没有年画，没有烟花爆竹，没有春联就不算过年，而寄托着百姓美好愿望的年画，也为春节增添了浓浓的年味。当时的另一盛况是，家族式的年画印制场所遍及全国各地。这期间，年画的内容也从威武的门神，扩展到期盼丰收、恭喜发财、连年有余的吉庆画，再到历史故事、戏曲人物、民间笑话、寓言和神话，内容无所不包。年画成了文化交流、道德教育、信仰传承的载体与工具，是老百姓喜闻乐见的文化艺术形式。
column2: Sòng Míng liǎng dài, mùbǎn niánhuà cóng wènshì zǒuxiàng chéngshú, zhīhòu zǒujìn le bǎixìng shēnghuó, yǐzhì guònián tiē niánhuà chéngwéi le yì zhǒng fēngshàng, fǎngfú méiyǒu niánhuà, méiyǒu yānhuā bàozhú, méiyǒu chūnlián jiù bú suàn guònián, ér jìtuōzhe bǎixìng měihǎo yuànwàng de niánhuà, yě wèi Chūnjié zēngtiān le nóngnóng de niánwèi. Dāngshí de lìng yí shèngkuàng shì, jiāzú shì de niánhuà yìnzhì chǎngsuǒ biànjí quánguó gèdì. Zhè qījiān, niánhuà de nèiróng yě cóng wēiwǔ de ménshén, kuòzhǎn dào qīpàn fēngshōu, gōngxǐ fācái, liánnián yǒu yú de jíqìnghuà, zài dào lìshǐ gùshi, xìqǔ rénwù, mínjiān xiàohua, yùyán hé shénhuà, nèiróng wú suǒ bù bāo. Niánhuà chéng le wénhuà jiāoliú, dàodé jiàoyù, xìnyǎng chuánchéng de zàitǐ yǔ gōngjù, shì lǎobǎixìng xǐwén lèjiàn de wénhuà yìshù xíngshì.
column3: During the Song and Ming dynasties, woodblock New Year pictures went from first appearing to maturity, and then entered ordinary people's lives, so much so that putting up New Year pictures became a custom—as if without New Year pictures, fireworks and firecrackers, and spring couplets, it wasn't really New Year. New Year pictures, carrying people's good wishes, also added a rich festive flavor to the Spring Festival. Another grand sight of the time was that family-run New Year picture printing workshops spread all over the country. During this period, the content of New Year pictures expanded from mighty door gods to auspicious pictures wishing for a good harvest, prosperity, and abundance year after year, and further to historical stories, opera characters, folk jokes, fables, and myths—they covered everything. New Year pictures became a vehicle and tool for cultural exchange, moral education, and passing on beliefs, an art form the common people loved.

column1: 年画传人张光宁
column2: Niánhuà chuánrén Zhāng Guāngníng
column3: Zhang Guangning, Heir to the New Year Picture Tradition

column1: 第一次见到张光宁的木版年画，是在春节庙会上。在众多摊位中，他的两只木版彩色套印技术做成的布老虎神气极了。那虎翘着尾巴，神态逼真，身上装饰着彩绘花纹和盛开的花朵，全身散发着喜气。我问多少钱，他耸耸肩，对我说：“这是魏州虎。”言外之意是在告诉我这个外行，这虎可是系出名门。我心想：“魏州是哪儿？我不知道别人也未必知道，这算什么推销术？”
column2: Dì-yī cì jiàndào Zhāng Guāngníng de mùbǎn niánhuà, shì zài Chūnjié miàohuì shang. Zài zhòngduō tānwèi zhōng, tā de liǎng zhī mùbǎn cǎisè tàoyìn jìshù zuòchéng de bù lǎohǔ shénqi jí le. Nà hǔ qiàozhe wěiba, shéntài bīzhēn, shēn shang zhuāngshìzhe cǎihuì huāwén hé shèngkāi de huāduǒ, quánshēn sànfāzhe xǐqì. Wǒ wèn duōshao qián, tā sǒngsong jiān, duì wǒ shuō: "Zhè shì Wèizhōu hǔ." Yánwài zhī yì shì zài gàosu wǒ zhège wàiháng, zhè hǔ kě shì xì chū míngmén. Wǒ xīn xiǎng: "Wèizhōu shì nǎr? Wǒ bù zhīdào biérén yě wèibì zhīdào, zhè suàn shénme tuīxiāoshù?"
column3: The first time I saw Zhang Guangning's woodblock New Year pictures was at a Spring Festival temple fair. Among the many stalls, his two cloth tigers made with woodblock color overprinting looked tremendously spirited. The tigers had their tails raised and lifelike expressions, their bodies decorated with painted patterns and flowers in full bloom, radiating festive joy all over. I asked how much they cost; he shrugged and said to me, "This is a Weizhou tiger." The implication was to tell me, a layman, that this tiger came from a distinguished lineage. I thought to myself, "Where is Weizhou? If I don't know, others probably don't either—what kind of sales technique is this?"

column1: 这是他给我留下的第一印象。
column2: Zhè shì tā gěi wǒ liú xia de dì-yī yìnxiàng.
column3: That was my first impression of him.

column1: “这个卖年画的不像个商人”，这是他给我留下的第二印象。当你和他讨价还价的时候，他立刻就变得不好意思起来，说话吞吞吐吐。什么“这是纯手工的”“残次品不可避免”这些现成的“谢绝”还价的理由他一条也说不出来，相反却啰啰唆唆地总想和你讨论木版年画中深厚的文化底蕴。
column2: Zhège mài niánhuà de bú xiàng ge shāngrén, zhè shì tā gěi wǒ liú xia de dì-èr yìnxiàng. Dāng nǐ hé tā tǎojià huánjià de shíhou, tā lìkè jiù biànde bù hǎoyìsi qilai, shuōhuà tūntūntǔtǔ. Shénme "zhè shì chún shǒugōng de" "cáncìpǐn bùkě bìmiǎn" zhèxiē xiànchéng de "xièjué" huánjià de lǐyóu tā yì tiáo yě shuō bu chū, xiāngfǎn què luōluōsuōsuō de zǒng xiǎng hé nǐ tǎolùn mùbǎn niánhuà zhōng shēnhòu de wénhuà dǐyùn.
column3: This New Year picture seller isn't much of a businessman—that was my second impression of him. When you haggle with him, he immediately gets embarrassed and starts stammering. Ready-made excuses for "declining" to bargain, like "this is all handmade" or "defective pieces are unavoidable"—he can't come up with a single one. Instead, he rambles on, always wanting to discuss with you the deep cultural heritage of woodblock New Year pictures.

column1: 相识久了才知道，他在年画的故乡出生、长大，从小就画年画，基本功扎实，后来又对年画的构图创作、人物塑造、雕版手法、颜料加工等进行了广泛的研究。当他的作品逐步被市场认可后，他又不满足了，中国年画虽不分派别，但不同地区的年画各有所长，都值得学习借鉴。于是，他再接再厉，数年间走遍了全国各大年画产地，与同行进行广泛的交流。不仅如此，参加民俗文化巡展，走进大学和师生就相关主题进行研讨，交流艺术心得，他从不缺席。
column2: Xiāngshí jiǔ le cái zhīdào, tā zài niánhuà de gùxiāng chūshēng, zhǎngdà, cóngxiǎo jiù huà niánhuà, jīběngōng zhāshi, hòulái yòu duì niánhuà de gòutú chuàngzuò, rénwù sùzào, diāobǎn shǒufǎ, yánliào jiāgōng děng jìnxíng le guǎngfàn de yánjiū. Dāng tā de zuòpǐn zhúbù bèi shìchǎng rènkě hòu, tā yòu bù mǎnzú le, Zhōngguó niánhuà suī bù fēn pàibié, dàn bùtóng dìqū de niánhuà gè yǒu suǒ cháng, dōu zhíde xuéxí jièjiàn. Yúshì, tā zàijiē zàilì, shù nián jiān zǒubiàn le quánguó gè dà niánhuà chǎndì, yǔ tóngháng jìnxíng guǎngfàn de jiāoliú. Bùjǐn rúcǐ, cānjiā mínsú wénhuà xúnzhǎn, zǒujìn dàxué hé shīshēng jiù xiāngguān zhǔtí jìnxíng yántǎo, jiāoliú yìshù xīndé, tā cóng bù quēxí.
column3: Only after knowing him for a long time did I learn that he was born and raised in the hometown of New Year pictures and had painted them since childhood, with solid basic skills. Later he did extensive research on the composition, characterization, block-carving techniques, and pigment processing of New Year pictures. Once his work gradually gained market recognition, he still wasn't satisfied: though Chinese New Year pictures aren't divided into schools, those from different regions each have their own strengths, all worth learning from. So he kept pressing on, and over several years traveled to all the major New Year picture centers in the country, exchanging ideas widely with his peers. Not only that—whether it was joining touring folk-culture exhibitions or going into universities to discuss related topics with teachers and students and share artistic insights, he never missed one.

column1: 张光宁一年到头真够忙的，可他总是干劲十足。他曾真诚地说：“年画占据了我生命的全部，我喜欢它，热爱它，靠它生活，也在努力探索它、发展它。”是啊，愈是热爱，他就愈是执着。他已确立了自己的目标——传播他喜爱的这一民俗文化。他的信念就是拓展年画的内容，使其雅俗共赏，为更多民众所喜爱，虽然任重道远，也不会一帆风顺，但他一定会坚持下去。
column2: Zhāng Guāngníng yì nián dào tóu zhēn gòu máng de, kě tā zǒngshì gànjìn shízú. Tā céng zhēnchéng de shuō: "Niánhuà zhànjù le wǒ shēngmìng de quánbù, wǒ xǐhuan tā, rè'ài tā, kào tā shēnghuó, yě zài nǔlì tànsuǒ tā, fāzhǎn tā." Shì a, yù shì rè'ài, tā jiù yù shì zhízhuó. Tā yǐ quèlì le zìjǐ de mùbiāo—chuánbō tā xǐ'ài de zhè yì mínsú wénhuà. Tā de xìnniàn jiù shì tuòzhǎn niánhuà de nèiróng, shǐ qí yǎsú gòngshǎng, wéi gèng duō mínzhòng suǒ xǐ'ài, suīrán rènzhòng dàoyuǎn, yě bú huì yìfān fēngshùn, dàn tā yídìng huì jiānchí xiaqu.
column3: Zhang Guangning is truly busy all year round, yet he's always full of drive. He once said sincerely, "New Year pictures take up my whole life. I like them, love them, make my living from them, and am working hard to explore and develop them." Indeed, the more he loves them, the more devoted he becomes. He has set his goal—to spread this folk culture he loves. His conviction is to expand the content of New Year pictures so that both refined and popular audiences can enjoy them and more people come to love them. Although the task is heavy and the road long, and it won't be all smooth sailing, he will certainly keep going.

column1: 中国藏书的历史很长，有2000多年了，有官方藏书，也有私人藏书。唐代有人把藏书的地方称作书院，之后各种书院层出不穷，甚至有人把自己的书屋也命名为书院。
column2: Zhōngguó cángshū de lìshǐ hěn cháng, yǒu liǎngqiān duō nián le, yǒu guānfāng cángshū, yě yǒu sīrén cángshū. Tángdài yǒu rén bǎ cángshū de dìfang chēngzuò shūyuàn, zhīhòu gè zhǒng shūyuàn céngchū bùqióng, shènzhì yǒu rén bǎ zìjǐ de shūwū yě mìngmíng wéi shūyuàn.
column3: China has a long history of book collecting, more than 2,000 years, with both official and private collections. In the Tang dynasty some people called the places where books were kept shuyuan (academies); after that all kinds of academies sprang up one after another, and some people even named their own studies shuyuan.

column1: 时光流转，书院渐渐发展成了藏书、教学和研究相结合的教育机构。比如，东佳书院就是中国书院史上最早拥有学田、订有规章制度、收有学生的私办书院。它前后存在了千余年，名字更换了三四次，直到清朝末年，书院制度终止，东佳书院改成了学校。可以这样说，萌芽于唐，完备于宋，废止于清的东佳书院是中国书院制度的一个缩影。
column2: Shíguāng liúzhuǎn, shūyuàn jiànjiàn fāzhǎn chéngle cángshū, jiàoxué hé yánjiū xiāng jiéhé de jiàoyù jīgòu. Bǐrú, Dōngjiā Shūyuàn jiù shì Zhōngguó shūyuàn shǐ shang zuì zǎo yōngyǒu xuétián, dìng yǒu guīzhāng zhìdù, shōu yǒu xuésheng de sī bàn shūyuàn. Tā qiánhòu cúnzàile qiān yú nián, míngzi gēnghuànle sān sì cì, zhídào Qīngcháo mònián, shūyuàn zhìdù zhōngzhǐ, Dōngjiā Shūyuàn gǎichéngle xuéxiào. Kěyǐ zhèyàng shuō, méngyá yú Táng, wánbèi yú Sòng, fèizhǐ yú Qīng de Dōngjiā Shūyuàn shì Zhōngguó shūyuàn zhìdù de yí ge suōyǐng.
column3: As time went on, the academies gradually developed into educational institutions combining book collecting, teaching and research. For example, Dongjia Academy was the earliest private academy in the history of Chinese academies to own school land, set down rules and regulations, and enroll students. It existed for over a thousand years and changed its name three or four times, until at the end of the Qing dynasty the academy system came to an end and Dongjia Academy was turned into a school. It can be said that Dongjia Academy, which sprouted in the Tang, matured in the Song and was abolished in the Qing, is an epitome of China's academy system.

column1: 历史上的书院立足于人才培养。它把灵魂塑造看得和学问同等重要；提倡刻苦、严谨的治学精神；努力实践自由活泼的办学宗旨。书院的历史是中国古代教育史上的一份珍贵遗产。
column2: Lìshǐ shang de shūyuàn lìzú yú réncái péiyǎng. Tā bǎ línghún sùzào kàn de hé xuéwen tóngděng zhòngyào; tíchàng kèkǔ, yánjǐn de zhìxué jīngshén; nǔlì shíjiàn zìyóu huópo de bànxué zōngzhǐ. Shūyuàn de lìshǐ shì Zhōngguó gǔdài jiàoyù shǐ shang de yí fèn zhēnguì yíchǎn.
column3: The academies of history were grounded in cultivating talent. They regarded shaping the soul as equally important as learning; they advocated a diligent and rigorous spirit of scholarship; and they strove to practice a free and lively educational philosophy. The history of the academies is a precious legacy in the history of ancient Chinese education.

column1: 德业并重是书院自始至终的追求目标。翻开各时代书院颁布的《学规》就能发现，书院重视学问，更重视品德修养。比如，丽泽书院《学规》第一条大意是：凡是本书院的学子，都要孝顺长辈，敬爱兄长，为人忠诚，守信用。不顺从长辈，和兄弟不友善，与人不和睦，对朋友不忠诚，言行不一，擅以虚伪的言辞掩饰过失的无耻之徒，一经发现，本书院定不容纳。短短一段文字透露出这样的信息：书院在人文环境的治理上是有标准的，那就是树立正气，唾弃卑鄙、堕落的腐败行为。因此，有学问、有道德、有崇高的境界，就成为了古代知识分子立志终生攀登的道德高峰。
column2: Dé yè bìng zhòng shì shūyuàn zìshǐ zhìzhōng de zhuīqiú mùbiāo. Fānkāi gè shídài shūyuàn bānbù de "Xuéguī" jiù néng fāxiàn, shūyuàn zhòngshì xuéwen, gèng zhòngshì pǐndé xiūyǎng. Bǐrú, Lìzé Shūyuàn "Xuéguī" dì-yī tiáo dàyì shì: fánshì běn shūyuàn de xuézǐ, dōu yào xiàoshùn zhǎngbèi, jìng'ài xiōngzhǎng, wéirén zhōngchéng, shǒu xìnyòng. Bú shùncóng zhǎngbèi, hé xiōngdì bù yǒushàn, yǔ rén bù hémù, duì péngyou bù zhōngchéng, yánxíng bù yī, shàn yǐ xūwěi de yáncí yǎnshì guòshī de wúchǐ zhī tú, yìjīng fāxiàn, běn shūyuàn dìng bù róngnà. Duǎnduǎn yí duàn wénzì tòulù chū zhèyàng de xìnxī: shūyuàn zài rénwén huánjìng de zhìlǐ shang shì yǒu biāozhǔn de, nà jiù shì shùlì zhèngqì, tuòqì bēibǐ, duòluò de fǔbài xíngwéi. Yīncǐ, yǒu xuéwen, yǒu dàodé, yǒu chónggāo de jìngjiè, jiù chéngwéile gǔdài zhīshi fènzǐ lìzhì zhōngshēng pāndēng de dàodé gāofēng.
column3: Giving equal weight to virtue and learning was the goal the academies pursued from beginning to end. Open the "School Rules" issued by academies of any era and you will find that they valued learning, but valued moral cultivation even more. For example, the gist of the first article of Lize Academy's "School Rules" is: every student of this academy must be filial to elders, respect and love elder brothers, be loyal, and keep their word. Any shameless person who disobeys elders, is unfriendly to brothers, cannot get along with others, is disloyal to friends, whose words do not match deeds, or who presumes to cover up faults with false words, will not be tolerated by this academy once discovered. This short passage reveals the following message: the academies had standards for governing their cultural environment, namely to promote integrity and spurn base, degenerate and corrupt behavior. Thus having learning, morality and a lofty state of mind became the moral peak that ancient intellectuals resolved to climb all their lives.

column1: 提倡刻苦、严谨的治学精神是古代书院的共同特点。古代书院学术思想各有不同，但治学态度却极为相似，认为读书没有窍门，没有捷径，唯有发扬勤奋好学的精神，扎扎实实，一步一个脚印，才能做好学问。在学习方法上，提倡读书百遍，因为“书读百遍，其义自见”；提倡温故知新；提倡博学求精；提倡读书须有疑。
column2: Tíchàng kèkǔ, yánjǐn de zhìxué jīngshén shì gǔdài shūyuàn de gòngtóng tèdiǎn. Gǔdài shūyuàn xuéshù sīxiǎng gè yǒu bùtóng, dàn zhìxué tàidu què jíwéi xiāngsì, rènwéi dúshū méiyǒu qiàomén, méiyǒu jiéjìng, wéi yǒu fāyáng qínfèn hàoxué de jīngshén, zhāzhāshíshí, yí bù yí ge jiǎoyìn, cái néng zuòhǎo xuéwen. Zài xuéxí fāngfǎ shang, tíchàng dúshū bǎi biàn, yīnwèi "shū dú bǎi biàn, qí yì zì xiàn"; tíchàng wēngù zhīxīn; tíchàng bóxué qiú jīng; tíchàng dúshū xū yǒu yí.
column3: Advocating a diligent and rigorous spirit of scholarship was a common feature of ancient academies. Their academic thought differed, but their attitudes toward scholarship were strikingly similar: they held that there is no trick or shortcut to study, and that only by carrying forward a spirit of diligence and love of learning, working solidly, one step at a time, can one do scholarship well. As for study methods, they advocated reading a book a hundred times, because "read a book a hundred times and its meaning will reveal itself"; they advocated reviewing the old to learn the new; they advocated broad learning while seeking depth; and they advocated that one must question while reading.

column1: 书院在办学方法上，努力实践自由活泼的办学思想。首先，书院本着贫富平等的原则，敞开大门，招收平民子弟入学，这在当时确实是令人震撼的开明之举。其二，书院重视自修和研究，在读书的过程中倡议自行思考，杜绝外来因素的干涉，也不会过多过问，以便开发学生的自主学习能力，激发学生的主动性和创造性。其三，鉴于一个人的知识是有限的，大家的知识是无限的，个人解决不了的问题，在众人的智慧面前就不是问题，书院倡导互相切磋、互相学习。其四，鼓励师生之间相互质疑，形成探讨争辩、求真求实的学习风气。另外，重视观点的多元化，开展不同观点的论辩、交流，也是书院提倡的。观点对立、有分歧不要紧，开放、保守也无关紧要，书院主张不同学派、不同主张之间的争辩与较量，为此书院设立了讲演辩论制度，类似今天的“论坛”。这种学术活动很受欢迎，学子们学习热情高涨，相互激励，取长补短，共同进步。
column2: Shūyuàn zài bànxué fāngfǎ shang, nǔlì shíjiàn zìyóu huópo de bànxué sīxiǎng. Shǒuxiān, shūyuàn běnzhe pín fù píngděng de yuánzé, chǎngkāi dàmén, zhāoshōu píngmín zǐdì rùxué, zhè zài dāngshí quèshí shì lìng rén zhènhàn de kāimíng zhī jǔ. Qí'èr, shūyuàn zhòngshì zìxiū hé yánjiū, zài dúshū de guòchéng zhōng chàngyì zìxíng sīkǎo, dùjué wàilái yīnsù de gānshè, yě bú huì guò duō guòwèn, yǐbiàn kāifā xuésheng de zìzhǔ xuéxí nénglì, jīfā xuésheng de zhǔdòngxìng hé chuàngzàoxìng. Qísān, jiànyú yí ge rén de zhīshi shì yǒuxiàn de, dàjiā de zhīshi shì wúxiàn de, gèrén jiějué bu liǎo de wèntí, zài zhòngrén de zhìhuì miànqián jiù bú shì wèntí, shūyuàn chàngdǎo hùxiāng qiēcuō, hùxiāng xuéxí. Qísì, gǔlì shīshēng zhījiān xiānghù zhìyí, xíngchéng tàntǎo zhēngbiàn, qiú zhēn qiú shí de xuéxí fēngqì. Lìngwài, zhòngshì guāndiǎn de duōyuánhuà, kāizhǎn bùtóng guāndiǎn de lùnbiàn, jiāoliú, yě shì shūyuàn tíchàng de. Guāndiǎn duìlì, yǒu fēnqí bú yàojǐn, kāifàng, bǎoshǒu yě wúguān jǐnyào, shūyuàn zhǔzhāng bùtóng xuépài, bùtóng zhǔzhāng zhījiān de zhēngbiàn yǔ jiàoliàng, wèicǐ shūyuàn shèlìle jiǎngyǎn biànlùn zhìdù, lèisì jīntiān de "lùntán". Zhè zhǒng xuéshù huódòng hěn shòu huānyíng, xuézǐmen xuéxí rèqíng gāozhǎng, xiānghù jīlì, qǔcháng bǔduǎn, gòngtóng jìnbù.
column3: In their way of running a school, the academies strove to practice a free and lively educational philosophy. First, following the principle of equality between rich and poor, they threw open their doors and admitted the children of commoners, which at the time was truly a startlingly enlightened move. Second, they valued self-study and research, encouraging students to think for themselves while reading, keeping out outside interference and not asking too many questions, so as to develop students' ability to learn independently and stimulate their initiative and creativity. Third, given that one person's knowledge is limited while everyone's knowledge together is unlimited, and that a problem an individual cannot solve stops being a problem in the face of collective wisdom, the academies promoted learning from one another through mutual exchange. Fourth, they encouraged teachers and students to question each other, creating a learning atmosphere of discussion and debate in pursuit of truth and facts. In addition, valuing a diversity of views and holding debates and exchanges between different viewpoints was also something the academies advocated. It did not matter if views were opposed or there were disagreements, nor whether one was open-minded or conservative; the academies favored debate and contest between different schools and positions, and for this purpose they set up a system of lectures and debates, similar to today's "forums". Such academic activities were very popular: students were full of enthusiasm for learning, encouraged one another, learned from each other's strengths to make up for their weaknesses, and progressed together.

column1: 书院讲究长幼，注重礼节，但不拘泥；主张刻苦自励，自主学习，却又鼓励相互质疑、辩论。书院内师生关系融洽，感情深厚，学生衷心爱戴名师，因为他们学识广博，品德过人，给学生做出了最好的示范，是学生崇敬的偶像。
column2: Shūyuàn jiǎngjiu zhǎngyòu, zhùzhòng lǐjié, dàn bù jūnì; zhǔzhāng kèkǔ zìlì, zìzhǔ xuéxí, què yòu gǔlì xiānghù zhìyí, biànlùn. Shūyuàn nèi shīshēng guānxi róngqià, gǎnqíng shēnhòu, xuésheng zhōngxīn àidài míngshī, yīnwèi tāmen xuéshí guǎngbó, pǐndé guòrén, gěi xuésheng zuòchūle zuì hǎo de shìfàn, shì xuésheng chóngjìng de ǒuxiàng.
column3: The academies paid attention to the order of elders and juniors and emphasized etiquette, but were not rigid about it; they advocated hard work, self-motivation and independent study, yet also encouraged questioning and debating one another. Relations between teachers and students in the academies were harmonious and their bonds deep; students sincerely loved and esteemed the famous teachers, because these teachers were widely learned and of outstanding character, set the best example for students, and were idols the students revered.

column1: 书院对中国封建社会教育、学术的发展，产生过重要影响。
column2: Shūyuàn duì Zhōngguó fēngjiàn shèhuì jiàoyù, xuéshù de fāzhǎn, chǎnshēngguo zhòngyào yǐngxiǎng.
column3: The academies had an important influence on the development of education and scholarship in China's feudal society.

column1: （一）优秀女警官
column2: (Yī) Yōuxiù nǚ jǐngguān
column3: (1) An Outstanding Policewoman

column1: 女警官李真是公认的“指纹破译专家”。
column2: Nǚ jǐngguān Lǐ Zhēn shì gōngrèn de "zhǐwén pòyì zhuānjiā".
column3: Policewoman Li Zhen is widely recognized as a "fingerprint decoding expert".

column1: 一次，某酒店一位正在化妆的女士被残忍地杀害在室内，现场没有烟头，没有纸屑，也没有抢劫等犯罪痕迹，侦破工作一时陷入停滞，一位曾在楼道内徘徊的男子有嫌疑，却苦于找不到证据。经过反复多次的现场勘查，窗台上一枚残缺的指纹成了唯一的线索，李真经过几个昼夜反复细致的比对，最终得出结论，抓住了歹徒。
column2: Yí cì, mǒu jiǔdiàn yí wèi zhèngzài huàzhuāng de nǚshì bèi cánrěn de shāhài zài shìnèi, xiànchǎng méiyǒu yāntóu, méiyǒu zhǐxiè, yě méiyǒu qiǎngjié děng fànzuì hénjì, zhēnpò gōngzuò yìshí xiànrù tíngzhì, yí wèi céng zài lóudào nèi páihuái de nánzǐ yǒu xiányí, què kǔyú zhǎo bu dào zhèngjù. Jīngguò fǎnfù duō cì de xiànchǎng kānchá, chuāngtái shang yì méi cánquē de zhǐwén chéngle wéiyī de xiànsuǒ, Lǐ Zhēn jīngguò jǐ ge zhòuyè fǎnfù xìzhì de bǐduì, zuìzhōng déchū jiélùn, zhuāzhùle dǎitú.
column3: Once, a woman putting on makeup in a hotel was brutally murdered in her room. At the scene there were no cigarette butts, no scraps of paper, and no signs of robbery or other crimes, so the investigation came to a temporary standstill. A man who had lingered in the corridor was a suspect, but unfortunately no evidence could be found. After repeated examinations of the scene, a partial fingerprint on the windowsill became the only clue. After several days and nights of repeated, meticulous comparison, Li Zhen finally reached a conclusion, and the criminal was caught.

column1: 另一次，某地发生多起入室抢劫案，附近居民恐慌感大增。其中两起案件提取到了犯罪嫌疑人的指纹，一枚是在玻璃上，而且指纹严重变形；另一枚是在铜制的框架上，指纹只残留有指尖部位。李真天天盯着指纹看，开始怎么也理不出头绪，两枚指纹都是残缺变形的，可以把两枚指纹结合起来分析吗？经过努力，李真发现因刑事犯罪被关押，一年前刑满放出监狱的王某的指纹与现场指纹具有共同特点，王某作案嫌疑很大。为了慎重起见，她又将其他现场遗留的指尖部位指纹与王某的指纹反复比较，最终认定该系列抢劫案为王某所为。
column2: Lìng yí cì, mǒu dì fāshēng duō qǐ rùshì qiǎngjié àn, fùjìn jūmín kǒnghuāng gǎn dà zēng. Qízhōng liǎng qǐ ànjiàn tíqǔ dàole fànzuì xiányírén de zhǐwén, yì méi shì zài bōli shang, érqiě zhǐwén yánzhòng biànxíng; lìng yì méi shì zài tóngzhì de kuàngjià shang, zhǐwén zhǐ cánliú yǒu zhǐjiān bùwèi. Lǐ Zhēn tiāntiān dīngzhe zhǐwén kàn, kāishǐ zěnme yě lǐ bu chū tóuxù, liǎng méi zhǐwén dōu shì cánquē biànxíng de, kěyǐ bǎ liǎng méi zhǐwén jiéhé qilai fēnxī ma? Jīngguò nǔlì, Lǐ Zhēn fāxiàn yīn xíngshì fànzuì bèi guānyā, yì nián qián xíng mǎn fàngchū jiānyù de Wáng mǒu de zhǐwén yǔ xiànchǎng zhǐwén jùyǒu gòngtóng tèdiǎn, Wáng mǒu zuò'àn xiányí hěn dà. Wèile shènzhòng qǐjiàn, tā yòu jiāng qítā xiànchǎng yíliú de zhǐjiān bùwèi zhǐwén yǔ Wáng mǒu de zhǐwén fǎnfù bǐjiào, zuìzhōng rèndìng gāi xìliè qiǎngjié àn wéi Wáng mǒu suǒ wéi.
column3: Another time, a series of home-invasion robberies occurred in a certain area, and panic among nearby residents rose sharply. In two of the cases the suspect's fingerprints were lifted: one was on glass and badly distorted; the other was on a copper frame, and only the fingertip area remained. Li Zhen stared at the fingerprints day after day, and at first she just couldn't make heads or tails of them—both prints were partial and distorted. Could the two be analyzed together? Through hard work, Li Zhen found that the fingerprints of a man surnamed Wang—who had been imprisoned for a criminal offense and released a year earlier after serving his sentence—shared features with the prints from the scenes, making Wang a strong suspect. To be prudent, she also repeatedly compared fingertip prints left at the other scenes with Wang's, and finally determined that the series of robberies had been committed by Wang.

column1: 李真说，指纹认定工作繁重、枯燥，不能有半点麻痹和失误，是一项考验耐心的工作。十余年间，李真全身心投入到痕迹检验和指纹管理工作中，查获了不少犯罪分子，使罪犯得到了应得的制裁。
column2: Lǐ Zhēn shuō, zhǐwén rèndìng gōngzuò fánzhòng, kūzào, bù néng yǒu bàndiǎn mábì hé shīwù, shì yí xiàng kǎoyàn nàixīn de gōngzuò. Shí yú nián jiān, Lǐ Zhēn quánshēnxīn tóurù dào hénjì jiǎnyàn hé zhǐwén guǎnlǐ gōngzuò zhōng, cháhuòle bù shǎo fànzuì fènzǐ, shǐ zuìfàn dédàole yīng dé de zhìcái.
column3: Li Zhen says fingerprint identification is heavy, tedious work that allows not the slightest carelessness or error—a job that tests one's patience. For more than ten years, Li Zhen has thrown herself heart and soul into trace examination and fingerprint management, tracking down many criminals and bringing them the punishment they deserved.

column1: （二）缉毒警察的故事
column2: (Èr) Jīdú jǐngchá de gùshi
column3: (2) The Story of an Anti-Drug Police Officer

column1: 公安局接到情报，有人要在某地进行毒品交易，志强立刻带领手下实地走访调查，很快了解到：几天前，的确有一伙人运来大批毒品。因各处防守严密，毒贩把东西藏在了桃花乡附近的大山里，准备参与交易的人也住在附近。志强感到毒贩十分狡猾，为了做到万无一失，他确定了“化装行动、引蛇出洞、主动出击”的破案思路。
column2: Gōng'ānjú jiēdào qíngbào, yǒu rén yào zài mǒu dì jìnxíng dúpǐn jiāoyì, Zhìqiáng lìkè dàilǐng shǒuxià shídì zǒufǎng diàochá, hěn kuài liǎojiě dào: jǐ tiān qián, díquè yǒu yì huǒ rén yùnlái dàpī dúpǐn. Yīn gè chù fángshǒu yánmì, dúfàn bǎ dōngxi cáng zài le Táohuā Xiāng fùjìn de dàshān li, zhǔnbèi cānyù jiāoyì de rén yě zhù zài fùjìn. Zhìqiáng gǎndào dúfàn shífēn jiǎohuá, wèile zuòdào wànwú yìshī, tā quèdìngle "huàzhuāng xíngdòng, yǐnshé chūdòng, zhǔdòng chūjī" de pò'àn sīlù.
column3: The Public Security Bureau received intelligence that someone was going to carry out a drug deal in a certain place. Zhiqiang immediately led his men to investigate on the ground and soon learned that a few days earlier a gang had indeed brought in a large batch of drugs. Because everywhere was tightly guarded, the traffickers had hidden the goods in the mountains near Taohua Township, and the people preparing to take part in the deal were also staying nearby. Zhiqiang felt the traffickers were extremely cunning, and to make sure nothing could go wrong, he settled on a plan for cracking the case: "act in disguise, lure the snake out of its hole, and strike first."

column1: 志强假扮成购买毒品的毒贩，与对方接上了头。对方提出在山里进行交易，志强认为山里地形复杂，提出在山下交易。信息传过去，对方却保持了沉默。时间一天天过去，志强心中十分焦急，但他清楚，必须沉着冷静，他决定暂且拖一拖这帮毒贩。他放出风说，自己在外地还有事，没货就算了。听到这话，对方急了，提出要不就在镇子附近交易。
column2: Zhìqiáng jiǎbàn chéng gòumǎi dúpǐn de dúfàn, yǔ duìfāng jiēshangle tóu. Duìfāng tíchū zài shān li jìnxíng jiāoyì, Zhìqiáng rènwéi shān li dìxíng fùzá, tíchū zài shān xià jiāoyì. Xìnxī chuán guoqu, duìfāng què bǎochíle chénmò. Shíjiān yìtiāntiān guòqu, Zhìqiáng xīnzhōng shífēn jiāojí, dàn tā qīngchu, bìxū chénzhuó lěngjìng, tā juédìng zànqiě tuō yi tuō zhè bāng dúfàn. Tā fàngchū fēng shuō, zìjǐ zài wàidì hái yǒu shì, méi huò jiù suàn le. Tīngdào zhè huà, duìfāng jí le, tíchū yàobù jiù zài zhènzi fùjìn jiāoyì.
column3: Zhiqiang posed as a trafficker wanting to buy drugs and made contact with the other side. They proposed doing the deal in the mountains, but Zhiqiang, thinking the mountain terrain was too complex, proposed doing it at the foot of the mountain. The message was passed on, but the other side stayed silent. As the days went by, Zhiqiang grew very anxious, but he knew he had to stay calm and composed, so he decided to stall the gang for a while. He let it be known that he had other business elsewhere, and if there were no goods, then forget it. Hearing this, the other side got anxious and suggested doing the deal near the town instead.

column1: 大清早，志强和全队民警出发了。到了交货地点，志强开始部署兵力。他让一个同事在车里隐藏好，一个随他下车，其他同事埋伏在附近。
column2: Dà qīngzǎo, Zhìqiáng hé quán duì mínjǐng chūfā le. Dàole jiāo huò dìdiǎn, Zhìqiáng kāishǐ bùshǔ bīnglì. Tā ràng yí ge tóngshì zài chē li yǐncáng hǎo, yí ge suí tā xià chē, qítā tóngshì máifú zài fùjìn.
column3: Early in the morning, Zhiqiang and the whole team of officers set out. When they reached the delivery point, Zhiqiang began deploying his forces. He had one colleague hide in the car, one get out of the car with him, and the other colleagues lie in ambush nearby.

column1: 刚刚布置妥当，一辆农用车和一辆摩托车朝自己缓缓驶来。面对毒贩，志强提出先验货后交钱，并告诉毒贩钱就放在车里。毒贩拿出毒品，奔向车门去取钱，车内民警扑上去，毒贩来不及反应就被制服。
column2: Gānggāng bùzhì tuǒdang, yí liàng nóngyòngchē hé yí liàng mótuōchē cháo zìjǐ huǎnhuǎn shǐ lai. Miànduì dúfàn, Zhìqiáng tíchū xiān yàn huò hòu jiāo qián, bìng gàosu dúfàn qián jiù fàng zài chē li. Dúfàn náchū dúpǐn, bēnxiàng chēmén qù qǔ qián, chē nèi mínjǐng pū shangqu, dúfàn lái bu jí fǎnyìng jiù bèi zhìfú.
column3: No sooner had everything been arranged than a farm vehicle and a motorcycle came slowly toward them. Facing the traffickers, Zhiqiang proposed inspecting the goods first and paying afterwards, and told them the money was right there in the car. The traffickers took out the drugs and rushed to the car door to get the money; the officer inside pounced, and the traffickers were subdued before they had time to react.

column1: 这次，缉毒大队成功破获了当地有史以来最大的一起非法运输贩卖毒品案。
column2: Zhè cì, jīdú dàduì chénggōng pòhuòle dāngdì yǒu shǐ yǐlái zuì dà de yì qǐ fēifǎ yùnshū fànmài dúpǐn àn.
column3: This time, the anti-drug brigade successfully cracked the largest case of illegal drug transport and trafficking in the area's history.

column1: （三）特殊的“缉毒警察”
column2: (Sān) Tèshū de "jīdú jǐngchá"
column3: (3) A Special "Anti-Drug Officer"

column1: 小罗是个兵，辉杰是只犬，这原本是一个平面上两条平行而非并列的线，却在缉毒战场上交叉，创造出感人的故事。
column2: Xiǎo Luó shì ge bīng, Huījié shì zhī quǎn, zhè yuánběn shì yí ge píngmiàn shang liǎng tiáo píngxíng ér fēi bìngliè de xiàn, què zài jīdú zhànchǎng shang jiāochā, chuàngzào chū gǎnrén de gùshi.
column3: Xiao Luo is a soldier and Huijie is a dog: originally two parallel—but not equal—lines on the same plane, they crossed on the battlefield against drugs and created a moving story.

column1: 接手缉毒犬辉杰，小罗心里包袱很重。小罗怕狗，小时候被狗狂追的经历让他提起狗就胆怯。和辉杰初次见面，小罗努力和它搞好关系，可任你怎么哄，辉杰就是不理，弄得小罗很着急。没几天，辉杰生病了，小罗悉心照顾它。辉杰很快就好了，自此它对小罗非常的信赖和忠诚，每次见到小罗就会亲热地伸出舌头舔一舔。训练中，辉杰表现突出，无论毒品藏得多隐秘，辉杰一出手，不出一分钟，肯定能查出来。
column2: Jiēshǒu jīdú quǎn Huījié, Xiǎo Luó xīnli bāofu hěn zhòng. Xiǎo Luó pà gǒu, xiǎoshíhou bèi gǒu kuáng zhuī de jīnglì ràng tā tíqǐ gǒu jiù dǎnqiè. Hé Huījié chūcì jiànmiàn, Xiǎo Luó nǔlì hé tā gǎohǎo guānxi, kě rèn nǐ zěnme hǒng, Huījié jiùshì bù lǐ, nòng de Xiǎo Luó hěn zháojí. Méi jǐ tiān, Huījié shēngbìng le, Xiǎo Luó xīxīn zhàogù tā. Huījié hěn kuài jiù hǎo le, zìcǐ tā duì Xiǎo Luó fēicháng de xìnlài hé zhōngchéng, měi cì jiàndào Xiǎo Luó jiù huì qīnrè de shēnchū shétou tiǎn yi tiǎn. Xùnliàn zhōng, Huījié biǎoxiàn tūchū, wúlùn dúpǐn cáng de duō yǐnmì, Huījié yì chūshǒu, bù chū yì fēnzhōng, kěndìng néng chá chulai.
column3: Taking over the drug-sniffing dog Huijie weighed heavily on Xiao Luo's mind. Xiao Luo was afraid of dogs—having been chased wildly by a dog as a child, he grew timid at the mere mention of them. When he first met Huijie, Xiao Luo tried hard to get on good terms with it, but no matter how he coaxed it, Huijie simply ignored him, which made Xiao Luo very anxious. A few days later Huijie fell ill, and Xiao Luo cared for it attentively. Huijie soon recovered, and from then on it was extremely trusting of and loyal to Xiao Luo, affectionately sticking out its tongue to lick him every time it saw him. In training Huijie performed outstandingly: no matter how well drugs were hidden, once Huijie got to work it would find them in under a minute.

column1: 小罗和辉杰可以正式执行任务了。这天辉杰按小罗的指令对一辆车实施搜嗅，很快就从车厢尾部空隙内查出了毒品。此后，辉杰累立战功。
column2: Xiǎo Luó hé Huījié kěyǐ zhèngshì zhíxíng rènwu le. Zhè tiān Huījié àn Xiǎo Luó de zhǐlìng duì yí liàng chē shíshī sōu xiù, hěn kuài jiù cóng chēxiāng wěibù kòngxì nèi cháchūle dúpǐn. Cǐhòu, Huījié lěi lì zhàngōng.
column3: Xiao Luo and Huijie were ready to carry out missions officially. One day, on Xiao Luo's command, Huijie sniffed a vehicle and quickly found drugs in a gap at the rear of the cargo compartment. After that, Huijie performed meritorious service again and again.

column1: 那是9月的一天，辉杰在一辆车上发现了毒品，它扒开车厢底板上铺着的塑料垫，直接从下面叼出一个装有粉末状毒品的塑料袋，薄薄的塑料袋一咬即破，毒品直接渗入了辉杰的口腔。辉杰中毒了，它呼吸急促，无法站立，得赶快上医院。路上，辉杰眼看就不行了，小罗来不及多想便给辉杰做起了人工呼吸。14公里路程，小罗一次次把辉杰从死亡线上拉回来。经过抢救，辉杰脱离了生命危险，半个月后它又出现在缉毒岗位上。
column2: Nà shì jiǔ yuè de yì tiān, Huījié zài yí liàng chē shang fāxiànle dúpǐn, tā bākāi chēxiāng dǐbǎn shang pūzhe de sùliào diàn, zhíjiē cóng xiàmiàn diāochū yí ge zhuāng yǒu fěnmòzhuàng dúpǐn de sùliàodài, báobáo de sùliàodài yì yǎo jí pò, dúpǐn zhíjiē shènrùle Huījié de kǒuqiāng. Huījié zhòngdú le, tā hūxī jícù, wúfǎ zhànlì, děi gǎnkuài shàng yīyuàn. Lùshang, Huījié yǎnkàn jiù bù xíng le, Xiǎo Luó lái bu jí duō xiǎng biàn gěi Huījié zuò qile réngōng hūxī. Shísì gōnglǐ lùchéng, Xiǎo Luó yí cìcì bǎ Huījié cóng sǐwáng xiàn shang lā huilai. Jīngguò qiǎngjiù, Huījié tuōlíle shēngmìng wēixiǎn, bàn ge yuè hòu tā yòu chūxiàn zài jīdú gǎngwèi shang.
column3: One day in September, Huijie found drugs in a vehicle. It pulled aside the plastic mat laid on the floor of the compartment and pulled out from underneath, in its teeth, a plastic bag containing powdered drugs. The thin bag burst at the first bite, and the drugs seeped straight into Huijie's mouth. Huijie was poisoned: it was gasping for breath and couldn't stand, and had to be rushed to the hospital. On the way, Huijie seemed about to die, and without a second thought Xiao Luo began giving it artificial respiration. Over the 14-kilometer journey, Xiao Luo pulled Huijie back from the brink of death again and again. After emergency treatment, Huijie was out of danger, and half a month later it was back at its anti-drug post.

column1: 中毒事件让辉杰的身体每况愈下，几年后，辉杰离世。参加过无数次大大小小“战役”的辉杰走完了它光辉的一生，也给小罗的心中留下了无尽的思念。
column2: Zhòngdú shìjiàn ràng Huījié de shēntǐ měikuàng yùxià, jǐ nián hòu, Huījié líshì. Cānjiāguo wúshù cì dàdàxiǎoxiǎo "zhànyì" de Huījié zǒuwánle tā guānghuī de yìshēng, yě gěi Xiǎo Luó de xīnzhōng liúxiàle wújìn de sīniàn.
column3: After the poisoning, Huijie's health went steadily downhill, and a few years later Huijie passed away. Having fought countless "battles" big and small, Huijie came to the end of its glorious life, leaving Xiao Luo with endless longing in his heart.

column1: 屡次创业，却屡次惨遭失败的人，总想知道，创业有窍门吗？当然有，窍门就是创业不可盲目，要依据市场规则捕捉商业机会。1903年吉列先生发明的可替换剃须刀、1958年安藤百福发明的方便面、1992年戚石川兄弟发明的罐装八宝粥，都受到了市场热捧，并给创业者带来了数额可观的财富。成功的案例告诉我们：创业必须依据市场需求，这是一条永恒的真理，只要遵循这条规则，就没有不成功的道理。
column2: Lǚcì chuàngyè, què lǚcì cǎn zāo shībài de rén, zǒng xiǎng zhīdào, chuàngyè yǒu qiàomén ma? Dāngrán yǒu, qiàomén jiù shì chuàngyè bù kě mángmù, yào yījù shìchǎng guīzé bǔzhuō shāngyè jīhuì. Yī jiǔ líng sān nián Jíliè xiānsheng fāmíng de kě tìhuàn tìxūdāo, yī jiǔ wǔ bā nián Ānténg Bǎifú fāmíng de fāngbiànmiàn, yī jiǔ jiǔ èr nián Qī Shíchuān xiōngdì fāmíng de guànzhuāng bābǎozhōu, dōu shòudàole shìchǎng rèpěng, bìng gěi chuàngyèzhě dàiláile shù'é kěguān de cáifù. Chénggōng de ànlì gàosu wǒmen: chuàngyè bìxū yījù shìchǎng xūqiú, zhè shì yì tiáo yǒnghéng de zhēnlǐ, zhǐyào zūnxún zhè tiáo guīzé, jiù méiyǒu bù chénggōng de dàoli.
column3: People who have started businesses again and again, only to fail miserably each time, always want to know: is there a trick to starting a business? Of course there is. The trick is not to start a business blindly, but to seize business opportunities according to the rules of the market. The replaceable razor invented by Mr. Gillette in 1903, the instant noodles invented by Momofuku Ando in 1958, and the canned eight-treasure porridge invented by the Qi Shichuan brothers in 1992 were all hugely popular on the market and brought their creators considerable fortunes. These success stories tell us that a business must be built on market demand. This is an eternal truth: as long as you follow this rule, there is no reason not to succeed.

column1: 独具慧眼，寻找机遇
column2: Dújù huìyǎn, xúnzhǎo jīyù
column3: Have a discerning eye and look for opportunities

column1: 市场需求无处不在，却往往易被忽视，别人没发现，或是不愿做的生意，往往孕育着机会。譬如，在新产品博览会上，王先生看到了一台叫作“电池分析修复仪”的小机器，它是用来修复手机电池的。手机电池的正常寿命是5至6年，事实上大家的电池却没有那么耐用，往往用一年就坏了，换新电池又很贵。而所谓坏了，只是化学物质沉淀到了绝缘层，美国人发现在一定条件下，能够将其还原成初始状态，于是发明了这种机器。王先生花4万元买下了这台能够像变魔术一样修好电池的机器。之后，在商场租了柜台，修一块电池收费50～70元，扣掉场地租金和税金，月收入上万，不到两个季度就轻松收回了本钱。类似这样的生意，即使碰上通货膨胀，也不会对他产生丝毫影响。可是，如果你没有眼光，就看不到商机；如果你思维平庸，就发现不了商机；只要你勤劳，市场就握在你的手里。
column2: Shìchǎng xūqiú wúchù búzài, què wǎngwǎng yì bèi hūshì, biérén méi fāxiàn, huò shì bú yuàn zuò de shēngyi, wǎngwǎng yùnyùzhe jīhuì. Pìrú, zài xīn chǎnpǐn bólǎnhuì shang, Wáng xiānsheng kàndàole yì tái jiàozuò "diànchí fēnxī xiūfùyí" de xiǎo jīqì, tā shì yòng lái xiūfù shǒujī diànchí de. Shǒujī diànchí de zhèngcháng shòumìng shì wǔ zhì liù nián, shìshí shang dàjiā de diànchí què méiyǒu nàme nàiyòng, wǎngwǎng yòng yì nián jiù huài le, huàn xīn diànchí yòu hěn guì. Ér suǒwèi huài le, zhǐ shì huàxué wùzhì chéndiàn dàole juéyuáncéng, Měiguórén fāxiàn zài yídìng tiáojiàn xià, nénggòu jiāng qí huányuán chéng chūshǐ zhuàngtài, yúshì fāmíngle zhè zhǒng jīqì. Wáng xiānsheng huā sìwàn yuán mǎixiàle zhè tái nénggòu xiàng biàn móshù yíyàng xiūhǎo diànchí de jīqì. Zhīhòu, zài shāngchǎng zūle guìtái, xiū yí kuài diànchí shōufèi wǔshí zhì qīshí yuán, kòudiào chǎngdì zūjīn hé shuìjīn, yuè shōurù shàng wàn, bú dào liǎng ge jìdù jiù qīngsōng shōuhuíle běnqián. Lèisì zhèyàng de shēngyi, jíshǐ pèngshang tōnghuò péngzhàng, yě bú huì duì tā chǎnshēng sīháo yǐngxiǎng. Kěshì, rúguǒ nǐ méiyǒu yǎnguāng, jiù kàn bu dào shāngjī; rúguǒ nǐ sīwéi píngyōng, jiù fāxiàn bu liǎo shāngjī; zhǐyào nǐ qínláo, shìchǎng jiù wò zài nǐ de shǒu li.
column3: Market demand is everywhere, yet it is often easily overlooked. Business that others haven't noticed or aren't willing to do often holds opportunity. For instance, at a new-products expo, Mr. Wang saw a small machine called a "battery analyzer and restorer", used to repair mobile phone batteries. The normal life of a phone battery is five to six years, but in fact people's batteries aren't that durable—they often die after a year, and new batteries are expensive. Yet so-called dead batteries are simply ones where chemicals have settled onto the insulating layer. Americans discovered that under certain conditions this can be restored to the original state, and so they invented this machine. Mr. Wang spent 40,000 yuan to buy this machine that could fix batteries like magic. He then rented a counter in a shopping mall and charged 50 to 70 yuan per battery repair. After deducting rent and taxes, his monthly income topped ten thousand, and in less than two quarters he had easily recouped his investment. A business like this wouldn't be affected in the slightest even by inflation. However, if you lack vision, you won't see business opportunities; if your thinking is mediocre, you won't discover them; but as long as you are hardworking, the market will be in your hands.

column1: 研究竞争对手，从中找出其产品的缺点及营销的薄弱环节，是捕捉商机的有效方法之一。
column2: Yánjiū jìngzhēng duìshǒu, cóngzhōng zhǎochū qí chǎnpǐn de quēdiǎn jí yíngxiāo de bóruò huánjié, shì bǔzhuō shāngjī de yǒuxiào fāngfǎ zhī yī.
column3: Studying your competitors and finding the shortcomings of their products and the weak links in their marketing is one of the effective ways to seize business opportunities.

column2: Dāngnián, rìjiàn xīngwàng de Rìběn pàopàotáng shìchǎng dà bùfen bèi Láotè lǒngduàn, Jiāngqí gōngsī xiǎng kuòchōng zhè fāngmiàn de yèwù, yúshì zhuānmén chénglìle tuánduì, yánjiū Láotè de chǎnpǐn, yǐ xúnzhǎo shìchǎng fèngxì. column3: Back then, most of Japan's increasingly booming bubble-gum market was monopolized by Lotte. The Ezaki company wanted to expand its business in this area, so it set up a dedicated team to study Lotte's products in search of a gap in the market. The research found four shortcomings in Lotte's products: first, the adult bubble-gum market was growing, but Lotte was still focused on children; second, Lotte's products came in a single flavor, while consumer demand was becoming more and more diverse; third, Lotte's gum looked old-fashioned and lacked new styles; fourth, Lotte's products sold for 110 yen, so buyers had to dig out 10-yen coins, which was inconvenient. So Ezaki boldly laid out its plans, designing products based on adults' consumer needs and drawing up a corresponding marketing strategy. Before long, it launched four functional bubble gums:

column1: 在产品可口的同时，精心设计包装和造型，定价分50和100日元两种。江崎的产品物美价廉，风味独特。不靠广告吹捧，品尝后，消费者购买踊跃，市场需求呈井喷式爆发，财务收入也呈井喷式增长。这就是市场，只要你细心研究市场，细心研究消费者的需求，细心研究市场产品的优劣，对产品的不足做些局部改进，就有可能得到消费者的认可；你愈是为消费者考虑得周全，消费者愈是会慷慨地关照你。
column2: Zài chǎnpǐn kěkǒu de tóngshí, jīngxīn shèjì bāozhuāng hé zàoxíng, dìngjià fēn wǔshí hé yìbǎi rìyuán liǎng zhǒng. Jiāngqí de chǎnpǐn wùměi jiàlián, fēngwèi dútè. Bú kào guǎnggào chuīpěng, pǐncháng hòu, xiāofèizhě gòumǎi yǒngyuè, shìchǎng xūqiú chéng jǐngpēnshì bàofā, cáiwù shōurù yě chéng jǐngpēnshì zēngzhǎng. Zhè jiù shì shìchǎng, zhǐyào nǐ xìxīn yánjiū shìchǎng, xìxīn yánjiū xiāofèizhě de xūqiú, xìxīn yánjiū shìchǎng chǎnpǐn de yōuliè, duì chǎnpǐn de bùzú zuò xiē júbù gǎijìn, jiù yǒu kěnéng dédào xiāofèizhě de rènkě; nǐ yù shì wèi xiāofèizhě kǎolǜ de zhōuquán, xiāofèizhě yù shì huì kāngkǎi de guānzhào nǐ.
column3: Besides making the products tasty, Ezaki carefully designed the packaging and shapes, and set two prices: 50 yen and 100 yen. Ezaki's products were high in quality, low in price and uniquely flavored. Without relying on advertising hype, consumers rushed to buy them once they had tasted them; market demand exploded like a gusher, and revenue shot up the same way. That's the market: as long as you carefully study the market, consumers' needs, and the strengths and weaknesses of products on the market, and make some partial improvements to a product's shortcomings, you may win consumers' approval. The more thoughtfully you consider consumers, the more generously they will look after you.

column3: Looking for business opportunities in latent market demand

column1: 在台湾某游览观光区，一台流动彩印车吸引了大家的目光，游客可以在这儿就近冲印照片，可以把喜欢的图案、肖像印在纪念品和纺织品上，作为独一无二的旅游留念。
column2: Zài Táiwān mǒu yóulǎn guānguāng qū, yì tái liúdòng cǎiyìn chē xīyǐnle dàjiā de mùguāng, yóukè kěyǐ zài zhèr jiùjìn chōngyìn zhàopiàn, kěyǐ bǎ xǐhuan de tú'àn, xiàoxiàng yìn zài jìniànpǐn hé fǎngzhīpǐn shang, zuòwéi dúyī wú'èr de lǚyóu liúniàn.
column3: At a sightseeing area in Taiwan, a mobile color-printing van caught everyone's eye. Here tourists could have photos developed on the spot, and could print their favorite designs and portraits on souvenirs and textiles as one-of-a-kind travel keepsakes.

column1: 流动彩印车的发明者是周家两兄弟，哥哥是汽车维修工，弟弟是摄影发烧友。台湾经济转型，旅游业成了台湾经济的支柱产业。兄弟俩发现，对照观光客的需求，传统彩色冲印做法太过陈旧，哪个游客能为冲洗照片等好几天？于是兄弟俩齐心协力，发挥各自的专长，以50万台币做资本，发明了这辆相当于一个小型专业冲印部的流动彩印车。
column2: Liúdòng cǎiyìn chē de fāmíngzhě shì Zhōu jiā liǎng xiōngdì, gēge shì qìchē wéixiūgōng, dìdi shì shèyǐng fāshāoyǒu. Táiwān jīngjì zhuǎnxíng, lǚyóuyè chéngle Táiwān jīngjì de zhīzhù chǎnyè. Xiōngdì liǎ fāxiàn, duìzhào guānguāngkè de xūqiú, chuántǒng cǎisè chōngyìn zuòfǎ tài guò chénjiù, nǎge yóukè néng wèi chōngxǐ zhàopiàn děng hǎo jǐ tiān? Yúshì xiōngdì liǎ qíxīn xiélì, fāhuī gèzì de zhuāncháng, yǐ wǔshí wàn táibì zuò zīběn, fāmíngle zhè liàng xiāngdāng yú yí ge xiǎoxíng zhuānyè chōngyìnbù de liúdòng cǎiyìn chē.
column3: The inventors of the mobile color-printing van were two brothers of the Zhou family: the elder was an auto mechanic and the younger a photography enthusiast. As Taiwan's economy transformed, tourism became one of its pillar industries. The brothers found that, measured against tourists' needs, the traditional way of developing color photos was too outdated—which tourist can wait several days to get photos developed? So the brothers joined forces, made the most of their respective skills, and with 500,000 Taiwan dollars as capital invented this mobile color-printing van, the equivalent of a small professional photo-processing shop.

column1: 流动彩印车一出现就大受欢迎，每逢周末、节假日以及人多的场合简直就忙不过来，它最大的优势就是方便快捷，不像以往，要等上好几天。旅游淡季，彩印车还可以为学生的制服、不同规格的运动服印制高品质的图案。彩印车很快就有了知名度，收益也呈递增趋势，很短的周期就收回了成本。
column2: Liúdòng cǎiyìn chē yì chūxiàn jiù dà shòu huānyíng, měi féng zhōumò, jiéjiàrì yǐjí rén duō de chǎnghé jiǎnzhí jiù máng bu guòlái, tā zuì dà de yōushì jiù shì fāngbiàn kuàijié, bú xiàng yǐwǎng, yào děng shang hǎo jǐ tiān. Lǚyóu dànjì, cǎiyìn chē hái kěyǐ wèi xuésheng de zhìfú, bùtóng guīgé de yùndòngfú yìnzhì gāo pǐnzhì de tú'àn. Cǎiyìn chē hěn kuài jiù yǒule zhīmíngdù, shōuyì yě chéng dìzēng qūshì, hěn duǎn de zhōuqī jiù shōuhuíle chéngběn.
column3: The mobile color-printing van was a big hit as soon as it appeared. On weekends, holidays and other crowded occasions it was simply swamped. Its biggest advantage was being convenient and fast—unlike before, you didn't have to wait several days. In the off-season, the van could also print high-quality designs on students' uniforms and sportswear of different sizes. The van soon became well known, its earnings kept rising, and it recouped its costs in a very short period.

column3: Clearly, starting a business is not gambling, nor can it rely on daydreams. Being able to accurately predict latent market demand and having forward-looking awareness are essential qualities for any entrepreneur.
